Accepted formats

FormatUseFiles
UMFNative declarative fighterassets/chars/<id>.json
M.U.G.E.NClassic fighters and stages.def, .sff v1/v2, .air, .cmd, .cns, .snd, .act

UMF and M.U.G.E.N fighters run on the same state machine and can fight each other.

Roadmap

Compatibility plans and architecture decisions are in docs/ROADMAP.md. Items marked planned in this wiki do not exist in the current version yet.

Compatibility status

The progress toward Ikemen GO v1.0.0 parity is tracked in issue #135, with one issue per missing controller, trigger or feature. The lists of supported controllers, triggers and redirections in CNS scripts are checked against the engine by cargo test -p ume-engine --test it wiki_sync::: a listed name the engine does not handle, an implemented name that is not listed, or a mismatch between the English and Portuguese pages fails the test. Every character load also reports the controllers, triggers and parameters it uses that the engine ignores (see "Load diagnostics" in the same page).

Acknowledgments

Thanks to the Ikemen GO team and to Elecbyte, creator of M.U.G.E.N, for the inspiration.

Installation

Download a ready build

Download the file for your platform from Releases, extract it and run ultimate-mugen (Windows: ultimate-mugen.exe or run.bat). The desktop build checks the newest GitHub release over HTTPS and asks before downloading and installing it; see Automatic updates. Hide the prompt with --no-auto-update / UME_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 or skip the check with --no-update-check / UME_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1.

Build from source

Requires stable Rust (rustup.rs).

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu):

sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libudev-dev libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev
TargetCommand
Desktopcargo run --release
Testscargo test --workspace --release
Web (PWA)rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown, then ./scripts/build-web.sh and python3 -m http.server -d web/dist 8080
Androidcargo install cargo-apk --version 0.9.6 --locked, then cargo apk build -p ultimate-mugen --lib --release --target aarch64-linux-android
iOScargo install cargo-bundle, then cargo bundle --release --target aarch64-apple-ios (macOS + Xcode)

Folder layout next to the executable

ultimate-mugen(.exe)
ultimate-mugen.cfg        settings saved by the menu
mugen/
  chars/<name>/<name>.def M.U.G.E.N characters
  stages/<name>.def       M.U.G.E.N stages
  <anything>.zip          zipped packs (characters or stages)

The mugen/ folder is searched in this order: UME_MUGEN_DIR, the current directory, next to the executable, and two levels above it.

Automatic updates

The desktop build updates itself from the latest GitHub Release. The release tag is the version source of truth: CI stamps UME_RELEASE_VERSION into the binary, publishes the assets, and the installed build replaces itself with the matching executable for its platform.

Release assets

Every release carries, per platform (windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, macos-aarch64):

AssetPurpose
ultimate-mugen-v<version>-<platform>.zip / .tar.gzManual install package (binary + README)
ultimate-mugen-v<version>-<platform>[.exe]Raw executable downloaded by the auto-updater
latest.jsonUpdate manifest read by the running build
SHA256SUMS.txtHuman-readable hashes for every asset

latest.json keeps the archive under platforms.<platform> and adds the raw binary:

{
  "version": "0.4.0",
  "notes": "Short release notes",
  "pub_date": "2026-11-05T12:00:00Z",
  "platforms": {
    "windows-x86_64": {
      "url": "https://github.com/juninmd/ultimate-mugen/releases/download/v0.4.0/ultimate-mugen-v0.4.0-windows-x86_64.zip",
      "sha256": "<archive sha256>",
      "size": 1234567,
      "binary": {
        "url": "https://github.com/juninmd/ultimate-mugen/releases/download/v0.4.0/ultimate-mugen-v0.4.0-windows-x86_64.exe",
        "sha256": "<binary sha256>",
        "size": 9876543
      }
    }
  }
}

Only the three published platforms can self-update. Other targets (web, Android, iOS, non-x86_64 Linux, Intel macOS) still read the notice-only path.

Flow

  1. At boot the game requests releases/latest/download/latest.json over HTTPS (8 s timeout, silently ignored when offline).
  2. A newer version with a binary entry for the current platform shows an update panel on the title/menu with the installed and the available versions. Nothing is downloaded until the player accepts "Update now".
  3. Accepting starts the background download (180 s timeout) to .update-v<version>[.exe] next to the running executable.
  4. The download is rejected unless its sha256 and byte size match the manifest and the staged executable answers --version with ultimate-mugen <version>.
  5. Once verified, the staged file replaces the installed executable (on Windows the running file is first renamed to .old) and the game restarts with --no-update-check, so a bad manifest cannot cause a restart loop.
  6. The previous .old file is removed at the next boot.

A failed download, an offline machine or a read-only install folder only changes the status line; the running build keeps working. "Not now" forgets the version until the next boot, and the footer notice stays visible.

Command line and opt-outs

FlagEffect
--check-updatePrints whether a newer release exists and exits
--updateDownloads, verifies and installs the newest release, then exits
--no-auto-update / UME_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1Keeps the footer notice, never shows the prompt (so never downloads or installs)
--no-update-check / UME_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1No network request at all

Local -dev builds never self-update.

Verifying a release

node scripts/release-manifest.mjs --verify latest.json --dir <assets> --version <version> --repo juninmd/ultimate-mugen checks that both the archive and the raw binary exist, that their URLs point at the tagged release and that their sha256 values match. The Release workflow runs exactly this check against the draft before publishing, and probes the live manifest afterwards.

Player card (player-card.json)

The Player card screen (main menu, Player card) stores the card, record, roster, rivals and achievements in player-card.json, next to the executable (browser: local storage). Training bouts do not count. The file stays on this device; there is no server sync.

Resizable window

The window can be dragged to any size. The game draws into a fixed 16:9 logical space that is scaled to the window, so the fight area, HUD and menus stay consistent at every size and the window size is independent from the game resolution. With Keep aspect on, the unused strip is black; with it off, the picture is stretched and mouse and touch input are mapped back to the stretched space. The --res WxH flag still sets the starting window size and takes priority over the saved window value.

Language and localization

The UI ships three locales: English (default), Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish. Settings › Language cycles through them at runtime and stores lang=en|pt|es in ultimate-mugen.cfg.

  • src/i18n/catalog.rs holds the keyed table (English and Portuguese) and src/i18n/es_catalog.rs the Spanish column; i18n::t(key) looks up current locale → English → the key name, so an incomplete catalog never shows a blank label.
  • Inline strings use i18n::tr3(pt, en, es); the older i18n::tr(pt, en) finds its Spanish text through src/i18n/es_phrases.rs, keyed by the English string. Placeholders use i18n::fill("{name}", &[("name", value)]).
  • A missing key is printed once to the log (i18n: missing key '<key>').
  • The catalogs are compiled in, so switching has no I/O cost and works on web/mobile.
  • Unit tests keep the catalogs in sync and fail if the migrated screens go back to hardcoded Portuguese.
  • Still Portuguese-only: story cutscenes and boss dialogue, fighter bios and stage names (content data).
  • First launch (no saved config) picks the system language: navigator.language on the web, LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG on desktop; English when unsupported.

Importing M.U.G.E.N content

Main menu › Import M.U.G.E.N is the single entry point. On the web the button opens the browser file picker (the page overlays an invisible <label> exactly on the button so the click is a real user gesture) and .zip files can also be dropped on the window. On desktop the button opens the system file dialog (PowerShell on Windows, osascript on macOS, zenity or kdialog on Linux); folders under chars/ and stages/ are still scanned at start.

The names x y z a b c are the same ones used in character commands (input).

While jumping, x y a b each throw an air normal, and down + b is the diving down kick (generated for every native fighter by native/air_normals.rs, reusing the fighter's own air animations).

Move shortcuts

Open the pause menu, pick a move in the move list and press 1-4 (or L1, L2, R1, R2 on a gamepad) to bind it to that slot. Pressing the same slot again clears it. From then on the bound move is performed by one key or button press, with the right motion and buttons played for you. Bindings are stored per fighter in ultimate-mugen.shortcuts next to the executable. On the web the gamepad mapping follows the same layout.

Button prompts

The pause move list and the Controls screen show the real key or button of the device you used last: keyboard keys, Xbox (A/B/X/Y, LB/LT/RB/RT) or PlayStation (✕ ○ □ △, L1/L2/R1/R2). On touch screens they show the virtual button names. Xbox pads are detected by name or by vendor ID 045E, PlayStation pads by 054C. Rumble works on both: Xbox through gilrs force feedback (and the Gamepad API on the web), DualShock 4 / DualSense through direct HID reports.

Tweaks (tweaks.toml)

Created next to the executable on first run (localStorage on web) with the defaults. Edit and save: the game reloads it within about one second and shows a toast. Mistakes never stop the game; the affected value keeps its default and the toast and log name the key, with a "did you mean" hint and the line for syntax errors.

Adding M.U.G.E.N content

Characters

  1. Put the folder in mugen/chars/<name>/ with the .def inside, or drop the .zip straight into mugen/.
  2. Open the game: the character shows up in the select screen. Tab filters between all, originals and M.U.G.E.N.

To download content from a GitHub repository instead, see the GitHub marketplace.

Use Main menu › Import M.U.G.E.N (the only import button; on the web it opens the browser picker, on desktop the system file dialog) or drag the .zip onto the web window. Imports are idempotent: the same archive, or the same fighter or stage found again under another path, name or letter case, is registered only once (identity is a hash of the normalized .def plus its sprite file). Packs saved in the browser from older versions are deduplicated automatically on the next load.

The screen shows a holographic mosaic of every imported fighter (F also lists the native roster). Arrows, gamepad or touch move the cursor, Enter or a click opens the character sheet: portrait, author, series, source .def, version, palette count, nationality and bio when known, stat gauges, and the full move list with input and energy cost (Left/Right switch fighter, Esc returns). Up from the first row focuses the import button. Capture with UME_SHOTS_ONLY=mugenroster (UME_ROSTER_ZIPS=a.zip:b.zip imports packs first).

A web import shows a full-screen loading overlay from the moment the files are selected until the last archive is registered. Archives are read, decompressed and registered one per frame, with at most two raw packs waiting in wasm memory; a batch of large packs no longer runs in one frozen frame. The same overlay appears on startup while the packs persisted in IndexedDB are restored, one at a time.

Hundreds of characters are registered without decoding everything; only the item under the cursor is loaded, and an LRU cache bounds memory.

Before a character reaches the roster, the catalogue checks that every file its .def names under [Files] exists inside the character's own folder (or the pack root, or data/): sprite, anim and cns are required. A character that fails the check is quarantined: it is kept out of the select screen, and the reason is listed. Files are never borrowed from another character's folder, so a copied .def that points to another fighter's sprites cannot load them by name. The check is structural (file presence), so it stays fast enough for the startup scan; a fighter whose files exist but whose animations reference missing sprites still loads and is shown with its missing frames.

Open Personagens MUGEN on the main menu to see the summary: how many characters loaded, how many are in quarantine and the most common reasons, plus a gallery of every loaded character (portrait, name and author; ←/→ change pages) and the quarantine list (TAB switches the view; ESC returns).

Stages

Put <name>.def and the .sff in mugen/stages/, or inside a .zip in mugen/.

Validate a character

cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example mugen_check -- mugen/chars/kfm
cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example sprite_audit -- mugen/chars/kfm
cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example hover_check -- mugen/chars/kfm

cargo run --release -p ume-formats --example mugen_refs -- mugen/chars cargo run --release -p ume-formats --example mugen_lint -- mugen/chars cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example mugen_pairs -- --matrix mugen/chars cargo run --release -p ume-formats --example mkselectdef -- mugen > mugen/select.def


| Tool | Shows |
|---|---|
| `mugen_check` | Loads and simulates a fight without a window; lists parse errors, invalid states and unsupported controllers, triggers and parameters (`--strict` fails on them); `--lint` adds source checks: duplicate parameters, invalid `trans`/`postype`/`space` values, `persistent` in negative states, `[State N]` not matching its `[Statedef]`, garbage lines, duplicate `[Command]` keys, duplicate and empty `.air` actions (`TRACE=1` lists each line) |
| `sprite_audit` | Missing or blank sprites referenced by the `.air` |
| `hover_check` | Fighter stuck off the floor (`TRACE=1` shows transitions) |

Characters whose license forbids redistribution must not be committed: `mugen/` is git-ignored.

GitHub marketplace

English · Português (BR)

Install characters, stages and music straight from any public GitHub repository. Open Mercado GitHub in the main menu.

Quick start

  1. Press U (or click + Adicionar) and paste a link: https://github.com/owner/repo, owner/repo, or a folder link such as https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/mugen.
  2. The game reads the repository tree and lists what it finds.
  3. Mark items (Space, click, or Todos) and press Instalar (I). Downloads run in parallel with a progress bar.
  4. Installed items are active right away. Use Ativar (E) and Desativar (O) on any selection, including bulk selections, or Remover (X) to delete them from the device.

Everything is stored locally, so the repository list, the installed items and their on/off state are still there next time.

Browsing: list, grid, formats and outdated items

  • List and grid. The Lista / Grade switch (V, or the gamepad aux button) toggles a dense list and a grid of cards with a portrait, and is remembered. In both, a tap or click marks an item and dragging scrolls (touch friendly); the mouse wheel, PageUp/PageDown and the arrow keys scroll too.
  • MUGEN and UMF badges. Every character, stage and pack shows its format. A pack is UMF when its path or name says so (umf/ folder, *_UMF.zip); everything else is MUGEN. The same fighter can exist in both formats: they are never merged, each variant keeps its own badge, state and download, and variants of one fighter are sorted next to each other (Goku_SS4 and Goku_SSJ4_UMF count as one fighter).
  • Outdated items. An installed item whose repository version (hash of file paths and shas, see above) differs from the one installed is marked DESATUALIZADO and outlined in orange. The listing then re-downloads it automatically, and Instalar does it on demand.
  • Filters. Type (F), format Todos/MUGEN/UMF (J) and Desatualizados (P) combine with the Explorar/Instalados tabs (Tab).
  • Pack vs character. A zip's kind comes from its contents (read via HTTP Range, never the whole file): one fighter shows CHARACTER, several show PACK · N and the footer lists them (Contém (N): ...). Filter Not installed (K) hides what you already have.
  • Batch actions. Install all (Z), Update all (Y) and Remove all (B) respect the active filters; removal asks for confirmation and progress is shown in the footer.
  • Portraits. Cards show the preview image of the item: a PNG in a previews/, portraits/ or thumbs/ folder with the same name as the item (previews/umf/Goku_SSJ4_UMF.png for umf/Goku_SSJ4_UMF.zip). Only visible cards are fetched (3 at a time, from raw.githubusercontent.com), downscaled to at most 240 px wide, kept in an in-memory cache of 48 portraits and, on desktop, on disk next to the listing by blob sha. Items without a preview show their initials.

Where data lives

PlatformState and downloads
Linux$XDG_DATA_HOME/ultimate-mugen/market (default ~/.local/share/ultimate-mugen/market)
macOS~/Library/Application Support/ultimate-mugen/market
Windows%APPDATA%\ultimate-mugen\market
Androidapp internal storage, market/
WebIndexedDB database ultimate-mugen-market

Set UME_MARKET_HOME to move the folder on desktop. Each installed item is a single bundle file; the list of repositories, the installed items, the ETag of each listing and the optional token are in state.json. Bundle file names are percent-encoded with lowercase letters only, so items and folders whose names differ just in letter case never share a file on Windows or macOS.

Rate limits, token and caching

The listing uses the GitHub API (60 requests per hour without a token) and file downloads use raw.githubusercontent.com, which is not limited the same way. Listings send the saved ETag, so an unchanged repository answers 304 and is served from the local cache. A repository is refreshed when you open it if the cache is older than 10 minutes, or on demand with R.

Automatic updates

Every listing entry keeps the Git blob sha of each file. An item's version is a hash of its file paths and shas, saved with the installed item. While the game runs (and at startup) each repository that has installed items is re-listed every 10 minutes; any installed item whose version differs from the repository is downloaded again, and only that item. Updated items keep their active or inactive state. Downloads add ?v=<sha> so a fresh push is never served from the raw.githubusercontent.com cache. Items installed before versions existed are reinstalled once.

To raise the API limit press T and paste a personal access token (no scopes needed for public repositories), or set UME_GITHUB_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN on desktop. The token is only ever sent to api.github.com.

Safety limits

  • Only https links to github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, media.githubusercontent.com and codeload.github.com are fetched. Redirects to other hosts are blocked.
  • Paths coming from a repository are validated: no .., absolute paths, backslashes, drive letters, control characters, leading spaces or Windows reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9). Unsafe entries are dropped from the listing.
  • Limits: 64 MB per file, 256 MB and 4000 files per item, 48 MB for the listing. Items above the limits are shown as "grande demais" and cannot be installed.
  • Content never runs as code. Characters are loaded by the same sandboxed parsers as manual imports.
  • Respect each author's license. Installing from a repository is a download, not a redistribution right.

Smoke test results and evidence: docs/evidence/mugen-chars-smoke.

Scrolling stages and wave villains

Each arena has a wide strip in assets/stages/story/<arena>.png, one segment per fight (4 waves plus the boss). Wave villains have around 10 % of the protagonist's maximum life (villain_life_ratio in src/story/stages.rs: 9 % to 12 % depending on archetype). When a wave is defeated the screen is released: the protagonist keeps control and explores the segment freely, a GO arrow shows at the right edge, and the camera only scrolls to the next segment once the player walks to the exit; the next wave then waits frozen off screen (the screen clamp ignores it) and walks in from the right edge once the scroll lands and the screen locks again (LaneRules::gate, Match::lane_scroll_step in crates/engine/src/lane.rs, App::story_advance_in_place in src/app/story/advance.rs). Upon reaching the rightmost segment at the end of the stage, the stage boss awaits. Regenerate the strips with python3 tools/story_segments.py; the original stage art is never modified.

Animated backdrops

The scrolling backdrop is alive in every segment. While a stage's eight ambient loop frames are loaded (see Stages), the renderer rebuilds the strip from the current frame on each draw instead of showing the static PNG: the first segment is the arena itself, the three middle segments are mirror chains of a window of the arena, and the boss segment is the arena flipped. Colour grading follows the same ramp as the baked strip and the 70 px seams are cross-faded with mirrored slices, so the result lines up with the static strip (a unit test compares both pixel by pixel outside the seams). The loop advances every eight simulation ticks, in step with versus mode, and costs no extra texture memory because it samples the frames the stage already loaded.

The layout lives in src/stages/story_loop.rs (runs, pieces, grade_at, seam_mix) and the drawing in src/render/story_loop.rs (Gfx::draw_backdrop). The static strip stays as the fallback when no loop frames exist and still defines the strip size. To capture the evidence set, run UME_TOUR=storyloop target/release/ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> (add UME_TOUR_BURST=1 for GIF frames); results are in screenshots/story-loop/.

Remaining health carries over between fights and recovers a little after each wave.

Breakables, food and bonus rounds

Crates and barrels along each strip break when struck and can drop food, a gem or a battery; stages 1 and 3 end with a bonus round (wreck the car, break the stash). See Stage objects.

Final boss and epilogues

Before the final fight, after the spare-or-finish choice, the player may call a helper: left and right cycle the native roster (or GO SOLO), confirm accepts. The helper fights beside the hero as a CPU teammate in that fight only (src/story/helper.rs, src/app/story/helper.rs); if the hero falls, control passes to the helper. Web hook: ?e2e=1&e2e_helper=1 jumps to this screen, smoke script scripts/web-helper-smoke.js.

The last stage (Kingpin Rooftop) ends against Valdric Morn, commander of the Red Star Empire and the kingpin behind the street gang. A player who picked Valdric faces Kaito Arashi instead (final_boss in src/story/epilogue.rs, which reads the last entry of STAGES).

Beating the final boss plays an epilogue before the STORY COMPLETE card. Every fighter of the roster has its own, in English, Portuguese and Spanish, made of five pages:

PageSceneContent
1Rooftop at night, boss on the groundthe boss speaks to this fighter
2Rooftop, fighter in the victory posethe fighter answers
3The fighter's home scenery at dawnnarration
4Home scenery in daylight, victory posenarration
5Home scenery, dimmedTHE END card with the fighter and the epilogue title

The scenery is the illustration of an existing stage with a slow pan, drifting light motes, letterbox bars, a fade when the scene changes and text typed letter by letter. OK reveals the line and then advances, ESC skips to the final card.

The fighter on screen plays its own animations: the walk cycle (20) carries it into the home scene, the taunt (195) or win pose (181) plays while it answers, and the win pose closes the story. Animations a fighter does not have fall back to the next one in the chain and finally to idle (src/story/epilogue_pose.rs).

Texts live in assets/story/epilogues.json, keyed by fighter id. A fighter with no entry (imported M.U.G.E.N characters or custom ones) gets an invented epilogue: one of the *:tale1 to *:tale6 templates, picked by a stable hash of the fighter id, with {name} replaced by the fighter's display name. * stays as the last resort when the name is empty:

{
  "mika": {
    "scene": "neon",
    "title": { "en": "Storm Season", "pt": "Temporada de Tempestade" },
    "boss": { "en": "Line the final boss says to this fighter." },
    "reply": { "en": "The fighter's answer." },
    "pages": [{ "en": "First narration page." }, { "en": "Second narration page." }]
  }
}

scene is any built-in stage id. A missing language falls back to English. To change or add epilogues without rebuilding, save a file with the same shape as story-epilogues.json next to the executable (or in browser storage): its entries replace the bundled ones fighter by fighter.

Code: data and lookup in src/story/epilogue.rs, flow in src/app/story/epilogue.rs, drawing in src/app/story/epilogue_draw.rs and epilogue_text.rs. Evidence in screenshots/story-epilogues/, captured with UME_TOUR=epilogue ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute; the browser check is node scripts/web-epilogue-smoke.js web/dist.

The loading screen is no longer a hero-versus-villain card in the story. Wave fights show a stage card (stage number, title, wave and hero name; src/app/story/stage_card.rs) so no enemy is exposed; the classic versus screen is kept for boss fights only, with a BOSS tag and the stage title over it.

Clearing a stage boss now pays a life bonus on top of the boss bonus: StageTally (src/story/tally.rs) gives remaining life x 2000 x stage number, and the Stage Clear screen lists both (STAGE BONUS +n LIFE +n). The browser hook ?e2e_clear=1 opens that screen for smoke checks.

Story juice (src/vfx/story_juice.rs, active only while lane rules are on): footstep dust while the hero walks, sparkles over pickups, a K.O.! pop-up with ring and sparks when a foe falls, a ring and sound when the screen is released, and an animated GO cue (pulse plus sliding chevrons). Everything is procedural, no sprite is touched.

When the scroll lands and the screen locks again, story_juice adds a screen shake, a thud, rings on both screen edges and dust bursts under the waiting wave; while the hero is below 25 % life the vignette pulses.

Stage objects: breakables, food and bonus rounds

English · Português (BR)

Story stages carry arcade-style objects that live inside the simulation: crates and barrels that break when struck, food and other pickups that pop out of them, and a bonus round where the goal is to wreck everything before the clock runs out. Everything on this page is original content and is driven by one TOML file, so a new object needs art and a few lines of data, not code.

What the player sees

  • Breakables. Any strike or projectile that reaches a crate or barrel damages it. The sprite switches to a cracked frame as it loses life, shakes and flashes on impact, and leaves splinters or a crushed drum behind for a few seconds.
  • Pickups. A broken object can drop one item. It pops up, bounces once and waits on the floor for 15 seconds (it blinks during the last 2.5). Walking over it collects it.
  • Bonus round. After the boss of the Back Alleys and of the Bamboo Grove, the villain leaves and a bonus round starts in place: wreck the car (4 damage stages, smoke and sparks when badly hit) or break the whole stash before the timer ends. No enemies and no way to lose; breaking everything pays the object score plus 200 points per second left.
PickupEffectScore
Apple+12 % life100
Pizza slice+25 % life200
Roast+50 % life400
Gemscore only1500
Battery+34 % power150

Rules (engine)

crates/engine/src/stage_objects.rs owns the state (Match::objects), so it is cloned with the match, hashed by the netplay checksum and never allocates during a tick.

  • A Breakable has a position on the floor, a lane, a hurt box (half_width, height), life and an optional PickupSpec drop. Standing strikes pass over low objects, so the hurt box is at least 100 units tall.
  • Depth: with lanes on, an attacker reaches an object when its lane is within LANE_REACH + depth of the object lane.
  • One hit per swing: after a hit the object ignores new hits for REHIT_TICKS (10). The attacker gets MoveContact/MoveHit and up to 8 ticks of hit pause, so normals cancel off a crate exactly like off a fighter.
  • solid objects (the car) push grounded fighters out of their body; jumping above the roof is free.
  • Pickups are collected only by root fighters of collector_side (the hero side), alive, within 18 units, within twice the strike lane reach and near the floor. Healing never exceeds life_max.
  • start_break_all_goal(ticks) turns the round into a bonus round: the round clock mirrors the goal clock and the round ends for side 0 when every object is broken (Goal::Cleared) or the clock runs out (Goal::TimedOut).
  • Presentation reads objects.events (Struck, Broken, Dropped, Collected, GoalCleared, GoalTimedOut) once per tick and clears it.

Data (assets/story/objects.toml)

A copy named story-objects.toml next to the executable (or in browser storage) replaces the bundled file.

[kinds.crate]
sprite = "crate"            # sheet in assets/props/story/, frames side by side
frames = 3                  # damage stages left to right, the last one is the remains
size = [48.0, 48.0]         # drawn size in world units
half_width = 20.0
height = 42.0
depth = 10.0
life = 120.0
score = 100.0
solid = false
debris = [0.78, 0.55, 0.3]  # particle colour
sound = "wood"              # "wood" or "metal"

[pickups.pizza]
sprite = "pizza"            # 6 frames, a shine sweeps across
heal = 0.25                 # fraction of the life bar
power = 0.0                 # fraction of the power bar
score = 200.0

[stages.brazil]
objects = [
  { fight = 0, kind = "crate", x = -78.0, lane = -22.0, drop = "apple" },
]

[stages.brazil.bonus]
seconds = 30
objects = [{ kind = "car", x = 34.0, lane = -16.0 }]

fight is the wave index inside the stage (the boss is the last one), x is measured from the centre of that fight's segment and lane is clamped to the stage floor band. A stage without a bonus table goes straight from the boss to the stage-clear screen.

Art

python3 tools/story_objects_art.py draws every sheet from code (flat shapes, dithered ramps, one-pixel ink outline) at 2 pixels per world unit, so the art is reproducible and free of third-party assets. Replace a PNG with a sheet of the same layout to reskin an object.

Audio

🇧🇷 Sons de personagens (.snd), música de cenário com loop e posição estéreo (pan). Formatos: WAV, OGG, MP3 e FLAC.

Formats

Character sounds come from the .snd file. Music files can be WAV, OGG Vorbis, MP3 or FLAC. Everything is decoded by symphonia (pure Rust), so the same code runs on desktop, web and Android.

Character sounds

  • Sounds play from where the fighter stands: a fighter on the left of the screen is heard on the left speaker.
  • channel works as in M.U.G.E.N: a new sound on the same channel of the same fighter replaces the old one; lowpriority = 1 keeps the old one if it is still playing.
  • PlaySnd reads pan, abspan, loop, freqmul, volumescale, channel and lowpriority. StopSnd stops one channel, or every sound of the character with channel = -1.
  • Looping sounds keep playing until the channel is stopped or the fight ends.
  • SndPan moves sounds that are already playing on that channel (or every channel and looping sound of the character with channel = -1); playback continues from the same point.
  • A sound that fails to decode still plays, without panning.

Move voices

Every special, super, finisher and awakening of the native roster is announced by its fighter when the move starts, anime style (Hellflame Orb!). Each fighter has its own voice and the Settings > Audio row Move voices scales or mutes them (0% turns them off).

  • Clips live in assets/voices/voices.bank, embedded in the binary (about 0.9 MB, 16 kHz Vorbis, one stream per fighter). A move's clip is found by the move id; ex_ versions reuse the base move's clip and the npc_* fighters borrow their parent's voice.
  • MoveInfo.state ties the move to its state, so the voice fires on the state change and follows cancels, combos and form moves.
  • Clips are generated offline with Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0, model and voices) through kokoro-onnx (MIT): python3 tools/voices/generate.py [fighter...] with KOKORO_MODEL / KOKORO_VOICES pointing at kokoro-v1.0.onnx / voices-v1.0.bin from the kokoro-onnx releases, plus ffmpeg with libvorbis. The cast table (voice, speed, effect per fighter) is at the top of that script. Nothing is synthesised at run time.
  • To add a fighter, add it to the cast table and rerun the script; moves without a clip stay silent.

Built-in music per stage

Every stage without a [Music] entry plays one of the built-in synthesized themes, picked by the stage (Stage.music), so the dojo, neon city, bamboo grove, volcano and the other arenas each have their own track. Themes are rendered once at startup on a background thread (music-synth) and loop until the fight ends.

Hit sounds and impact ducking

  • Hits come in tiers: hitlight, hit and hitheavy, each with three detuned variants, so repeated hits never sound identical. Counter hits, supers, transformations and the KO have their own sounds.
  • Impact ducking dips the music for a moment on a hit (hit 0.8, hitheavy 0.55, counter 0.45, super 0.35, ko 0.2 of the current level) and recovers smoothly.
  • A crowd cheer plays on the KO.
  • AssertSpecial nomusic silences the music and keeps the effects.

Stage music (M.U.G.E.N stages)

[Music]
bgmusic = sound/stage.ogg
bgmloopstart = 88200
bgmloopend = 1764000

bgmloopstart and bgmloopend are in samples. The song plays once up to bgmloopend, then repeats the part between the two points. With both at 0 the whole file loops. If the file is missing or cannot be decoded, the built-in music for the stage plays instead.

Character select

Research summary

Common traits of well-known fighting-game select screens (Street Fighter, Tekken, King of Fighters, Guilty Gear, Marvel vs. Capcom, Smash):

  • A compact roster grid in the centre, with a highly visible cursor and the hovered fighter shown large on the side of the player who owns the cursor.
  • Each player has a distinct colour (blue for P1, red for P2) used for the cursor, the name plate and the panel edge.
  • The big portrait changes instantly on hover with a short slide and fade, never a hard pop.
  • Confirming gives an immediate, clearly different response: flash, pose change, a "ready" mark and a sound.
  • Team modes show a row of slots that fill in order, with the next slot highlighted.
  • The stage is chosen on the same screen or right after it, with a thumbnail and name.
  • Every fighter is shown at a comparable on-screen size so small characters are not lost.

Design adopted

  • Glass panels, the same look as the menu and HUD: translucent body, light top edge, accent edge per side.
  • Left and right panels with the hovered fighter in a large frame, a coloured glow from the fighter's own colour, a floor shadow, slide and fade on change, a flash and ring on confirm and the confirmation pose.
  • Smoothly following cursor with pulsing fill, corner brackets and a P1/P2/CPU tag; non-hovered tiles are dimmed.
  • Team slots (up to 5) with portrait, name and a numbered badge on the picked tiles.
  • Stage chip in the header, cycled with [ and ] or by clicking the arrows; the stage grid still confirms it after the fighters.
  • Palette row under each side panel: 12 numbered swatches with the current one highlighted. , / . cycle, P picks a random palette, clicking a swatch jumps to it; each side keeps its own palette and team members are stored independently. The last palette of each player is persisted in ultimate-mugen.cfg (pal1, pal2) and in replays.
  • Keyboard, gamepad and touch/mouse use the same navigation as before.
  • Grid navigation moves by column: Up and Down keep the current column and land on the closest tile of the target row, so a shorter last row never blocks or skips the cursor. PgUp/PgDn move a whole page, Home/End jump to the ends, the wheel scrolls by row and R picks a random tile.

Uniform character size

draw_char_fit scales a fighter so the union of the bounding boxes of all idle-animation frames fits a fixed frame, centred horizontally with the feet on the baseline. The extent is computed once per fighter and cached (App::char_extent). The same function is used by the select panels, the roster tiles that fall back to sprites, and the versus screen. Sprite and stage art files are never modified.

Performance

  • Only visible tiles are drawn and decoded; one portrait is decoded per frame.
  • Upper-case names and the stage/filter labels are cached or written into a reused buffer, so the screen allocates nothing per frame in steady state.

Strength, life and sorting

Each tile has a thin gold bar at its bottom edge for strength. The side panel shows three gauges above the name plate: FOR (strength), VID (life) and VEL (walk speed).

Definitions, read from each character's data (native and M.U.G.E.N alike):

  • Strength = data.attack × data.life / 1000 (defaults 100 and 1000, so an average character is 100). Gauge full at 200.
  • Life = data.life (default 1000). Gauge full at 2000.
  • Speed = velocity.walk.fwd.x (default 2.4). Gauge full at 6.0.

Press O on the select screen to cycle the order: roster, strength, life, speed, name. The choice is saved as sort= in the config. Stats come from the character's cached preview and are computed once per character.

Limitation: sorting by a stat loads the preview of every character in the view the first time, so a very large M.U.G.E.N roster can take a moment on that first press.

Large rosters (1000+ fighters and stages)

  • The visible list (filter, search and sort) is computed once and reused until the filter, sort, search text or the playable set changes (src/app/select_view.rs). With 1017 fighters a name sort costs about 0.9 ms when rebuilt and 0.08 ms when reused.
  • The grid only uses as many rows as fit above the footer, or above the team slots in team modes, so the slots never cover the last row (src/app/select_grid.rs).
  • The cursor tag (P1, P2, CPU) is drawn inside the tile, so it no longer covers the name of the tile above. Tile names are cut to the tile width with an ellipsis (App::fit_label).
  • A search pill under the title shows the current search and the number of results; / or a click opens the search page, Esc or a click clears it. Search matches name, id, author and series. On the search page the arrows and PgUp/PgDn choose a result and Enter moves the cursor to it.
  • The footer shows the page (page 3/15) next to the position.
  • F or the star button marks the fighter under the cursor as a favorite; favorites show a gold star on their tile and are saved (favorites.txt). Every pick is recorded in the 24 most recent picks (recent.txt). The FAVORITES and RECENT filter chips show only those fighters, recent ones newest first (src/app/select_marks.rs).
  • The author chip (U, Shift+U or a click) cycles through authors ordered by fighter count and combines with the other filters (src/app/select_author.rs).
  • On touch devices the search page shows an on-screen keyboard (letters, digits, space, delete, OK, close) and fewer result rows; tapping a result picks it (src/app/select_search/keyboard.rs). UME_OSK=1 forces it on desktop.

Stage select

  • Filter chips (All, Originals, M.U.G.E.N), cycled with Tab, and a search box opened with / or a click; Esc clears the search.
  • Names are cut to the tile width with an ellipsis; Home/End jump to the ends; the footer shows position and page.
  • Random picks among the stages that match the current filter and search.
  • M.U.G.E.N stage previews start only after the cursor rests for 0.12 s, one per frame, and previews more than six rows away are released, so scrolling through hundreds of M.U.G.E.N stages does not keep every decoded stage in memory.

Stress mode

UME_STRESS=<n> (desktop) or ?stress=<n> (web) adds n generated fighters and n generated stages (up to 5000) that reuse the bundled content with generated names, authors and series. It is a test hook only. UME_STRESS=1000 UME_SHOTS_ONLY=roster ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute prints roster-perf: lines (view cost per sort, CPU time per frame while walking the grid and the stage list, memory) and saves screenshots of the grid, search and stage filters.

Game modes

English · Português (BR)

The main menu offers single fights (Arcade, Versus CPU, 2 Players, Training, CPU vs CPU) and three team modes. The select screen has a mode chip (< > or M) that cycles Versus CPU, 2 Players, CPU vs CPU and the team modes; in a team mode a size chip (- + or Q / E) picks the squad. The web build allows up to 7 per side; native Android and iOS cap at 5 because their sprite atlas is 2048.

ModeFighters in playRound ends when
Team · Sequence1 per side, the next teammate enters after a KO; the winner keeps its lifeone side runs out of fighters
Team · Parallelthe whole team at once (2 to 7), each fighter spawning at a random spot of the stage (seeded, so replays match); Tab hands your controller to the next teammateevery member of a side is KO'd
Team · Tag1 active + the rest on standby (2 or 3 per side)every member of a side is KO'd

Arcade / Story Mode

Arcade in the main menu runs the Scarlet Eclipse Tournament story campaign with full cutscenes, dynamic villain progression, and secret fighter unlocks:

  • Prologue (Cutscene kind: 0). Each of the 15 native fighters has a unique opening narrative and personal vow before entering the tournament ladder.
  • Dynamic Boss Rotation. The 8-opponent ladder culminates in a dedicated final boss battle with tailored pre-boss dialogue cutscene and boss arena:
    • Tier 0 (First Run): The supreme architect Mikazuki Oboro (oboro) at Gate of Spirits (spirit).
    • Tier 1 (After Beating Oboro): Garan the Ashen Oni (garan) becomes the new main villain at the Volcanic Crater (volcano).
    • Tier 2 (After Beating Garan): Valdric Morn (valdric) ascends as the imperial tyrant final boss at Neo-Metropolis (neon).
    • Subsequent Clears: Rotates cyclically among the 3 main villains. If the player selects the active villain, the engine shifts to an alternate boss to prevent mirror fights.
  • Boss Empowerment & Oboro Phases. When fighting as the arcade final boss, villains receive true boss status (boss = true, 2000 HP, 125% attack multiplier, boss AI level, power gauge auto-generation, aura VFX, and a dedicated CHEFE FINAL banner). When facing Oboro:
    • Phase 1: Oboro fights with flight, shadow teleportation, super speed, and his first awakening (Véu Desperto, form = 1). If Oboro loses a round during the match, he automatically breaks his seal at the start of the next round (Match::awaken_defeated_boss).
    • Phase 2 (Awakening: Absolute Eclipse - Cutscene kind: 3): Defeating Oboro the first time triggers the Awakening: Absolute Eclipse cutscene (kind: 3), launching Phase 2 (Match::awaken_boss_phase(2)) where Oboro starts in Eclipse Absoluto (form = 2) with boosted max life (1.15x), dark regeneration, accelerated meter gain, level-8 AI, and Phase 2 moves (Corte do Eclipse Carmesim, Chama do Eclipse Eterno, Julgamento do Eclipse Absoluto).
    • Phase 3 (Climax Battle Cutscene - Cutscene kind: 4 & Supreme Awakening): Defeating Oboro in Phase 2 triggers an animated supersonic combat clash cutscene (src/app/cutscene/battle.rs) with striking animations, weapon sparks, and speedlines where Oboro ascends into his ultimate celestial form: Eclipse Primordial (form = 3). Phase 3 features supreme stats (1.62x attack, 1.48x defense, 1.30x life), supernova cyan aesthetic, enhanced AI, and exclusive moves (Colapso Primordial, Supernova do Eclipse Primordial).
    • Finishing Strike Cutscene (Cutscene kind: 5) & Shattered Eclipse: Defeating Oboro's supreme form triggers a climactic finishing blow cutscene where the hero delivers a supersonic decisive strike, an anime impact frame, shatters Oboro's cursed blade, and breaks the eclipsed moon into radiant golden dawn rays.
  • Character Ending Cutscenes (Cutscene kind: 2) & Oboro Unlock. Following the defeat cutscene, the player's character-specific ending cutscene plays (src/app/cutscene/endings.rs) with personalized victory epilogue narrative. Completing the ladder unlocks Mikazuki Oboro on the character select screen, advances the villain rotation, and returns directly to the Main Menu (Screen::Menu).

Story (brawler stages)

Story in the main menu is a Final Fight / Sengoku style run: five stages, each a few waves of street thugs fought all at once (1 versus 2 to 4, using the simultaneous-team rules) closed by a stage boss.

  • Stage checkpoints. Clearing a stage saves the next stage, fighter, palette, life, score and credits in one local checkpoint. Open Story again and select Resume to start that stage, or New campaign to choose a fighter. A new campaign replaces that checkpoint when it clears a stage. Finishing the campaign clears the checkpoint. Saves are stored in story-checkpoint.json beside the executable or in browser storage.
  • Structure & right-scrolling progression. Stage = 4 waves + 1 boss along a wide stage strip (assets/stages/story/<arena>.png). As each wave of street thugs is defeated, the protagonist advances to the right while the camera scrolls smoothly into the next stage segment (Match::lane_scroll_step, App::story_advance_in_place), culminating in the stage boss at the far right end of the stage. Backdrops: Back Alleys (Brazil square), Subway (Neo-Metropolis), Bamboo Grove, Industrial Area (Volcanic Crater) and the Kingpin Rooftop (Dojo). Bosses: Bruno, Marlow, Lian, Garan, Valdric. Picking a boss as your fighter swaps in the alternate (Daichi, Kaname, Shion, Haruki, Kaito).
  • Wave villain & boss tuning. Wave villains have around 10 % of the protagonist's maximum life (9 %–12 % via villain_life_ratio in src/story/stages.rs) so waves play like brisk beat-'em-up encounters; stage bosses at the end of the stage get 150 % life and 110 % attack.
  • Life carries over. The bar you end a wave with is the bar you start the next with, plus 20 % after a wave and 60 % after a stage (the "food pickups" of the arcade originals).
  • Breakables, food and bonus rounds. Every fight has crates or barrels that break when struck and may drop food (apple +12 %, pizza +25 %, roast +50 % life), a gem (score) or a battery (power). After the bosses of stages 1 and 3 a bonus round starts in place: wreck the car or break the whole stash before the clock runs out. Rules, data file and art: Stage objects.
  • Credits. You start with 3 credits; a KO offers Continue (resumes the same fight with 60 % life) until they run out.
  • Score. The engine's ScoreTotal of the fight plus a wave bonus (500 x stage, boss x4).
  • Difficulty. CPU level rises with the stage and +2 on bosses (cap 8).
  • Rebinding conflicts. In Controls, binding a key that another action of the same player uses swaps the two keys and says so; binding a key the other player already uses is allowed but shows a warning (KeyMap::conflicts, src/keybinds/conflict.rs; UME_SHOTS_ONLY=keys captures it).
  • Depth lanes (Final Fight style). Story fights have a floor band: two extra buttons walk the fighter toward the back or the front of the scene (P1 Z / X, P2 Num - / Num +, rebindable under Controls; the engine bits are LANE_UP / LANE_DOWN). Walking works only while grounded and in control, and each stage limits the band to its real floor (lane_far / lane_near in src/story/stages.rs). A strike connects, and bodies push each other, only when both fighters are within 14 units of depth (Match::lanes, crates/engine/src/lane.rs); the CPU thugs line up with the hero by themselves. Sprites, shadows, reflections and effects follow the lane and nearer fighters draw in front. Other modes never enable lanes.
  • Final boss and epilogues. The final boss is Valdric Morn on the Kingpin Rooftop (a player using Valdric faces Kaito Arashi). Beating him plays a five-page cutscene epilogue written for each fighter, in English, Portuguese and Spanish, before the STORY COMPLETE card. Texts live in assets/story/epilogues.json and can be replaced with a story-epilogues.json file next to the executable. Details: Story Mode.
  • Guard button. Story has a dedicated guard button (P1 C, P2 Num *, rebindable). While held, a grounded fighter with control blocks like holding back, but without walking away (hold Down with it to guard crouching). It is ignored outside Story.
  • Story HUD. Thugs get no life bar or roster tile. The hero keeps the left panel, a bottom strip shows stage, wave, score and credits, and the boss fight adds a wide Stage Villain bar (name and life) on the right.
  • Street thugs (assets/chars/npc_*.json, generated by ume-tools gen-story-npcs). Fighters with dedicated sprite packs under assets/chars/sprites/npc_*/, hidden from select ("npc": true), scaled in Story Mode to ~10 % of the protagonist's life, each with its own trait:

Their move sets retain a playable fighter as a mechanical base. Their art is PNG sprites only; replace the files under assets/chars/sprites/npc_*/ and rebuild the web packs with ume-tools pack-sprites.

NPCMove set baseStory LifeTrait
BruteBruno11 % of herostrong and hkick carry armor
RazorSuzume9 % of hero35 % faster, kicks lunge forward
SpitfireAkio10 % of herojab throws a small orb (ranged pressure)

Evidence capture: UME_TOUR=storymode ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute plays the whole run with a CPU-driven hero and saves every intro, wave, boss and result screen.

Survival

Sobrevivência in the main menu is an endless run against the whole roster:

  • Opponents. After you pick your fighter, the game picks the opponent each round (never the hidden boss, never a broken pack). The stage rotates every round.
  • Escalation. The CPU level climbs every two fights, starting from your difficulty setting and capped at 8.
  • Life carries over. The bar you end a fight with is the bar you start the next one with, plus the recovery configured under Gameplay › Life recovered (Survival) (0 / 20 / 35 / 50 / 100 %). A KO ends the run.
  • Score. Each win banks the engine's own Score/ScoreTotal for your side plus a 1000 × round clear bonus, so the number is deterministic and comes from the simulation itself.
  • Game over. The end screen shows the score, how many fights you won and the local best; the best is persisted in ultimate-mugen.cfg (survival_best) and a new record is highlighted.
  • Replays. The last fight is archived like any other and can be watched from the game-over screen (R button) or the Replays browser; the replay keeps the starting life so the re-simulation matches exactly.

Engine score stats used: Fighter::score and Fighter::score_total, filled by HitDef.score and the ScoreAdd/TargetScoreAdd controllers and read by the Score/ScoreTotal triggers.

Two-player co-op (Arcade and Survival)

Press V on the character select screen (or click the CO-OP 2P button) to start Arcade or Survival with two human players on the same side:

  • P1 and P2 pick one fighter each; both are on the field together (2 versus 1) using the engine's simultaneous-team support, so the normal pushboxes, targeting and camera work apply.
  • The side only loses the round/run when both fighters are KO'd (team_simul KO rule).
  • Inputs are independent: P1 uses the player-1 keys/pad, P2 the player-2 ones (Tab is not needed). The HUD tags each fighter P1 / P2 by its pilot slot instead of by side.
  • Arcade keeps both fighters across the ladder and swaps the opponent each round; Survival does the same each wave.
  • Replays record both slots, so a co-op fight replays exactly.

Engine switches: Match::team_simul. Slots are added interleaved (P1, opponent, P2), so roots()[0] and roots()[2] are the human pair.

Tag team

Each side lists 2 or 3 fighters. Only the first one is in play at the start of every round; the others wait on standby.

  • Swap. Press the Tag button (F for P1, Num Enter for P2; rebindable under Controls, action "Troca (Tag)"). On gamepads and touch the awakening button (R3 / SELECT) swaps instead, because awakening is disabled in this mode. The CPU swaps by itself when its fighter is below 30 % life and the partner is clearly healthier.
  • Cooldown. After every swap the side waits tag_cooldown_max ticks (default 180, three seconds) before it can swap again. The HUD shows a bar and a TAG mark under each teammate's portrait.
  • Tag cancel window. A swap is accepted only when the active fighter has control, or during the first tag_cancel_window ticks (default 30) after one of its attacks touched the opponent (hit or block). So you can cancel the recovery of a connected move into the partner, but not in the middle of a whiff or while being hit.
  • Standby fighters. They are invisible, cannot be hit, pushed or targeted (enemy, P2, EnemyNear skip them), receive no input and keep their life. They follow the active fighter's position so they enter exactly where the swap happened, in state 0 with control.
  • KO. When the active fighter dies, the next living teammate enters automatically after 50 ticks (cooldown ignored). The round ends only when every member of a side has no life left; the round timer decides by the summed life of the whole team.
  • Life and variables of a swapped-out fighter are untouched; everybody starts the next round with full life.
  • Scripts. TeamMode returns 3 in this mode. TagOut / TagIn swap the fighters for real (see Ikemen extensions); Standby is 1 for the waiting fighters and NumPartner counts the teammates.
  • Replays record the Tag button like any other input, so a Tag fight replays exactly.

Engine switches (Match): team_tag, tag_cooldown_max, tag_cancel_window. Events: Event::Tag { side, fighter }.

Training dummy

In Training the pause menu (Game tab) has a Dummy behaviour row. Confirming it cycles the plan, which applies at once and is kept across restarts of the fight:

PlanWhat the dummy holds
StandNothing
CrouchDown
JumpUp on every landing
GuardBack, only while the rival attacks or a projectile is alive (it does not walk away)
Low guardDown, plus back while threatened
Record my inputsNothing; every input you press is recorded (up to 10 s)
Play recordingYour recorded inputs on a loop, mirrored to the dummy's facing
AI learns youCounts how you switch actions (walk, crouch, jump, attack) and answers your likeliest next one: back guard before an attack; attack when you jump, walk or crouch. Keeps learning across plan changes

The plan lives in Pilot::Dummy(DummyPlan) (src/session/dummy.rs); the dummy presses real input bits, so guard rules, pushback and chip damage are the engine's own. The recording lives in src/session/dummy_tape.rs; a right-side panel shows the best combo and the tape length (src/hud/training_panel.rs). Screenshots: UME_SHOTS_ONLY=pause writes training-dummy-*.png and pause-training-dummy.png; UME_SHOTS_ONLY=training writes training-tape-playback.png.

Power Arena

Choose Power Arena in the main menu, set up the match and pick your fighters to start against the CPU. Climb 40 floating platforms across eight tiers. Jump through them from below and land on them while descending. Fighters can recover while they are above the base. Once they fall past its edge, they tumble into the void, and the round ends when the fighter falls out. The camera follows changes in elevation and zooms out as fighters separate horizontally or vertically.

The two fighters start on the floor under an inner platform of the first tier, so a walk and a jump reach it. Until the rival lands on a platform, or until a hit connects, the CPU climbs toward its own platform and does not attack. After that first landing the CPU fights with its usual pressure, and a ring-out still ends the round.

Open a match directly on the web with ?modo=arena&p1=kaito&p2=shion&luta=1.

Squad vs. swarm (1 to 5 against up to 100)

The menu entry opens a setup screen before the fighter select: your squad (1 to 5 fighters), enemies (1, 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100) and the enemy type (random fighters, or pick one fighter who is repeated). Mouse, touch, keyboard and gamepad all work on it.

  • Only a capped number of enemies is on the field at once (16 on desktop, 12 in the browser, 8 on Android/iOS). When one falls, a fresh one enters after a short delay at a random spot of the stage (floor or platform) away from your squad, until the chosen total is spent. The round ends when the last enemy is down or your whole squad is.

  • Random enemies come from at most 8 distinct fighters (6 in the browser, 3 on mobile) that share their sprites, so the sprite atlas and memory stay flat no matter how many enemies you choose.

  • The map grows with the crowd: it is built from an odd number of tiles of the original 1,108 px arena (1, 3, 5 or 7), with the platform layout repeated. Ring-out edges follow the wider map.

  • The camera follows your squad only, so far-away enemies do not stretch the zoom. Fighters outside the view are not drawn.

  • A minimap appears under the top HUD whenever the map is wider than the view: green and cyan dots are your squad, red dots the enemies, and the yellow frame is the camera. The HUD shows enemies left over the chosen total.

  • Power elixir: a glowing flask floats on the highest platform (marked in gold on the minimap). Whoever reaches it first, your fighter or any enemy, doubles their maximum life and refills it completely. It exists once per round and is given back when the next round starts. Code: crates/engine/src/matchs/elixir.rs, drawing in src/power_arena_elixir.rs.

Code: simulation in crates/engine/src/matchs/swarm.rs (Match::enable_swarm, swarm_step) and crates/engine/src/matchs/power_arena.rs, opening climb in crates/engine/src/ai/arena.rs, setup screen in src/app/arena_setup.rs and arena_pick.rs, minimap and tiled platforms in src/power_arena.rs. Evidence capture: UME_SHOTS_ONLY=arena ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute also prints step and draw times, atlas fill and upload size (UME_ARENA_SLOTS, UME_ARENA_POOL and UME_ARENA_TOTAL override the profile).

In-Fight Easter Eggs

Ultimate MUGEN includes a presentation-only in-fight Easter Egg system (src/easter.rs and src/easter/) that reacts to classic fighting-game moments, stage phenomena, and fighter lore without touching the deterministic simulation (crates/engine).

Architecture

  • Deterministic safe: reads &Match state on the presentation thread (src/app/fight_screen.rs), never mutates simulation state, and keeps rollback/replay checksums unchanged.
  • Localized: every banner, speech bubble, and cameo caption ships in English, Portuguese, and Spanish via crate::i18n::tr3.
  • Pixel-art animated sprites: compact multi-frame RGBA sprite sheets in assets/easter/ rendered with FilterMode::Nearest.
  • Non-intrusive pacing: per-round and per-match bitset tracking, global cooldowns, and a 3-item on-screen cap keep fights readable.

TOML Customization (assets/interactions.toml)

Taunts, fighter rivalries, home-turf stage reactions, and in-fight character triggers are all data-driven in assets/interactions.toml. Players and creators can place an interactions.toml file in their user storage directory to override taunt pools or append custom interactions for both native UMF fighters and imported M.U.G.E.N characters without recompiling:

[[matchup]]
id = "custom_rivalry"
fighters = ["ryu", "ken"]
speaker_id = "ken"
speaker = "KEN"
style = "speech"
sfx = "easter_banter"
color = [1.0, 0.45, 0.2]
title_pt = "Vamos nessa, Ryu! Sem segurar!"
title_en = "Come on, Ryu! Don't hold back!"
title_es = "¡Vamos, Ryu! ¡Sin contenerse!"

Supported sections:

  • [taunts]: opening_pt/en/es and answer_pt/en/es round-start taunt pools.
  • [[matchup]]: fighters = [a, b] or mirror = true, style, sprite, sfx, color, localized title_* and sub_*.
  • [[stage_interaction]]: fighter + stage_contains = [...].
  • [[fighter_trigger]]: fighter or fighter_prefix, trigger ("low_hp", "combo", "opp_combo", "super", "super_or_combo", "taunt"), threshold, per_round.

Two-Part Rival Exchanges ([[exchange]]) & Full-Roster Taunts

assets/interactions.toml also supports back-and-forth two-part [[exchange]] dialogues (Fighter A speaks, and Fighter B automatically replies delay_ticks later), plus first_attack, transform, and round_win triggers, and dedicated taunt lines for all 16 playable fighters.

Netplay and Replays

English · Português (BR)

🇧🇷 O netplay usa rollback (GGRS): cada jogador roda a luta localmente, prevê o controle do adversário e corrige quando o controle real chega. Replays guardam só os controles de cada frame.

Playing online (desktop)

Both players use the same build and the same characters and stage files. Each one opens UDP port 7000 (player 1) or 7001 (player 2), or the port given with --port.

ultimate-mugen --netplay 1 --peer <friend-ip>:7001 --chars kfm,kfm --stage dojo
ultimate-mugen --netplay 2 --peer <friend-ip>:7000 --chars kfm,kfm --stage dojo
FlagMeaning
`--netplay 12`
--peer ip:portthe other player's address
--port nlocal UDP port (default 7000 / 7001)
--chars a,bcharacter ids or names for P1 and P2 (same on both sides)
--stage idstage id or name
--delay ninput delay in frames (default 2)

The bottom of the screen shows the connection state and ping. Pause is disabled online. Browser and mobile netplay arrive with the WebRTC transport after the wgpu/winit migration.

How rollback works here

  • The whole fight state is Match. Saving a frame is match.clone(); character data (CharDef) is shared through Arc, so a snapshot only copies the moving parts.
  • ume_netplay::Rollback answers the GGRS requests: save, load and advance. Only the newest frame returns presentation events (sounds, hit sparks), so rolled-back frames never replay a sound twice.
  • ume_netplay::checksum hashes positions, states, life, power, variables, explods and projectiles. GGRS compares it between peers to detect desyncs.
  • Inputs are one u32 per player per frame (the same bits as local play).

Spectators and netplay data in replays

A third connection type observes without contributing input:

ultimate-mugen --spectate --peer <host-ip>:7000 [--port 7002] [--chars a,b --stage id]

It builds a GGRS SpectatorSession (PlayerType::Spectator), renders the confirmed inputs from the host and never sends local input; the overlay shows SPECTATOR · ping · frames behind.

Replays recorded online store the session configuration (netplay: side, peer, port, delay, rollback window, player count, spectator flag) next to the inputs, so a desync can be reproduced with the same settings. When GGRS reports a desync, the game writes replays/desync-<unix>.json with that config, the frame, Match::checksum() and the last 120 input frames. A desync report is a diagnostic, not a replay: the Replays menu never lists it (neither as a fight nor as an unreadable file), so it does not look like a corrupted replay after a desync.

Rules for deterministic content

  • Never read real time (Instant, now) or random numbers from the operating system (rand::random, rand::thread_rng) during a tick; use the match's seeded PRNG.
  • Floating-point calculations must run in deterministic mode (all target platforms use IEEE 754 with standard rounding).
  • All collections whose iteration affects the simulation must have deterministic ordering (use Vec or sorted keys, never direct iteration over a raw HashSet/HashMap).

Binary format (ume_netplay::Replay)

A raw stream of recorded inputs:

FieldType
magicUMRP
versionu32 (1)
playersu32
metadata count, then key/value stringsu32 length + UTF-8
frame countu32
runsu32 repeat count + one u32 input per player

Equal consecutive frames are stored once, so held buttons cost almost nothing.

The reader rejects incomplete or overlong frame runs, trailing bytes, files larger than 129 MiB, decoded input streams larger than 64 MiB and more than 16,384 metadata entries. The writer returns an error when player counts, frame data or metadata exceed these limits. The encoded size allows a worst-case run per frame while decoded frames remain capped at 64 MiB.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
let mut rec = Replay::new(2);
rec.meta.push(("p1".into(), "kfm".into()));
rec.push(&[p1_bits, p2_bits]);
std::fs::write("fight.umr", rec.to_bytes().expect("valid replay size"))?;
}

Saved replays in the game (replays/)

Every finished fight is archived automatically to replays/ beside the executable as a small JSON file (<label>-<unix-time>.umr.json). The menu entry Replays lists them newest first.

FieldMeaning
format / versionultimate-mugen-replay / 1; a different version is refused with a clear message
label, saved_atname shown in the browser and the Unix timestamp (sorted by it)
modeArcade, Cpu, Versus, Training, Watch, TeamSeq, TeamSimul, TeamTag
chars, stage, palettesfighter ids, stage id and the palette of each side
seedinitial RNG seed of the match (replays restore it before the first tick)
teams, simul, tagteam line-ups by fighter id (team modes)
rulesrounds, round time, life %, single round, pushbox, shared team life, game speed
inputsrun-length encoded input stream: slots, then count + one input per slot per run

Replay decoding bounds files to 16 MiB, 500,000 runs and 2,000,000 total frames to keep malformed or corrupt streams from allocating unbounded memory. Desync reports (desync-*.json) in replays/ are preserved without being listed as corrupt replays.

Replaying feeds the recorded inputs through Pilot::Replay; the simulation is deterministic, so the fight is rebuilt exactly. A round-trip test records 1200 ticks, reloads the file and compares the final state checksum (cargo test -p ume-engine --test it replay_roundtrip::).

Browser keys:

KeyAction
↑ / ↓, Enterpick and play
Rrename (Enter confirms, Esc cancels)
Delete (twice)delete the selected file
Stoggle sorting between date and name
Escback to the menu

Playback keys:

KeyAction
Space / Startpause and resume
1 / 2 / 4playback speed 1x, 2x, 4x
. or → while pausedadvance one frame
Escleave the replay and return to the browser

The folder keeps the newest 64 files; older ones are pruned when a new replay is saved. Files that cannot be read (for example, recorded by another build) are listed with the reason instead of failing silently.

Universe and Lore — The Great Convergence

The world of Ultimate MUGEN is set in an era known as The Great Convergence (A Grande Convergência), where time, geography, and dimensions have collided following the cataclysmic awakening of the Scarlet Eclipse (Eclipse Escarlate).

The Genesis: The Astral Loom and The Severing

For millennia, human history unfolded along distinct cultural and martial currents. Warriors from secluded Japanese mountain shrines, Chinese Taoist sanctuaries, Nordic glacial fortresses, futuristic cyberpunk megacities, Mongolian plateaus, and dusty Latin American towns trained in isolation, oblivious to the existence of parallel realms.

Beneath the physical world hummed the Astral Loom (A Trama Astral) — a metaphysical network of cosmic leylines that regulated the flow of life force, ancestral spirits, and elemental energies.

This delicate equilibrium shattered when Mikazuki Oboro, an immortal sorcerer and master of illusions from an ancient forgotten dynasty, cast the forbidden ritual of the Scarlet Eclipse. By harnessing black flames and celestial alignment, Oboro fractured the dimensional membrane, pulling disparate epochs, technology levels, and landscapes into a singular, unstable battleground known as The Convergence Domain.

flowchart TD
    subgraph AstralSource ["The Primordial Astral Loom"]
        Ki["Ki / Wind Arts"]
        Glacial["Glacial Ice Essence"]
        Stellar["Stellar & Plasma Ki"]
        Cyber["Neon Grid & Cyber-Drive"]
        Shadow["Shadow & Cursed Arts"]
        Tao["Taoist Chi & Balance"]
    end

    AstralSource --> Eclipse["The Scarlet Eclipse (Mikazuki Oboro)"]

    subgraph Factions ["Factions of the Convergence"]
        Heroes["The Convergence Protectors<br/>(Kaito, Daichi, Akio, Lian, Bruno, Jin, Haruki)"]
        Rogues["The Solitary Exiles & Neutral Rogues<br/>(Shion, Suzume, Volta, Marlow, Sylene, Kaname)"]

    end

    Eclipse --> Factions
    Factions --> Climax["The Apex Confrontation: The Volcanic Caldera & Spirit Gate"]

Energy Systems & Martial Disciplines

Warriors in Ultimate MUGEN channel their fighting spirits through distinct energy sources:

  1. Primordial Wind (Arashi-Ki): Channelled by Kaito Arashi and Jin Kazaguruma. It draws power from atmospheric currents, typhoons, and aerial pressure, enabling high-speed gap-closers, vacuum strikes, and cutting gale projectiles.
  2. Stellar Plasma (Hoshi-No-Hikari): Mastered by Akio Hoshi. Taps into cosmic radiation and fallen meteorites, manifested as incandescent bursts, supernova impacts, and blazing plasma fist strikes.
  3. Lupine Earth & Primal Ki (Ginrou-Ki): Harnessed by Daichi Ginrou. Drawn directly from wild predatory instincts and mountain earth leylines, converting battle thirst into a radiant golden aura.
  4. Absolute Zero & Spirit Frost (Hyōketsu): Wielded by Sylene Vashti and Kaname Fuyutsuki. Freezes moisture in the air into crystalline blades, glacial barriers, and piercing soul-severing slashes.
  5. Taoist Chi & Wind-Silk (Yu-Chi): Practiced by Lian Feng. Focuses on deflection, gravitational redistribution, and fluid roundhouse kicks that ripple through kinetic space.
  6. Kinetic Iron Supremacy (Punho de Ferro): Refined by Bruno "Bulldozer" Volk. Pure human musculoskeletal conditioning, heavy-weight kinetic momentum, and unbreakable close-quarters boxing devastating enough to shatter mystic auras.
  7. Cyber-Drive & Overcharge (Grade Neon): The energy framework of VX-9 Volta. High-frequency dielectric capacitors, super-conducting servos, and digital particle beams running on artificial consciousness.
  8. Ashen Hellfire (Oni-No-Hai): Erupted from Garan the Ashen Oni. Cold violet flames forged in subterranean demon gates that consume spiritual fortitude rather than burning flesh.
  9. Tempest Aether (Aether dos Mares): Harnessed by Captain Marlow Reyes. Sky-sailor energy infused with storm lightning and tide currents, channeled through an enchanted cutlass.
  10. Imperial Scarlet Core (Estrela Rubra): Engineered by Valdric Morn. High-yield dark matter cannons built into heavy power armor, capable of orbital-scale shockwave blasts.
  11. Sealed Twilight Titans (Crepúsculo Selado): Locked inside Haruki Sumi. Forbidden eldritch power contained by paper talismans; if cracked by mortal peril, it unleashes cataclysmic calamity.
  12. Lunar Requiem (Kurogane Tsuki): Channelled by Shion Kurogane. Gravitational tides of the Pale Moon condensed into an impossibly heavy broadsword.
  13. Shadow Lotus Mirage (Kagerou-Ryu): Inherited by Suzume Kagerou. Phantom displacement, sensory blind-spot manipulation, and silent assassination daggers.
  14. The Scarlet Veil: The supreme illusion eye of Mikazuki Oboro. Bends optical perception, summons murder-crows, and rewrites the physical consequences of combat inside the victim's subconscious.

The Three Factions: Heroes, Neutrals, and Villains

The warriors of the Convergence are divided into three distinct philosophical camps:

1. The Convergence Protectors (Heroes)

Dedicated to mending the Astral Loom, closing the dimensional fissures, and protecting innocent mortals from annihilation:

  • Kaito Arashi (Japan): Wandering righteous karateka seeking balance through the storm.
  • Daichi Ginrou (Mongolia): Free-spirited mountain warrior whose golden spirit protects the vulnerable.
  • Akio Hoshi (Mexico): Impetuous star-striker whose fiery heart never backs down from tyranny.
  • Lian Feng (China): Jade Lantern Grandmaster maintaining the ancient cosmic harmony.
  • Bruno "Bulldozer" Volk (Brazil): Heavyweight people's champion defending his hometown with thunderous fists.
  • Jin Kazaguruma (Jamaica): Swift messenger of freedom fighting to preserve peace in the hidden valleys.
  • Haruki Sumi (South Korea): Gentle archivist and scholar enduring the burden of sealed apocalyptic titans.

2. The Solitary Exiles & Free Rogues (Anti-Heroes / Neutrals)

Warriors driven by personal codes, vendettas, sovereign restoration, or existential self-discovery:

  • Shion Kurogane (Egypt): Tragic swordsman bearing the crushing guilt of an exiled moon clan.
  • Suzume Kagerou (Vietnam): Vengeful shadow kunoichi hunting the masterminds who massacred her people.
  • VX-9 Volta (USA / Neo-Metropolis): Escaped military android seeking the philosophical meaning of the soul.
  • Captain Marlow Reyes (Spain / Caribbean Sky): Swashbuckling sky pirate raiding tyrants and seeking mythic loot.
  • Sylene Vashti (Norway / Borealia): Displaced glacial princess determined to reclaim her usurped frozen kingdom.
  • Kaname Fuyutsuki (Switzerland): Impartial frost samurai judge executing divine severance without emotional hesitation.

3. The Harbingers of Eclipse & Tyranny (Villains)

Entities seeking universal subjugation, demonic awakening, or reality erasure:

  • Mikazuki Oboro (Eclipse Dimension — Final Boss): Master illusionist aiming to dissolve all reality into an eternal dream of black fire.
  • Garan the Ashen Oni (Subterranean Abysm): Primordial demon unleashed to burn civilization into cold ash.
  • Valdric Morn (Germanic Red Star Empire): Megalomaniacal prince using cybernetic plasma armaments to conquer and subjugate "inferior plebeians".

The Grand Tournament: The Apex of Convergence

To sustain the dimensional tears and feast upon the combat energy of the world's greatest souls, Mikazuki Oboro manifested the Apex Crucible — a series of battlegrounds spanning ancient temples, futuristic sky-rises, primeval bamboo groves, rocky plateaus, spirit shrines, volcanic calderas, and peaceful village squares.

Fighters find themselves drawn together by cosmic gravity. Each battle fuels the convergence or brings the fighters one step closer to dismantling Oboro's grand illusion before reality permanently fades into the Scarlet Eclipse.

1. Kaito Arashi (嵐 海斗)

Standard In-Game Combat Stance

Biography & Background

Kaito Arashi is a wandering martial artist who journeys wherever the trade winds blow. Clad in a sea-green kimono that has witnessed hundreds of grueling matches across Asia, Kaito considers fighting not a sport of vanity, but a profound form of spiritual communication. Raised on the cliffs of Izu and trained by an ascetic master on the Izu Peninsula, he learned to synchronize his breathing with coastal typhoons, generating sonic shockwaves and gale-force momentum through disciplined fist thrusts.

When the Scarlet Eclipse fractured reality, Kaito was among the first to witness the sky bleeding crimson. Sensing the spiritual disharmony tearing the world apart, he took up his walking staff and descended from the mountains, determined to confront Mikazuki Oboro and safeguard the mortal realm.

Iconic Quotes

  • Intro: "I feel the tempest approaching. On guard."
  • Taunt: "Your guard has an opening. Take advantage while you can."
  • Win Quote: "The wind brought me here. Your careless guard only brought you to the floor."

Signature Moves

  • Gale Fist (Reppūken): Throws a spinning orb of condensed wind pressure along the floor.
  • Rising Tempest (Shoryū-Arashi): An airborne spiraling dragon uppercut enveloped in gale vortices.
  • Kangaroo Kick (~D, DB, B, a+b): Kaito crouches, hops forward and drives a front kick into the opponent, launching them on hit.
  • Thunderstep Kick (Tatsumaki-Kyaku): A horizontal multi-hit vacuum spin kick that breaks opponent momentum.
  • Super — Typhoon Barrage: A nine-hit chain combination culminating in a skyward tornado launch.

Key Character Dynamics

  • vs. Mikazuki Oboro: Moral and metaphysical clash. Kaito rejects Oboro’s nihilistic illusion, seeking to blow away the black flames with pure gale energy.
  • vs. Jin Kazaguruma: Fraternal mentorship. Kaito respects Jin’s raw aerial agility but frequently reminds the young ninja that wind without solid footwork is easily grounded.
  • vs. Daichi Ginrou: Legendary martial rivalry. Kaito’s serene aerodynamic precision matches Daichi’s fiery golden wolf ferocity in an endless series of respectful duels.
  • vs. Bruno Volk: East meets West striking duel. Kaito admires Bruno's indomitable human fortitude and honest punching discipline.

Shion Kurogane is a brooding exile wrapped in a midnight-black cloak. He wields an ancient greatsword forged from fallen lunar meteorite iron — a blade so unimaginably dense that ordinary warriors cannot lift it even an inch off the ground. Shion was once the supreme champion of the Kurogane Clan, but was banished after refusing to slaughter innocent pilgrims in a ritual designed to feed the blood moon.

Haunted by the ghosts of his fallen kin, Shion wanders between the bamboo forests and misty ravines under perpetual moonlight. He hunts the demonic aberrations released by the Eclipse, viewing every swing of his colossal blade as a penance for past failures.

Iconic Quotes

  • Taunt: "No rush. The night is long."
  • Win Quote: "The moon takes its time. My blade does the same."

  • Super — Requiem of the Crescent Horizon: Unleashes a panoramic midnight slash that shears through space.

Key Character Dynamics

  • vs. Kaname Fuyutsuki: Dueling philosophies of the blade. Kaname fights for solemn divine duty, while Shion fights from personal grief and atonement.
  • vs. Suzume Kagerou: Shared bond of clan survivors. Suzume respects Shion's silence, recognizing in him the same quiet hatred for the forces of Oboro.
  • vs. Garan the Ashen Oni: Nemesis match. Garan revels in suffering, while Shion’s lunar blade seeks to extinguish demonic violet fire permanently.

Every cent of his prize money goes to financing community sports gyms, orphanages, and free clinics across the countryside. Built inside the high-security black-ops laboratories of Nexkor Industries in Neo-Metropolis, the VX-9 "Volta" was designed as the ultimate autonomous combat unit: an emotionless synthetic assassin created to terminate rogue superhuman martial artists. Equipped with high-output carbon-nanotube muscles and electromagnetic particle dischargers, Volta was nearly invincible.

However, during a mission to eliminate a secluded temple, Volta’s quantum neural network experienced an emergent anomaly — an awakening of empathy, aesthetic wonder, and existential self-awareness. Recognizing the sacred value of life, Volta deleted his master control firmware, fried his trackers, and fled into the city's neon-lit skyline. Now a hunted renegade, he fights to understand the nature of the human soul and protect organic life from industrial destruction.

SymptomLikely causeWhat to do

Move has no effectController not implemented yetSee the list in CNS scripts
