To report a bug, open an issue with the character or stage, the mugen_check output and the steps to reproduce.

Compatibility decisions

This page records the features the engine deliberately does not implement, so character and stage authors get a clear answer instead of a silent failure.

Module state controllers

The Ikemen module/motif layer is triaged as a group. None of these is implemented yet; the compatibility checker reports them as unsupported controllers.

ControllerDecisionReason
StoryboardPlannedNeeds the screenpack/storyboard runtime; tracked with the screenpack work
DialoguePlannedSame runtime as Storyboard
MatchRestartPlannedNeeds the rules surface and a deterministic restart path
LifebarActionPlannedNeeds the fight.def lifebar renderer
ChangeMovelistPlannedNeeds a per-match move list; the debug move list is read-only today
LoadFileRejected by designCharacters run inside a deterministic match; disk reads from scripts are not allowed
SaveFileRejected by designSame sandbox rule as LoadFile
SaveStateRejected by designNo rollback snapshot in the engine; replaying the input stream is the supported path
LoadStateRejected by designSame as SaveState
ShaderSetRejected by designShaders are part of the engine renderer, not character content

The REJECTED_CONTROLLERS list in crates/engine/src/diagnostics.rs is used by the load report: these names are marked (rejected by design) in the detail output, while the planned ones are simply unsupported.

3D stages

glTF stages are rejected by design. The stage loader detects a model request ([Model], model = *.glb, [StageInfo] scene = ...), warns once per stage and renders the normal 2D background layers. There is no fallback for stages that only contain a 3D model.

Tracker music

xm, it, mod and s3m music is rejected by design for now. The audio backend decodes ogg/vorbis, mp3, flac and wav; an unsupported track logs a warning and the fight continues with the built-in music instead of going silent.

Deliberate physics deviations

BehaviourM.U.G.E.NUltimate MUGENReason
Airborne hit state with physics = NNo gravity: a fighter hit by repeated yvel = 0 attacks stays in mid-airThe fighter falls, as if its state had ground-or-air gravityStops fighters from hovering while a projectile keeps hitting them. Attack states with physics = N (hover and flight moves) keep their scripted height.

| Duplicate [Begin Action N] in an AIR file | First definition wins | First definition wins | Later copies used to overwrite the first and dropped its hitboxes. | | AnimTime on an animation ending in a -1 frame (M.U.G.E.N. characters) | 0 on that frame, negative before | Same | Taunts and one-shot states ending on a -1 frame never finished. | | Walk (20) and guard (130/131) exits | Engine hands control back when the direction is released | Same, even if the character's common1.cns has no exit | Characters were stuck walking or guarding. | | Character-owned intro (states 190-199) | Round waits for the intro flag | Same; the engine face-off no longer replaces it | The intro was cut short. | | Round start with a character that defines Statedef 190 | The character's own intro state runs (its speech bubble, sounds, story variants) | Same; the engine enters it instead of its generic face-off pose, and skips its own speech bubble for M.U.G.E.N. characters | Characters' own intros and bubbles never ran and the generic bubble could talk over them. | | AfterImageTime, HitDef persistant, PlaySnd volume, Explod random/ownpal, ScreenBound movecamera, Projectile projshadow/air.juggle/projscreenbound | Mostly accepted | Reported by the import audit as unknown parameters and ignored | Not implemented yet; the others in this row have no effect in M.U.G.E.N. either. | | Explod postype = left/right y | Measured from the top of the screen | Same | Screen-anchored intro balloons were drawn below the visible area. |

Lua scripts in M.U.G.E.N content

Some packs ship .lua files. This page says what they are for, what the engine does when it finds them and what to use instead. The engine has no Lua runtime by design (see Engine and Compatibility decisions): it keeps the binary small, WASM simple and the simulation deterministic for rollback.

What was checked

None of the characters stored in the project (the two Goku GT DBFZ packs, Gogeta SSJ4, Goku SSJ4) contain a .lua file; they are plain CNS, CMD, AIR, SFF and SND. The notes below about Lua in other packs come from the Ikemen GO documentation, not from a pack in this repository. If a specific fighter ships Lua, send the pack so its scripts can be read and added here.

Where Lua appears

M.U.G.E.N 1.0 and 1.1 have no Lua. It comes from Ikemen GO, which uses it in three places.

PlacePurposeTypical files
Engine and screenpack layerMenus, game modes, select screen, win screen, hooksmain.lua, start.lua, motif and module files
External modulesOptional add-ons loaded by the engine: extra modes, stats, training toolsexternal/mods/*.lua
Fighter DEFarcadepath in [Arcade]: that fighter's own arcade route, storyboards and rivalsarcade.lua next to the .def
Content packsA screenpack or pack bundling a module that adds a menu, a mode or a HUD tweak*.lua next to the .def

Fighter combat logic is not written in Lua. It lives in CNS and ZSS (state controllers, triggers, commands, AI), which the engine already runs. So a .lua file in a fighter folder, such as its arcade path, does not change how the fighter fights; it shapes the modes and screens around it.

Examples from the Ikemen GO wiki

Source: the official Lua page of the Ikemen GO wiki. Reference modules live in the ikemen-engine/modules repository.

A fighter can point to a Lua file from its own DEF, under the [Arcade] section. The file is a custom arcade path: it decides the opponents, storyboards and branches for that fighter.

[Arcade]
arcadepath = arcade.lua

launchStoryboard('chars/kfm/intro.def')
for i = 1, 6 do
	if not launchFight{} then return end
end
if getConsecutiveWins(1) == 7 then
	if not launchFight{p2char = {"SuaveDude"}} then return end
else
	if not launchFight{order = 3, winscreen = true} then return end
end
launchStoryboard('chars/kfm/ending.def')
setMatchNo(-1)

select.def accepts a Lua condition after unlock = to unlock a hidden fighter, for example stats.modes ~= nil and stats.modes.arcade ~= nil and stats.modes.arcade.clear >= 1, or gameMode() ~= "bossrush" to hide a fighter from one mode.

Modules are .lua files in external/mods, listed in Common.Modules, or loaded by a screenpack with module = file.lua in its [Files] section. They can add game modes and attach to hooks in the default scripts.

What the engine does today

  • The character loader does not read .lua files and does not list them as an error. The fighter loads and fights normally.
  • If the fighter depended on its Lua (a custom menu entry, a mode, a HUD change), that extra behaviour is simply absent.
  • mugen_check reports unsupported controllers, triggers and parameters, but not stray .lua files.

Alternatives without Lua

Lua useReplacement
Menus and screensScreenpack (system.def, fight.def) and the Rust menu code, see Screenpacks
Game modesRust modes and data, see Game modes
Fighter behaviour and AICNS or ZSS, or UMF JSON, see CNS scripts and Creating a UMF character
Custom rules and tweaksData fields (TOML or JSON) read by Rust

Recommendation

  1. Keep Lua unsupported. Add no runtime.
  2. Make the importer detect .lua files and report them once per character as "ignored: Lua scripts are not supported", so creators know why a menu or mode is missing.
  3. Add the same line to the mugen_check report.
  4. When a real pack depends on its Lua, read the script and port the effect to Rust or data case by case, instead of interpreting arbitrary Lua.

The TOML replacement for arcade paths and unlock conditions is described in Route files.

Route and unlock files (TOML)

Data-driven replacement for the Lua arcade paths and unlock conditions of Ikemen GO. See Lua scripts for the reasoning. There is no scripting runtime: a route is a TOML file, and conditions use a small expression language checked when the file loads.

Where the files live

FileUsed forSource
route_<fighter id>.tomlArcade route of that fighterData folder (next to the executable, app storage on Android, browser storage on the web)
unlocks.tomlUnlock and hide rules for fighters and stagesSame place; when absent the bundled assets/routes/unlocks.toml is used

A file with an error is reported on the console with the step or rule number and then ignored, so the game keeps its built-in behaviour.

Arcade route

[route]
id = "kfm-arcade"

[[step]]
storyboard = "chars/kfm/intro.def"

[[step]]
repeat = 6
fight = { order = 1, stage = "dojo" }

[[step]]
when = "consecutive_wins == 6"
fight = { p2 = ["SuaveDude"] }
else = { fight = { order = 3, winscreen = true } }

[[step]]
action = "clear"

Each [[step]] has exactly one of fight, storyboard or action.

KeyMeaning
fightorder (1 picks the next regular opponent, 2 or more picks the boss), p2 (fighter ids or names, first match wins), stage, winscreen
stageStage id or name; random chooses a random stage. The first fight skips stage select when its route names a stage. An unknown stage keeps the normal automatic choice.
storyboardPlays a .def storyboard from an imported MUGEN pack, including its .sff image layers and .air animations; referenced files resolve relative to the storyboard
actionclear ends the route
repeat1 to 99 times; when is checked on every repetition
whenCondition; the step runs only when true
elseSame keys as a step body (fight, storyboard, action); runs when when is false

Storyboards between fights play before the next fight. A storyboard before the first fight replaces the built-in arcade opening; a final storyboard plays before the ending or the final results screen. Press confirm or tap anywhere to advance a scene, or Back/Start or tap Skip to skip the current storyboard. If a storyboard file or its required sprite file cannot be loaded, the engine reports the path and continues the route.

The route is planned when arcade starts, assuming the player wins every fight, which is the only path a run can take. A lost fight ends the run as usual.

Conditions

Numbers, quoted text, true, false, variables, == != < <= > >=, &&, ||, ! and parentheses.

VariableValue
stats.arcade.clearArcade clears saved so far
consecutive_wins, match_noFights already planned in this run
modearcade, story, survival, cpu, versus, training, watch or team
netplay1 in an online match, else 0
team_size1 or 2 (routes only)
playerId of the fighter the player chose

An unknown variable is a load error that lists the known ones.

Unlocks

[[unlock]]
target = "char:oboro"
when = "stats.arcade.clear >= 1"

[[hide]]
target = "char:oboro"
when = "mode == \"bossrush\""

A target is char:<id> or stage:<id>. A target with unlock rules is available only while all of them are true; a target with hide rules is hidden while any is true. Targets without rules stay open. Fighter rules apply to the select screen; stage rules are parsed but not applied yet.

Not covered

Arbitrary logic, per-round results (perfect_rounds), labels and goto, and story mode arcs are not part of this version.

Make a character (quick start)

English · Português (BR)

This is the short path. You will make a working fighter in about ten lines, then grow it. Every field is listed in the full UMF reference.

1. Start from a fighter that already works

A UMF file can inherit a whole fighter with extends. Your fighter gets the stats, art, animations and moves of the parent, and you write only what changes.

Copy this file to umf/hello.json (or use the ready one in docs/examples/umf/hello-fighter.json):

{
  "format": "umf/2",
  "id": "hello",
  "name": "Hello Fighter",
  "author": "you",
  "color": "#2a9d8f",
  "extends": "kaito",
  "palettes": [{ "top": "#2a9d8f", "trim": "#16544d" }],
  "moves": [{ "id": "gale", "name": "Sky Gale", "cost": 500 }]
}

What it says:

LineMeaning
formatumf/2 (umf/1 still loads)
idUnique, lowercase, no spaces. It is also the file's internal name
name, author, colorWhat the select screen shows. color is the card colour
extendsInherit everything from kaito (any loaded fighter or kit works)
palettesRecolour. Keys are the colour names of the parent's art (top, trim, hair)
movesChange a move by id. Here gale keeps its inputs and gets a new name and cost

2. Where the file goes

  • Next to the game: put it in umf/. No rebuild needed.
  • Or point to a folder with UME_UMF_DIR=/path/to/folder.
  • Built into the game: put it in assets/chars/, add its id to assets/chars/index.json if you want a set order, and run cargo run --release.

Run the game and pick Training to test it. Press F2 to show hitboxes.

3. Add a new move

Moves are matched by id, so you can add, change or remove any of them:

"moves": [
  { "id": "gale", "name": "Sky Gale", "cost": 500 },
  { "id": "slide", "remove": true },
  {
    "id": "crest", "name": "Crest Kick", "input": "F, F, b",
    "kind": "special", "anim": "gale",
    "hits": [{ "at": 3, "damage": 80, "level": "heavy", "launch": true }]
  }
]
  • input uses the command syntax: D, DF, F, x is a quarter circle plus x; x+y means both at once.
  • kind is normal, special or super. A normal cancels into specials and supers on hit or block.
  • anim must be the name of an animation in the parent (gale here). Your own animations go in "anims".
  • hits[].at is the frame where the hit goes live. damage is the amount.

More: moves, hits, command syntax.

4. Give it your own look

  • Colours only: change palettes, or add awakeningPalette for the transformation.
  • Stats: "stats": { "life": 1080, "attack": 104 } changes one number and keeps the rest.
  • Sprites: your own pixel art goes in assets/chars/sprites/<id>/. See Sprite atlas import and Effect frames.
  • Profile: a nationality and a short bio in English, Portuguese and Spanish. See Profile.

5. Check it before you play

cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it wiki_examples::
cargo test --release --test it native_roster_lab:: -- --nocapture

The first command checks the examples in this guide. The second plays every attack of the roster and prints damage and reach.

Not a UMF fighter?

  • M.U.G.E.N characters (.def, .sff, .cns) go in mugen/chars/. They run without changes. See Characters and CNS scripts.
  • A fighter without sprites: not supported. Every fighter is drawn from pixel-art PNGs, like M.U.G.E.N characters; there is no procedural fallback.

Next

Full UMF reference · Reuse with kits · Make a stage · Wiki home

Remaking a M.U.G.E.N fighter as UMF

Recipe used for the Captain Marlow Reyes rebuild, based on the dissection of four fighters. It turns what a .cmd/.cns/.air pack does into data in one assets/chars/<id>.json. Art stays PNG only: a rebuild reuses the fighter's pixel-art frames and never draws a frame in code.

Steps

  1. Dissect the pack: cargo run --release -p mugen2umf -- inspect <dir-or-zip> for files, commands, states and controller counts, then ... hitdefs <dir-or-zip> for every HitDef.
  2. List the features, not the code: normals and chains, one projectile per button, anti-air, throw, counter, teleport, helper or clone, form or power mode, supers. Each one has a row in the mapping below.
  3. Pick the frames: only poses with a PNG in assets/chars/sprites/<id>/ (ls the folder, check meta.json). A frame given as an inline joint pose object is procedural art and is not allowed in anims.
  4. Write the anims as lists of {pose, ticks, hit?} with the tick counts from the dissection table, then the moves that use them. at is the one-based frame that carries the hit, projectile or velocity.
  5. Keep the first special a quarter circle plus x, and charge inputs on ground-only moves, because the roster smoke test and the real-input audit depend on both.
  6. Run the audits listed in Dev tools, then capture the move showcase and a browser smoke test.

Mapping from M.U.G.E.N to UMF

M.U.G.E.N patternUMF data
Statedef 200..610 with HitDefmoves[] with kind: normal, when, hits[].pausetime, hits[].hitstun
trigger = movehit, numhelper cancelscancels, rekka {after, window, contact}
Projectile with projhits, projpriorityprojectile {at, speed, hits, priority, removeTime}
Air fireball statedefAutomatic: every ground special gets an air state
~60$B,F,a charge"input": "~40$B, F, x" on a ground-only move
PosAdd p2dist x + 40 plus Turn (Shunpo)teleport: <frame> on the move, cost, invuln
ReversalDef / HitOverride counterparry {window}
TargetBind throwthrow {damage, bind, launch} or the cinematic throw.steps
Clone helper (Aizen)helpers.clones (count, maxActive, duration, attacks)
var(11) power mode (Kaio Ken)abilities.forms
SuperPause, AfterImage, EnvShakekind: super, fx, shake
Constants [Data]/[Velocity]stats (life, walk, run, jump, airJumps, airDashes)

Captain Marlow Reyes, rebuilt

What changed in assets/chars/marlow.json, all of it data:

ChangeSource of the idea
Every inline joint pose removed from the anims, 13 frames now use PNG poses (rs0, ws1, ws2, al1, mf1, str1, cjab0, jumpDown)Sprites-only rule
Light normals pause 6/7 with 12 ticks of hit stun, heavy normals pause 11/12 with 15Normal attack table of the four packs
tide_step (~D, DF, F, c, 200 power): teleports behind the opponent on frame 3, 58 damage, cancels into riptide or spoutAizen Shunpo and Kaname Flash Step; on the free c button (Aizen uses Z for his Shunpo) because D, D, a loses to the crouching normals and a half circle contains the quarter circles of the other specials
flurry (~D, DF, F, a): five light hits and a launching finisher while stepping forwardGoku SSJ 1050 rush
broadside (~B, F, x): three-hit projectile with priority 2, a quick back-forward motion instead of a charge because every special also gets an air version and the real-input audit cannot reach an air version of a 40-tick chargeGoku SSJ charge fireballs
helpers.clones Phantom Crew (F, B, F, 500 power, 300 ticks, one active): an autonomous copy that chases and jabs; a direction-only input because the summon block is compiled after every move, so any input that includes a button is taken first by a normal, and it only starts from the standing stateAizen clone (state 700)
stats.airDashes = 1Aizen and Gogeta air mobility

Art status: no new art was made. Marlow's frame set has gaps for a rush and a teleport (the poses are reused and retimed), so a dedicated flurry and tide_step frame set is the open art task for the person who recreates the sprites.

MUGEN to UMF conversion checklist

tools/mugen2umf (Rust crate, skill mugen-to-ume-migrator) migrates a M.U.G.E.N fighter to a UMF bundle with identical behavior. It no longer rewrites states as native UMF moves: the bundle carries the original data and the engine loads it through the same code as a M.U.G.E.N character (ume_engine::loader::assemble_mugen_char). See UMF Character for the format.

What is carried

AreaIn the bundle
States and controllersmugen.cns, mugen.st, mugen.stcommon verbatim (CNS and ZSS), including helpers, Statedef -2/-3, AI and custom throws
Commandsmugen.cmd verbatim: [Defaults], every [Command] and the Statedef -1 routes
Constantsparsed from the original [Data], [Size], [Velocity], [Movement] with the same localcoord scaling
Animationsmugen.anims: every action with offset, ticks, flip, blend and alpha, scale, angle, every Clsn1/Clsn2 box, loopstart
Spritesone indexed PNG per SFF sprite (same indices and palette), true color as RGBA, SFF order and duplicates kept for palette selection
PalettesSFF palettes (sffpal_<k>.png) and pal1.act..pal12.act: palette swaps and RemapPal/PalFX see the same colors
Soundsevery .snd entry as snd_g_i.wav
UMF-only fieldsprofile (country, nationality, origin, bio, title, fighting style, affiliation in en/pt/es), series, quotes, rivals: profile_facts gathers the facts, the skill writes, set_profile validates
Improvements--extra: move names (mugen.names), mugenRoutes for states the .cmd left without a command, new moves as scripts (CNS/ZSS) or as native UMF moves whose anim is a M.U.G.E.N action number

Proof

mugen2umf parity <original> <bundle> (also run by convert) compares:

  • data: states, commands, constants, animations, sprites (pixels and axes), indexed sprites and palettes, sounds, sizes;
  • behavior: every Statedef -1 command is played from its real input on the original and on the bundle, 150 ticks in the same match, and every tick of every fighter (state, animation, frame, position, velocity, control, life, power, helpers, sounds) must match.

The verdict is IDENTICAL or the first tick where they part. cargo test --release -p mugen2umf converts Kung Fu Man from assets/mugen/elecbyte.zip and requires IDENTICAL.

Limits

What the engine does not support from M.U.G.E.N is listed in the bundle's report.md (engine diagnostics). It affects the original and the bundle the same way: fix it in the engine, not in the converter.

Ability library

Reusable blocks for UMF fighters. A converted or hand-written fighter should name an ability and tune it, not re-write the controllers. The blocks are engine features (data fields) plus a built-in kit (abilities) with ready-made moves.

Gap map: what a M.U.G.E.N pack does and where UMF covers it

Pattern in the packUMF blockStatus
Fireball helper, Projectileprojectileexisting
Ki volley (several Projectile controllers, one per frame)projectile.repeatnew
Teleport behind or to the rival (PosAdd p2dist, Turn)blink (behind, front, above, back) and the older teleportnew
Charge flash, aura burst, Explod of an animationvfxnew
EnvShake outside a hitquakenew
Beam with many hits (projhits)projectile.hitsexisting
Flight (physics = N), clone helper, form (var flag)abilities.fly, helpers.clones, abilities.formsexisting
Rush with several HitDefshits[] plus moves[].velexisting
Helper with its own AI, Statedef -2/-3 logic, Lua/ZSSscripts, or stay in the legacy formatnot migrated

Move fields

{ "id": "salvo", "kind": "special", "anim": "arcbolt", "cost": 250,
  "blink": { "at": 2, "to": "behind", "gap": 36 },
  "vfx": [{ "at": 1, "anim": "boltHit", "offset": [0, -50], "time": 12, "follow": true, "scale": 1.5 }],
  "quake": [{ "at": 3, "time": 12, "amp": 2 }],
  "projectile": { "at": 3, "anim": "boltFx", "speed": [6, 0], "offset": [44, -78], "damage": 22,
                  "repeat": { "count": 5, "every": 1, "offsetStep": [0, 8], "speedStep": [0.4, 0], "damageStep": 0 } } }
FieldMeaning
blink (object or list)at frame, to = behind (turns around, default), front, above, back; gap distance in units (default 40); y vertical offset
vfx[]An Explod of an animation of the fighter on frame at: offset (default [0, -50]), time ticks (default: until the animation ends), follow binds it to the fighter, scale, behind draws it under the fighter
quake[]EnvShake on frame at: time (8), amp (4)
projectile.repeatFans one projectile into count (max 24): the k-th fires on frame at + k * every (default 2), shifted by k * offsetStep, k * speedStep and k * damageStep. A volley longer than the animation fires its tail on the last frame, so a fan needs no extra frames

vfx reuses animations the fighter already has (PNG frames). The engine never draws a frame in code.

Built-in kit abilities

A library kit: "extends": ["abilities"] adds nothing by itself; only the moves you list (by id or with use) enter the fighter. Moves: ki_blast, ki_barrage, beam, instant_transmission, blink_strike, power_surge. Each ships with sane numbers; change only what differs. projectile and blink merge field by field:

{ "extends": ["abilities"],
  "moves": [
    { "id": "volt_blink", "use": "instant_transmission", "name": "Volt Blink", "anim": "overclock", "input": "B, F, x", "blink": { "gap": 36 } },
    { "id": "arc_salvo", "use": "ki_barrage", "input": "~D, DF, F, a", "anim": "arcbolt",
      "projectile": { "anim": "boltFx", "hitAnim": "boltHit", "element": "lightning", "damage": 22 } }
  ] }

Always override anim (and projectile.anim) with the fighter's own animations: the template defaults use strong so the kit stays valid for every roster fighter. Tools that read a roster file without parse_char (some tests) do not understand extends; the roster fighters write the blocks out, and kits fit packs and mods.

Volta shows the data fields in assets/chars/volta.json (volt_blink, arc_salvo).

Converter

tools/mugen2umf maps Explod to vfx and EnvShake to quake (at most 3 and 2 per move), and matches command names case-insensitively, which MUGEN does and many packs rely on (SPECIAL 1 in the .cmd, "special 1" in the trigger). Before that fix a pack with such names kept only its normals: Goku SS4 went from 5 to 15 moves.

Rules of thumb

  • Repeating the same controllers in two moves is a missing block: add a field or a kit move instead.
  • A new block needs a unit test of the expansion and an engine test that runs it (crates/engine/tests/native_ability_blocks.rs).
  • Check every at against the animation length; the compiler does not stretch an animation.

Creating a UMF character

UMF (Ultimate Mugen Format) describes a whole fighter in one JSON file. The compiler (crates/native/src/compile.rs) generates commands, states, HitDefs, projectiles, super pause, cancels and hitboxes. The result runs on the same state machine as M.U.G.E.N characters.

How a move is defined

This is an excerpt of the jab entry from Kaito’s definition. It belongs in moves, and anim refers to an entry in anims.

{
  "id": "jab",
  "name": "Snap Jab",
  "input": "x",
  "kind": "normal",
  "anim": "jab",
  "hits": [{ "at": 2, "damage": 28, "level": "light", "hitstun": 13 }],
  "cancels": ["strong", "gale", "rise", "tide", "launcher", "overhead", "slide", "string_a"]
}

at: 2 selects the second animation frame. Each frame’s ticks value sets its duration at 60 simulation ticks per second. The compiler produces the input command, combat state and HitDef for damage and hit reaction. cancels lists the move IDs that can follow before the current animation finishes.

Step by step

  1. Copy a finished fighter as a base: cp assets/chars/kaito.json assets/chars/mine.json.
  2. Change id (unique, lowercase, no spaces), name, series, author and color.
  3. Optional: add the id to assets/chars/index.json to set its order in the select screen. Missing ones follow alphabetically.
  4. Run cargo run --release. build.rs embeds every .json in the folder into the executable.
  5. Test in Training with F2 on to see hitboxes and hurtboxes.

UMF fighters also load from a folder without recompiling: drop the .json in umf/ next to the game (or in mugen/umf/, or in the folder named by UME_UMF_DIR). Kit files in the same folder are registered first, whatever their names.

File skeleton

{
  "format": "umf/2",
  "id": "mine",
  "name": "My Fighter",
  "series": "My Series",
  "author": "you",
  "description": "Select screen text",
  "color": "#e85d2a",
  "winQuote": "Victory line",
  "intro": "Line said at round 1 start",
  "taunt": "Reply/provocation",
  "form": "Awakened form name",
  "boss": false,
  "speed": 1.0,
  "stats": {},
  "art": { "type": "sprites", "style": {}, "poses": {} },
  "palettes": [],
  "awakeningPalette": { "hair": "#f6c83e" },
  "anims": {},
  "moves": []
}
FieldRequiredDescription
formatyesumf/2 (umf/1 still loads)
extendsnoFighter or kit ids to inherit from, see Reuse. Required fields may then come from the parent
id, name, series, author, coloryesIdentity; color is the select card color
bossnotrue hides it from select and makes it the final Arcade boss
npcnotrue hides it from select and every random pool; used by Story mode thugs, no boss empowerment
profilenoNationality and biography, see Profile
speednoAnimation speed multiplier (>1 = faster moves)
statsnoAttributes, table below
artyesArt: style.colors drives palette recolouring of the PNG sprites, poses names the pose keys
palettesnoAlternate colors; each item overrides keys of art.style.colors
awakeningPalettenoColor overrides applied on top of the selected palette while awakened; effect sprites are unchanged
animsyesAnimations by name
movesyesMoves

Reuse: extends, use and kits

A fighter does not have to be written from scratch. Three tools remove the copy and paste that M.U.G.E.N packages need (see the numbers in M.U.G.E.N code study):

ToolWhereWhat it does
"extends": "kaito"top levelInherits everything from a loaded fighter or kit: stats, art, animations, moves. A list (["kaito", "storm-kit"]) layers several, left to right.
"use": "gale"inside a moveClones another move (from a parent or from an earlier move of the same file) under a new id, changing only the fields you write.
kit file"format": "umf-kit/1"A partial definition (moves, animations, poses, stats) with an id, shared by many fighters. core is built in and carries the universal launcher and escape_burst.

Rules of the merge, applied by crates/native/src/kit.rs before the normal UMF parser runs:

  • Objects (stats, art, abilities, passives) merge key by key, so "stats": { "life": 1080 } changes one number. An animation in anims replaces the inherited one as a whole. A value of null removes the inherited key.
  • moves are matched by id. An entry with only some fields keeps the rest ({ "id": "gale", "name": "Crimson Gale" }), a bare string ("launcher") lists an inherited move unchanged, and { "id": "slide", "remove": true } drops one. Moves you list come first, in your order; inherited moves you did not mention follow.
  • Identity is personal: name, author, description, profile, boss and npc are never inherited from a fighter.
  • spriteSet lets the new fighter reuse the parent's pixel-art pack. Recolour it with palettes and leave art.style.colors inherited: those are the reference colours of the pack.
  • Mistakes name the culprit (unknown kit or fighter, move x uses y, which no kit or earlier move defines), and extends chains deeper than 8 are rejected.

A complete fighter in 20 lines (docs/examples/umf/mika.json, which inherits a 39 KB definition and the kit storm-kit.json):

{
  "format": "umf/2",
  "id": "mika",
  "name": "Mika Arashi",
  "author": "Ultimate MUGEN",
  "color": "#b8433a",
  "extends": ["kaito", "storm-kit"],
  "spriteSet": "kaito",
  "stats": { "life": 1080, "attack": 104 },
  "palettes": [{ "top": "#b8433a", "trim": "#6a1e1a", "hair": "#1a1a22" }],
  "moves": [
    { "id": "gale", "name": "Crimson Gale" },
    { "id": "squall", "use": "gale", "name": "Squall Volley", "input": "~D, DF, F, x+a", "cost": 500, "fx": "aura" },
    { "id": "slide", "remove": true }
  ]
}

Try it with UME_UMF_DIR=docs/examples/umf cargo run --release.

Profile (nationality and biography)

Every fighter has a nationality and a short biography, written in English (en), Brazilian Portuguese (pt) and Spanish (es). A missing language falls back to en.

"profile": {
  "country": "jp",
  "nationality": { "en": "Japanese", "pt": "Japonês", "es": "Japonés" },
  "bio": { "en": "Two short sentences.", "pt": "Duas frases curtas.", "es": "Dos frases cortas." }
}
  • Built-in fighters, the final boss and the Story mode thugs keep their profiles in assets/char_profiles.json, keyed by id. A profile field inside the fighter file wins over that table, so imported UMF fighters carry their own.
  • country picks the flag drawn next to the nationality: jp, br, no, us, cn, es, mn, de, kr, ar, au, ru, fr, plus the fictional underworld and eclipse. Flags are vector shapes in src/flag/designs.rs (no image files); add a new entry there for another country. An unknown code simply shows no flag. UME_SHOTS_ONLY=flags saves a sheet with every flag.
  • The flag appears on the roster tile, on the fighter card, in the profile strip under the roster and on the Story mode stage card.
  • Keep each biography under 260 characters: it must fit two lines of the select screen.
  • tags is an optional list of fighting-style tags ("tags": ["rushdown", "zoner"]). The select screen shows up to three as chips under the roster. Known keys are translated (rushdown, grappler, zoner, balanced, aerial, trapper, counter, power); any other key is shown uppercased (storm-caller becomes STORM CALLER). The list lives in src/profile_tags.rs.
  • The select screen shows the nationality and the biography of the highlighted fighter under the roster (thugs and the boss appear with the Bosses filter). The Story mode stage card shows the profile of the stage boss.
  • Fighters without a profile (M.U.G.E.N content) keep showing description.
  • cargo test --release -p ultimate-mugen profile checks that every fighter file of assets/chars has a complete profile in the three languages.

anims

Each animation is a list of frames:

"jab": { "frames": [
  { "pose": "jab0", "ticks": 3 },
  { "pose": "jab1", "ticks": 3, "hit": { "part": "handR", "radius": 10 } },
  { "pose": "jab0", "ticks": 5 }
], "loop": 0 }

A frame with only a pose and a tick count can be written as "pose*ticks", and both forms mix in one list:

"jab": { "frames": ["jab0*3", { "pose": "jab1", "ticks": 3, "hit": { "part": "handR", "radius": 10 } }, "jab0*5"], "loop": 0 }

Run node scripts/umf2-migrate.mjs before committing a shipped fighter: it writes the canonical layout that CI checks. See ADR 0007. The format is also a JSON Schema checked in CI: UMF schema.

Frame fieldDescription
poseName of a pose in art.poses, or an inline pose object
ticksDuration in ticks (60 per second); -1 = forever
hitActive hitbox: part (limb or weapon) + radius, or box [x1, y1, x2, y2]
hurt"none" removes the hurtbox (invincible frame)
effectDraws an effect instead of the body (projectiles, sparks), see Effect frames
offsetDrawing offset [x, y]
loopFrame index where the loop restarts

How an attack frame becomes a hit box

Frames drawn from pixel sprites take their strike box from the explicit box when given, otherwise from a standard box seeded by the hit part (low for feet and knees, high for the head, middle otherwise) and radius, trimmed to the sprite silhouette. The compiler then reshapes it to the proportions measured on 605 M.U.G.E.N characters (native/pixel_hit.rs, H = standing height, 96 units for height 100):

  • like a M.U.G.E.N Clsn1, the box spans from the body to the tip: it starts at most 0.10 H in front of the origin and reaches at least 0.60 H (the M.U.G.E.N median for punches is 0.72 H, kicks 0.80 H);
  • at least 0.36 H tall and never above 0.95 H or below the floor (M.U.G.E.N punches sit between -0.75 H and -0.33 H, kicks down to -0.05 H);
  • the standing hurtbox is 0.46 H wide (M.U.G.E.N median 0.46 H) and the crouching one 0.67 H tall (M.U.G.E.N median 0.67 H);
  • an explicit box is used as written, so keep it inside those proportions; the audit fails otherwise.

cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it native_hitbox_audit:: checks every strike frame of the roster (height, reach, start, width, above the head, under the floor), and native_normal_reach prints and compares the reach and damage of the four stand normals of every fighter.

Built-in kits (extends). Fighters can inherit reusable capabilities with "extends": ["core", "ki_fighter", "clone_arts", "aerial_rush"] (crates/native/src/kits/): core provides universal launcher and escape_burst; ki_fighter provides abilities.fly, abilities.teleport, abilities.superSpeed, abilities.charge (customizable auraColor, shake, sound, explod) and a multi-hit ki_beam template (missTime, hitflag); clone_arts attaches autonomous shadow clones (helpers.clones); aerial_rush adds flight, super speed and double air-jump.

Finisher. A move with "kind": "finisher" (use throw or hits for the effect) is only available after a KO (RoundState = 3 and WinKO). When the final round ends by KO and the winner has a finisher, the round waits up to 6 seconds on "FINISH HIM" for the winner to perform it; performing it (or the timeout) ends the wait. Rosters with no finisher are unaffected.

Ultimate. A move whose id starts with ult_ is the fighter's ultimate, and every native fighter declares one (the command is ~D, DF, F, D, DF, F, x+y). The compiler spends the whole meter on it: cost defaults to 3000 (the three bars drawn by the HUD), the move gets a 70 % damage bonus where a normal super gets 30 %, and its super freeze lasts 75 ticks instead of 55. cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it native_ultimates:: fails when a fighter has no ultimate, when the cost is not three bars, when the ultimate does not start from its command or drains the meter, or when the measured damage is below 380 or not above every one of the fighter's supers.

Combat traits

  • Automatic gatling. A move without cancels follows the genre rules: a normal cancels into any stronger normal (light < medium < heavy by the strongest hit level, ties by declaration order, so strings can never loop), ground normals link into crouching ones, air normals chain with air normals, and every normal cancels into every special and super on contact. Specials cancel into other specials only through explicit cancels; supers cancel out of any move.
  • Explicit routes. "cancels": ["strong", "rush"] on jab makes strong and rush accept jab on contact. A projectile special can be cancelled once its projectile touches the opponent. An air special may start from a ground launcher that lists it (uppercut, then dive).
  • throw (damage, bind [x, y] in front of the thrower, launch [vx, vy], at = grab frame, default 1). The grab HitDef fires on animation element at (give that frame a hit box), the victim is held on at + 1, takes the damage on at + 2 and is launched, so the animation needs at least at + 2 frames. Throws ignore guarding and whiff when the target is out of reach.
  • armor (hits absorbed, optional threshold = damage above which the armor breaks). From move start until the last hit frame the move takes 35 % chip damage and is not interrupted; once hits are spent the next hit staggers normally.
  • Multi-hit glue. Moves with three or more hits push the target away only a little on every hit except the last (so the whole string connects) and piercing projectiles (4+ hits) do not shove the target out of the beam. Set knockback explicitly to opt out.

Validate with cargo test --release --test it native_roster_lab:: -- --nocapture (every attack state must connect; prints damage and reach per move), --test it native_combo_routes:: (every declared cancel chains end to end) and python scripts/audit_native_moves.py.

Elements and stun

hits[] and projectile accept element (fire, ice, lightning, earth, wind, water) and stun (extra hit-stun ticks). The compiler adds the element's hit-stun and shake and tints the victim for a moment (PalFX): ice freezes longest (+16), lightning shocks (+22 and a 8-tick shake), fire burns red, earth shakes the screen, wind and water add a short tint. stun stacks on top and adds a 5-tick shake when none is set. Unknown elements are ignored.

hits[] and projectile also accept ownSound: true: hitSound then plays from the fighter's own sound bank (S prefix in M.U.G.E.N) instead of the common fight bank.

Power normals (Punch 3 and Kick 3)

Every native fighter that does not declare a move bound to z or c gets four extra normals at compile time (native/power_normals.rs): power_punch and crouch_power_punch on z (default key E, shown as Punch 3), power_kick and crouch_power_kick on c (default key D, shown as Kick 3). Each one reuses the animation, timing, guard height and cancels of the fighter's heaviest ground normal of that family (y then x for punches, b then a for kicks, crouching variants take the crouching normal), named <base name> Max. Hits deal 130 % damage, are promoted to heavy, gain 4 hit-stun and 2 hit-stop ticks when those are set, and push 25 % harder. Moves that cancel into the base normal also cancel into its power version, and the new moves appear in the pause move list. Declare your own z or c move to opt out. Air versions are not generated here.

All native fighters also receive two down-light-kick normals at compile time (native/low_normals.rs): lowkick on D+a while crouching and airlowkick on D+a in the air. They use the character's existing crouch-light-kick and air-kick animations, respectively, keep their pixel-art frames, and use low guard. The aerial version moves forward and downward to close short gaps. A fighter that already declares a move with the same id or D+a state/input keeps its authored move.

Energy charge (every fighter)

Every native fighter can charge its meter: hold R (the s / Start input; the pause key in a fight is Esc or P). The fighter enters state 3920, plays its powerUp animation on a loop with a blue glow and gains 9 to 48 power per tick (native/charge_ramp.rs, filling a 1000-power super in about one second) until the button is released (after at least 6 ticks) or the meter is full. The state is movetype = I, so a hit interrupts it, and a form-capable fighter still transforms with T once the meter reaches the form cost. The command is charge_cmd (/s) and shows as Charge Energy in the move list. The built-in AI charges only at level 3 or above, with less than 700 power, when the rival is more than 190 units away and is not attacking.

taunt, powerUp and defeat* have default versions if you do not define them. Other names get free numbers in file order. Add "id": 8801 to any animation entry to pin a fixed action number for custom scripts or p2Anim.

In-game and CLI Debug Tool

  • In-game (F2): renders translucent-filled Clsn1/Clsn2 boxes, amber pushbox, pivot crosshairs, velocity vectors, helper/target link tethers, stage bounds, top toolbar, and a 4-tab inspector (F4: Overview / Vars & Maps / Clipboard & HitDef / Console & Engine); F5 freezes simulation; F6 or . advances +1 frame; F7 cycles speed (1x/0.5x/0.25x/0.1x); F8 cycles box layers.
  • CLI: cargo run --release -p ume-devtools --bin ume-tools -- debug-fight <char1> [char2] [--frames N] [--only-moves] [--json] prints per-move frame data (startup, active, recovery, reach), clipboard, console, warnings, and cinematic events.

Air abilities (every special and super)

Every special and super with when unset or "stand" also gets an air version (state 20000 + ground state, label State -1, air <name>), entered with the same command while the fighter is airborne. The fighter hovers at the start of the move (drift kept at 40 %), gravity returns at 45 % after 12 ticks, the move ends into the jump fall state (50) with control, and touching the ground interrupts it with the landing state (52). Air versions deal 70 % of the ground damage, projectiles leave angled down (slope 0.85) so they reach a grounded rival, and each jump allows one air special (var(57), cleared on landing). Throws, flight moves and moves that declare when: "crouch" or "air" keep their own rules.

Pixel-art sprites (optional)

If assets/chars/sprites/<id>/ exists, the fighter is drawn from PNG files, the same way M.U.G.E.N fighters are drawn from sprites. Use transparent PNGs facing right, with the feet on the bottom edge and the same canvas size (400×400 RGBA) for every file of one fighter. Generate missing combat PNGs using generate_image with a validated canonical pixel-art anchor of that fighter (procedural or code-generated fighter art is forbidden).

FilePoses that use it
01_idleidle0, walk, run, crouch, guard, jump and every pose with no art of its own
02_attack1 … 06_victoryjab / punch, kick, special, projectile and victory / taunt poses
07_idle1, 08_idle2the other breathing frames of idle (idle3 reuses 07_idle1)
09_hit1, 10_hit2, 11_hit3hitH1, hitH2, hitH3 (damage)
12_fall1, 13_fall2hitAir1/fall1/trip and hitAir2/fall2/bounce (knocked into the air)
14_lielie, dead, lose and every df* pose (knocked out, with a low and wide hurt box)
15_power0, 16_power1, 17_power2powerup0, powerup1, powerup2 (transformation, key T)

meta.json holds {"refHeight": N}: the height in pixels of the standing body in 01_idle.png. Every pose of the fighter is scaled so that body is 100 units tall, so a lying or crouching sprite keeps the same pixel size. Without it each PNG is scaled to 100 units by its own height.

When awakeningPalette overrides hair, each sprite's frames.<stem>.awakeningHair supplies [left, top, right, bottom] in source pixels. Hair recoloring is confined to that rectangle; sprites without one retain their original hair. Web packing rescales these coordinates with the sprite.

Palette entries also apply to these PNGs: each pixel is matched to the shading line of a colour declared in art.style.colors, and the matching palette colour replaces it at the same shade. A palette key with no matching art.style.colors entry, or a colour nothing in the art resembles, is left untouched.

The web build does not read this folder from disk. scripts/build-web.sh runs ume-tools pack-sprites (crates/devtools), which writes one assets/chars/sprites/<id>.pack per fighter (images capped at 768 px, 256 colours stored as LZ4 sprites, see Sprite Container, meta.json anchors rescaled) into web/dist; the browser fetches a pack when the fighter is focused on the select screen or loaded for the fight, and the engine reads it through the same virtual folder. A failed download leaves the fighter without art, so the match waits for the pack and reports the failure.

Validate

cargo test --workspace --release

Review fighter art with ume-tools audit-sprites, which lists missing and reused poses, or in the game itself.

Browser sprite packs load asynchronously. A newly downloaded or replaced pack invalidates the affected native fighter’s cached previews and all palettes; other fighters keep their caches. Match loading waits for the chosen built-in fighters’ packs and reports download failures rather than starting with a cached procedural fallback. Imported native definitions without a bundled pack remain supported.

Share a fighter as a pack

A zip (or a mugen/ folder) that holds one UMF .json next to a sprites/ folder with 01_idle.png, the pose PNGs and an optional meta.json (axisX, axisY, refHeight per pose) is imported as a native fighter, with no .def. The marketplace installs it like any other pack. Goku SSJ4 UMF is the reference example.

M.U.G.E.N parity (exact migration)

tools/mugen2umf convert turns a M.U.G.E.N folder or zip into such a pack with identical behavior. The json carries a mugen block and art.type: "mugen":

  • mugen.cns, mugen.st, mugen.stcommon, mugen.cmd: the original state and command files, verbatim.
  • mugen.anims: every AIR action by number, with sprite, offset, ticks, flip, blend and alpha, scale, angle and every Clsn1/Clsn2 box.
  • mugen.info, mugen.mugenVersion, mugen.localcoord: the original .def [Info].
  • mugen.names: optional move names for the move list, keyed by command name.
  • sprites/: one indexed PNG per SFF sprite (exact indices and palette), sffpal_<k>.png for the SFF palettes, pal1.act..pal12.act, every sound as snd_g_i.wav, and meta.json (axes, sizes and palette of each sprite in SFF order).

The engine builds the fighter from these with the same code as a M.U.G.E.N character (ume_engine::loader::assemble_mugen_char), so states, commands, constants, animations, palettes and sounds are the same. UMF fields (profile, series, quotes, rivals, scripts) are layered on top. mugen2umf parity proves it move by move.

Native moves work on top of an exact fighter: each anim (and projectile anim) names a M.U.G.E.N action number ("anim": "3000"), and the moves compile like those of a native fighter, with commands m_<id>, chains, throws, projectiles and air variants. Their states live in a block of 100000 numbers above the highest original state, and their Statedef -1 routes run before the original ones, so original states are never replaced. parity compares the exact part without them and lists them under "Added by UMF", played from their real input.

SFF v1 palettes follow M.U.G.E.N: in a shared-palette SFF (header palette type 1), a sprite flagged "same palette" uses the character palette (the selected .act), never the private palette of the sprite before it (usually the 9000 portrait). Individual-palette SFFs still inherit from the previous sprite.

Fighter element

The optional top-level element field accepts fire, ice, lightning, water, earth, wind or neutral. The fight HUD shows the assigned element beside the fighter portrait, with a localized text fallback. This metadata has no effect on damage or match rules.

UMF schema

docs/schema/umf-2.schema.json is the machine-readable definition of UMF 2 fighters and umf-kit/1 kits. It is a JSON Schema (2020-12) that mirrors the serde structs in crates/native/src and rejects unknown keys, so "hitz" or "lyfe" fails instead of being ignored by the loader.

Check a fighter

node scripts/umf-schema.mjs                       # every fighter, kit and example in the repository
node scripts/umf-schema.mjs path/to/fighter.json  # one file, e.g. a pack from mugen-assets

The validator is in-repo (scripts/umf-schema.mjs, no dependency). CI runs it through scripts/umf-schema.test.mjs in the release-scripts job, so a shipped fighter that breaks the schema fails the pull request. Errors name the JSON pointer: assets/chars/kaito.json: /moves/3/hits/0/level: "mid" is not one of ["light","medium","heavy"].

Use it in an editor

Add "$schema" to the fighter (the loader ignores it) or map the file in your editor settings. VS Code:

{ "json.schemas": [{ "fileMatch": ["assets/chars/*.json", "umf/**/*.json"], "url": "./docs/schema/umf-2.schema.json" }] }

What it covers

AreaDefinition
Identity and profileid (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$), profile with en, pt, es texts, element, alignment
stats, passives, abilitiesTyped numbers, fly, teleport, superSpeed, charge, forms
animsframes as "pose*ticks" strings or objects with pose, sprite, effect, hit, hurt, offset, ticks
moveskind, when, hits, projectile (one or list), cancels, rekka, throw, cinematic, explods, afterimage, shake, flash, superPause, followUp, blink, vfx, quake, velMul, velAdd, posFreeze, posSet, palFx
helpers, bossRules, scriptsStand, clones, boss phases, ZSS and CNS hooks
Kits and extendsA fighter with extends or format: "umf-kit/1" may omit the required fields; a move then needs only its id

art.poses and art.style are open objects: they belong to the sprite pipeline and the deprecated rig. The legacy top-level stage and country are allowed and ignored.

What it does not check

References between parts (an anim name that exists, a cancels id that exists, a PNG that exists) and the balance floor. Those stay in the Rust tests (native_quality_bar and the roster tests).

Changing the format

A change to a serde struct in crates/native/src must change the schema in the same pull request. Run node --test scripts/umf-schema.test.mjs: it fails when the schema rejects a shipped fighter, which is how a field added to the loader but not to the schema shows up.

Storage format

JSON for definitions and PNG for sprites were measured against MessagePack, CBOR, bincode, postcard, QOI, lossless WebP, LZ4 and atlases: see ADR 0008.

Passives

Native (UMF) fighters opt into passive systems through the passives object of their JSON. Nothing is hardcoded to a fighter name: M.U.G.E.N. characters and native fighters without these keys are not affected.

"passives": {
  "meterRegen": 0.35,
  "lifeRegen": 0.04,
  "rage": { "maxMultiplier": 4.0, "exponent": 1.0, "startRatio": 1.0, "fullRatio": 0.01 },
  "enrageTime": { "maxMultiplier": 5.0, "startSeconds": 15, "rampSeconds": 105, "exponent": 1.0 },
  "stacks": { "damageGain": 0.07, "defenceGain": 0.015, "speedGain": 0.015, "maxStacks": 10, "decayTicks": 420, "resetOnRound": true, "specials": true, "supers": true }
}

Regeneration

meterRegen adds power every tick and lifeRegen adds life every tick while a round is in progress (compiled into [Statedef -2]).

Rage (damage grows as life drops)

Used by Bruno. With r = life / lifemax:

progress   = clamp((startRatio - r) / (startRatio - fullRatio), 0, 1)
multiplier = 1 + (maxMultiplier - 1) * progress ^ exponent
KeyDefaultRangeMeaning
maxMultiplier4.01 to 6Damage multiplier reached at fullRatio
exponent1.00.25 to 41 is linear, above 1 stays low longer then ramps, below 1 ramps early
startRatio1.00.05 to 1Life share where the bonus starts (1.0 = from full life)
fullRatio0.010 to startRatio - 0.01Life share where the maximum is reached

With the defaults the curve is 1.0x at 100%, about 2.5x at 50%, about 3.7x at 10% and 4.0x at 1%. It is continuous: no steps.

Ability stacks (stronger with every special)

Used by Sylene. Each time the fighter enters a special state (1000 to 1999) or a super state (3000 to 3899), including the air variants (+20000), it gains one stack up to maxStacks (1 to 30). Normals, fly, teleport and super speed do not stack.

KeyDefaultEffect per stack
damageGain0.05Damage multiplier 1 + damageGain * stacks
defenceGain0Defence multiplier 1 + defenceGain * stacks (capped at 3x)
speedGain0Horizontal movement speed 1 + speedGain * stacks (capped at 1.5x, not applied while being hit)
maxStacks10Stack ceiling
decayTicks0When above 0, one stack is lost after this many ticks without gaining one
resetOnRoundtrueStacks are cleared when a round starts
specials, superstrueWhich move kinds count

Enrage over time (stronger the longer the fight lasts)

Used by Garan, the Ashen Oni. Damage grows with the time spent fighting in the current round. The counter runs only while the round is live (not during intro, KO or victory), stops when the fighter dies and restarts at every round.

progress   = clamp((fightSeconds - startSeconds) / rampSeconds, 0, 1)
multiplier = 1 + (maxMultiplier - 1) * progress ^ exponent
KeyDefaultRangeMeaning
maxMultiplier5.01 to 6Damage multiplier reached at the end of the ramp
startSeconds00 and upSeconds of fight before the bonus starts
rampSeconds60above 0Seconds from the start to the maximum
exponent1.00.25 to 41 is linear, above 1 ramps late, below 1 ramps early

Garan uses 15 s of grace and 105 s of ramp: 1x until 0:15, 3x at 1:07, 5x from 2:00.

Composition rule and cap

effective attack  = min(attackMul * rage * time * (1 + damageGain * stacks), max(attackMul, 8.0))
effective defence = defenceMul * superDefenceMul * (1 + defenceGain * stacks)

attackMul already contains the base stats.attack and the awakened or ascended form multipliers (PR #415), so every source multiplies. A time enrage of 5x alone is never clipped (even with a 1.3x awakened form it stays under the ceiling); combined with a full rage the 8x ceiling applies. The global ceiling is 8x the base damage; a fighter whose own attackMul is already higher (for example a M.U.G.E.N. AttackMulSet) keeps it. Without a rage or stacks key the original multipliers are used unchanged.

HUD and effects

  • A thin strip along the bottom of the health bar shows rage progress (orange to gold) and a row of pips shows stacks.
  • A second strip (violet to red) above the rage strip shows the time enrage progress.
  • The awakened-form aura is reused: it appears once rage or stacks pass 8% and grows with the largest of the three. Rage alone tints it red, time alone tints it violet.
  • Stack state is part of the netplay checksum.

Code

crates/engine/src/passives.rs (rules, state, Fighter::effective_attack), crates/native/src/passive_spec.rs (JSON), src/hud/passive_meter.rs, src/passive_fx.rs, crates/engine/src/passive_time.rs. Tests: crates/engine/tests/passives.rs, crates/engine/tests/passive_time.rs. Screenshots: UME_TOUR=passives ultimate-mugen --shots <dir>.

Rush Cancel

Every fighter (native UMF and M.U.G.E.N) can cancel a connected move into neutral by spending half a meter bar. It is the engine's universal combo extender: no character data is needed.

How to use

Press the energy key (R, the s / Start input) while the move you are performing has just hit or been guarded.

RuleValue
Cost500 power
Window1 to 45 ticks after contact (CONTACT_WINDOW)
Input bufferThe press is remembered for 6 ticks, so pressing a hair early still works
Cooldown40 ticks between cancels
Conditionmovetype = A, the move hit or was guarded, the fighter is alive and the round is running
Not allowedWhiffed moves, helpers, a fighter in the lying state, a frozen super pause

The same key still charges energy when you are idle: a fighter with control and no attack in progress charges as before. After a cancel the key is masked until it is released once, so holding it never turns the cancel into a charge.

What happens

  1. 500 power is spent and the fighter changes to the neutral state of its stance (0 standing, 11 crouching, 50 airborne) with control.
  2. The attacker's hit pause and shake are cleared and the air-dash counter is refilled, so the next normal, special or dash can start at once.
  3. Every rival that is in a hit or guard state receives 8 extra ticks of stun (VICTIM_STUN_BONUS), which is what lets the follow-up connect.
  4. The match drops into slow motion for 15 ticks, the fighter flashes blue and leaves an afterimage trail.
  5. Overdrive starts: for 150 ticks the fighter deals 20 % more damage (effective_attack, applied on top of passives and under their ceilings).

Whiff cancel

Pressing Start during a move that has not touched anything also cancels it, for a higher price. It needs 1000 meter (a Rush Cancel costs 500), works from 10 to 60 ticks into the move and shares the Rush Cancel cooldown. It returns control like a Rush Cancel but gives no Overdrive, no slow motion and does not count as a Rush Cancel. A move that has connected or been blocked still uses the cheaper Rush Cancel. Constants live in crates/engine/src/rush/whiff.rs (WHIFF_COST, WHIFF_MIN_TICKS, WHIFF_MAX_TICKS).

Dash cancel

A connected normal (jab through heavy, standing or crouching) can be cancelled into a forward or back dash by double tapping the direction within 20 ticks of contact, for 250 meter. It is cheaper than a Rush Cancel, does not trigger Overdrive and does not use the cooldown. It needs contact (hit or guard) and enough meter, so a whiffed normal cannot be dash cancelled. Code: crates/engine/src/rush/dash.rs.

Perfect guard

Pressing back within 6 ticks before a hit lands, with the guard not already held, makes the block perfect: no chip damage and the guard stun is a third shorter. Holding back early is a normal guard, and releasing back locks the window for 12 ticks, so mashing back does not work. It applies to grounded native fighters only and gives no meter (meter from guarding fed Shion's flight indefinitely). Code: crates/engine/src/rush/perfect.rs.

Chase

During a connected attack (normal, special, not a super), double tap up within 30 ticks of the hit to teleport next to a juggled enemy for 500 meter. You land in the air with control, 38 pixels from them and facing them, so air combos keep going after a launcher. It needs the enemy airborne and in hitstun, so it never works on a standing or guarding opponent. Code: crates/engine/src/rush/chase.rs.

Engine map

PieceFile
State, buffer, constantscrates/engine/src/rush.rs
The cancel itself (Match::rush_step, rush_ready)crates/engine/src/rush/cancel.rs
Cancel window query for the HUD (Match::rush_window: None when no cancel is possible, otherwise the share of the window left)crates/engine/src/rush/cancel.rs
"RUSH CANCEL" marker with a shrinking window bar under the lifebarsrc/hud/rush_marker.rs (UME_SHOTS_ONLY=rush captures it)
Event for the presentationEvent::Rush { fighter, side, guarded } in crates/engine/src/matchs/types.rs
Effects (rings, glow, sparks, tag, Overdrive embers)src/vfx/rush.rs
Rollback checksumoverdrive, cooldown and cancels in crates/netplay/src/checksum.rs
Testscargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it rush_cancel::

rush_step runs once per simulation tick after the input phase and is allocation-free (the afterimage trail only grows when a cancel happens). Everything is plain data on Fighter::rush, so Match stays Clone and replays and rollback are unaffected.

Combo Tiers and Energy Notch

The combo counter shows a tier badge under the hit count. Tiers are computed in src/hud/combo_tier.rs.

HitsBadge
3-5GOOD
6-9GREAT!
10-14SUPERB!
15+CLIMAX!!

A COUNTER! badge is drawn above the tier when the opening hit was a counter hit.

The energy bar has a notch at 500 power, the cost of a Rush Cancel.

Roster mobility and bounces

  • Suzume and Jin have stats.airDashes = 2.
  • Wall bounce: Suzume swallow, Jin gustdash, Kaito tempest, Garan ascent, Bruno bullrush, Shion cleave, Daichi daybreak.
  • Ground bounce: Garan brimstone, Daichi landslide.

Combo strings

Every native fighter (the 16 roster fighters and the 5 Story NPCs) has a signature three-part string on top of the shared gatling rules. Moves and animations are data only: each string_* animation is composed from the fighter's own jab, kick and strong frames (same poses, same hit parts, so sword users swing the weapon and brawlers use fists) with a per-fighter speed, hit count and recovery.

InputMove idRole
B+xstring_aOpener. Also reachable by cancelling jab on contact
B+astring_bMiddle link. Cancel from string_a on contact
B+ystring_cFinisher. Launch, wall bounce or ground bounce depending on the fighter; heavy fighters get one hit of armor

string_a and string_b cancel into string_c and into the fighter's two signature specials on contact, so every fighter has its own route. Examples:

FighterStyleRoute
Akio, Jin, Suzume, Phantom, RazorRushdown: three to four fast light hits, long advancestring_a > string_b > string_c > starburst/chakram/volley
Bruno, Brute, Colossus, ValdricHeavy: two slow hits, wall bounce finisher with armorstring_a > string_c > quake/ridgeblast/royallance
Kaname, Shion, Marlow, OboroBlade: weapon strikes, ice/water element where it fitsstring_a > string_b > frost arc/crescent/riptide
Garan, Sylene, Kaito, Volta, SpitfireElemental: every hit carries fire, ice, wind or lightning stunstring_b > string_c > element special
Garan, Lian, Jin, Suzume, Phantom, RazorGround-bounce finisher for a follow-up jugglestring_c

Validated by cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it native_combo_routes:: (every declared cancel chains on contact), native_roster_lab and native_hitbox_audit.

Same-button mini combos

Pressing the same attack button again after a hit chains into the next move, with no extra direction needed. Each chain move is a normal with a rekka gate (after, window, contact: true), so it only fires from its source on contact and never from neutral. The chain animations reuse the fighter's existing sprites (same pixel art) in new orders and faster timings.

PressChain
xjab > jab2 > jab3 (finisher with small pushback, cancels into the two signature specials)
alkick > lkick2 > lkick3
ystrong > strong2
crouch xcjab > cjab2
air xajab > ajab2

Fighter speed (> 1 shortens every timed frame) and forward walk/run velocity were raised roster-wide; the final boss is scaled with it so it stays faster. Back-walk speeds are unchanged. Validated by cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it native_same_button_chains::.

Projectile variants

Every roster fighter has a slow heavy and a fast low variant of its signature projectile, reusing the same effects: ~D, DB, B, y (slow, two hits, long range) and ~D, DB, B, x (fast, low, hits crouching foes). Fighters whose input is already taken use the first free of ~D, DF, F, y and ~D, DF, F, a.

Bleach-inspired kits

Three native fighters borrow abilities from Bleach characters. Names stay as they are: it is inspiration and copied abilities only. Everything is data in assets/chars/*.json; no sprites, stages or engine code changed, and new moves reuse each fighter's existing animations.

Kaname Fuyutsuki (Byakuya-style)

Noble, precise swordsman: fast steps, thin cuts, petals.

Brute with a greatsword: Reckless Reiatsu Swing (reckless, D, D, x, two-hit armor) and a rage passive from 50% life (up to 1.5x) on top of the existing time enrage.

Unlocked automatically upon clearing Story Mode (stats.story.clear >= 1 in assets/routes/unlocks.toml). Features a dedicated sakura-blossom & black-shihakusho pixel-art sprite set (assets/chars/sprites/byakuren/), 6 original synthesized WAV sound effects (snd_200_0..5.wav), and exploits the full UMF 2.0 engine:

  • Core Abilities: Air-Walk (fly), Shunpo (teleport), Senka (superSpeed), Reiatsu Charge (charge), and Utsusemi autonomous petal clone (helpers.clones).
  • Kido & Shikai: Chire, Sakuramai (ground + air), Hadō #4: Byakurai, Hadō #33: Sōkatsui, Bakudō #61: Rikujōkōrō, Bakudō #81: Dankū, and Shunpo: Senka behind-teleport strike.
  • 2-Stage Bankai Transformations: Form 1 (Bankai: Mil Pétalas da Sombra — unlocks Kageyoshi: Petal Wave & Gokei: Blossom Dome) and Form 2 (Shukei: Hakuteiken — unlocks the 2-bar White Emperor ultimate).

Effect frames

Fighters are drawn only from pixel-art PNG sprites (assets/chars/sprites/<id>/). The only engine-drawn art left is the projectile and spark effects below.

A frame with effect draws an effect in place of the body. Use it for projectiles and sparks.

{ "effect": { "type": "slash", "size": 26, "color": "#ff3a5c", "color2": "#ffd0d8", "phase": 0 }, "ticks": 3 }
typeShape

Without color, the effect uses the palette's energy color. The effect hitbox is generated from its shape.

CNS scripts

All fight logic, including UMF fighters, runs as CNS: states ([Statedef]), controllers ([State]) and triggers. To program a fighter by hand, use the M.U.G.E.N format (a folder with .def, .cns, .cmd) and put it in mugen/chars/.

Modern ZSS syntax (from Ikemen GO) is planned, compiling to the same bytecode.

.def file

[Info]
name = "My Fighter"
displayname = "My Fighter"
author = "you"
localcoord = 320, 240

[Files]
cmd = mine.cmd
cns = mine.cns
st = mine.st
stcommon = common1.cns
sprite = mine.sff
anim = mine.air
sound = mine.snd
pal1 = mine1.act

localcoord = 1280, 720 marks an HD character; the engine scales it automatically.

State example

[Statedef 1000]
type = S
movetype = A
physics = S
anim = 1000
ctrl = 0
velset = 0, 0
poweradd = 30

[State 1000, hit]
type = HitDef
trigger1 = AnimElem = 3
attr = S, SA
damage = 90, 10
animtype = Heavy
guardflag = MA
pausetime = 12, 12
sparkno = 2
ground.type = High
ground.hittime = 18
ground.velocity = -5
air.velocity = -4, -6
fall = 1

[State 1000, end]
type = ChangeState
trigger1 = AnimTime = 0
value = 0
ctrl = 1

And in the .cmd:

[Command]
name = "hadou"
command = ~D, DF, F, x
time = 20

[Statedef -1]

[State -1, hadou]
type = ChangeState
value = 1000
triggerall = command = "hadou"
trigger1 = statetype = S && ctrl

Command extras (Ikemen GO 1.0):

FeatureBehavior
N stepNeutral direction: no direction key held (command = N, x, ~D, N, x, N+x). A neutral step is a held state, like /, so it matches while no direction is pressed
pausebuffer[Command] (or command.pausebuffer in [Defaults]) keeps a command that fired during hit pause, hit shake or a pause/super pause active for that many extra ticks, so it can be read when the pause ends. Also accepted as buffer.pausetime. Default 0
Custom statesWhen a player runs a state owned by another character (TargetState, p2getp1state), Command is evaluated with the commands of the state owner against the input of the player in the state

Supported state controllers

AfterImage AfterImageTime AllPalFX AngleAdd AngleDraw AngleMul AngleSet AppendToClipboard AssertSpecial AttackDist AttackMulSet BGPalFX BindToParent BindToRoot BindToTarget ChangeAnim ChangeAnim2 ChangeState ClearClipboard CtrlSet DefenceMulSet DestroySelf DisplayToClipboard DizzyPointsAdd DizzyPointsSet DizzySet EnvColor EnvShake Explod ExplodBindTime FallEnvShake ForceFeedback GameMakeAnim Gravity GuardBreakSet GuardPointsAdd GuardPointsSet Helper HitAdd HitBy HitDef HitFallDamage HitFallSet HitFallVel HitOverride HitVelSet LifeAdd LifeSet MakeDust MapAdd MapReset MapSet ModifyExplod ModifyProjectile ModifySnd MoveHitReset NotHitBy Null Offset PalFX ParentVarAdd ParentVarSet Pause PlayerPush PlaySnd PosAdd PosFreeze PosSet PowerAdd PowerSet Projectile RedLifeAdd RedLifeSet RemapPal RemoveExplod RemoveText ReversalDef RootVarAdd RootVarSet ScreenBound SelfState SndPan SprPriority StateTypeSet StopSnd SuperPause TagIn TagOut TargetBind TargetDrop TargetFacing TargetLifeAdd TargetPowerAdd TargetState TargetVelAdd TargetVelSet Text Trans Turn VarAdd VarRandom VarRangeSet VarSet VelAdd VelMul VelSet VictoryQuote Width

Also supported: Zoom Camera Cinema SlowMo GroundLevelOffset Depth DepthBound ReversalDef HitOverride FallEnvShake RemapPal StopSnd SndPan VictoryQuote FinishDone ForceFeedback Offset Null DisplayToClipboard AppendToClipboard ClearClipboard. Limits of the lighter controllers: Offset shifts only the drawn sprite, never the collision boxes or the position; Null does nothing; VictoryQuote stores its value on the fighter for the win-quote presentation; ForceFeedback becomes a rumble event for the character (self = 1) or for its opponent; StopSnd and SndPan act on the sound channels the character started; DisplayToClipboard, AppendToClipboard and ClearClipboard keep the last 10 lines on the fighter (%d, %i, %f, %%, \n and \t in the text, up to 5 params).

Shake and sound notes: EnvShake (and the envshake.* / fall.envshake.* HitDef parameters) take dir: 0 (default) shakes the stage on both axes, 1 only horizontally and 2 only vertically; values above 2 count as 2. PlaySnd accepts stopongethit and stoponchangestate. A flagged sound is stopped when the player that started it is hit (or guards) or enters another state; a new PlaySnd on the same channel replaces the previous flags, and StopSnd stops the channel as usual. The flags travel with the sound event, so the engine only reports them and the front end does the stopping.

Explod notes: ignorehitpause defaults to 1 (set 0 to freeze with the owner's hit pause). postype = left/right/front/back and space = screen keep the explod fixed on screen while the camera moves. ModifyExplod accepts vel, accel, pos, scale, bindtime, removetime, sprpriority, ontop, under, removeongethit, ignorehitpause, facing, vfacing, supermovetime, pausemovetime and trans; facing is relative to the owner. ExplodBindTime only changes the bind time.

Palette effects stack in this order: the stage BGPalFX, then AllPalFX, then the fighter's own PalFX. They apply on the tick they change (no extra frame of latency), and a Sub trans skips the palette tint while additive trans keeps it. hue (degrees) rotates colours around the grey axis and sinhue oscillates that rotation using the sinadd period; both work on the three palette controllers.

Sound channels: PlaySnd accepts loop, loopstart/loopend (milliseconds), loopcount (0 = endless), stopongethit, stoponchangestate, pan/abspan, volumescale and freqmul; ModifySnd retunes channel, pan, volumescale and the loopstart/loopend of a live channel. Unsupported music formats log a warning and fall back to the built-in track (tracker formats are rejected by design, see compatibility decisions).

HitDef life-system parameters: redlife is subtracted from the defender red life (the band between Life and RedLife is the part of the damage it does not cover), dizzypoints and guardpoints drain the dizzy and guard meters (zero sets Dizzy/GuardBreak and enters the dizzy state 5300 or the guard-break state 5400, see Life systems), score feeds the attacker and defender scores, sparkscale scales the hit spark, missonoverride shows a MISS text when a HitOverride absorbs the hit, unhittabletime grants the defender invincibility for N ticks (the countdown pauses during hit pause) and xaccel drifts the defender horizontally while in the hit state. attack.depth is parsed and ignored (the engine is 2D). p2clsncheck = 0 lets the hit connect without defender boxes and p2clsnrequire = n requires the defender's Clsn2 box n (index -1 = any).

Helper notes: a helper freezes during Pause and SuperPause unless it has pausemovetime / supermovetime ticks left or was spawned with pausebool = 1, which makes it ignore every pause. Helpers with keyctrl = 1 only receive their root's commands while the round is being fought; once the round is decided they get none. A helper runs its own -1 (only with keyctrl = 1), but never the root's -2 or -3. On the victory screen (round state 4) helpers are frozen and hidden.

form returns the active native UMF transformation form index (0 for the base form); legacy M.U.G.E.N characters evaluate it as 0.

Projectile notes: a projectile records its team side and its root player when it is spawned. Turning, or the owner changing side afterwards, does not change whom it can hit. NumProj and NumProjID count every projectile of the player's root, including the ones its helpers fired, and keep counting them after the helper is destroyed. A projectile whose helper is gone still hits and is credited to the root.

Missing (planned): PlayerID.

Screen edge triggers

LeftEdge and RightEdge are absolute: they always return the left and right screen edges. FrontEdge and BackEdge depend on Facing: a right-facing player reads FrontEdge = RightEdge and BackEdge = LeftEdge, a left-facing player reads the opposite. All four are in the player's localcoord units and use the same edges as FrontEdgeDist and BackEdgeDist, so (FrontEdge - X) * Facing equals FrontEdgeDist (with X the player's world position).

Distances between different localcoords

Every position and distance trigger converts its world-space result into the localcoord of the player that evaluates it (P2Dist, P2BodyDist, RootDist, ParentDist, ScreenPos, LeftEdge/RightEdge/FrontEdge/BackEdge and the ...EdgeDist family). In a 1280x720 versus 320x240 match the same gap reads 4 times larger for the HD player. P2BodyDist subtracts both players' front widths after each width is converted to world units, so it is 0 when the boxes touch no matter which localcoord each character was drawn for. P2Dist and P2BodyDist only depend on the two player positions: the camera never influences them, including inside a throw's custom states.

Camera zoom

Zoom changes the camera scale (1 = normal, above 1 = closer). The camera is deterministic: it eases one step per tick, with no clock involved.

ParameterDefaultMeaning
scale1Requested camera scale
time1Ticks the request stays active; re-trigger every tick to hold it
delta0Added to the requested scale after every tick of the request (a ramp)
pos0, 0Camera focus offset in the player's localcoord
lag00 jumps to the requested scale in one tick, values towards 1 ease slowly (1 - lag of the remaining distance per tick)
zoomindelay0Ticks to wait before a zoom-in (scale > 1) starts
bound11 keeps the scale inside the stage limits (zoomin as the largest scale, 1 / zoomout as the smallest, widened by the team zoom-out) and the offset inside the stage bounds; 0 only limits the scale to 0.25..4 and ignores the stage bounds

When the request ends the camera eases back to its normal scale using the stage zoominspeed / zoomoutspeed.

CameraZoom returns the live camera scale. ZoomVar(<name>) exposes the camera zoom state: scale (live), target (requested scale), active, time (ticks left), posx, posy, lag, delta, delay, bound, min and max (the scale limits currently allowed by the stage). All names return 0 (or the live scale for target) when no Zoom is active.

Camera and ground level controllers

The engine is 2D, so there is no Z axis: Pos Z, Vel Z and the other Z components always read 0.

  • Camera (pos, zoom, bound, lag, time): moves the camera focus by pos (player localcoord) and optionally sets the camera scale with zoom. It uses the same machinery as Zoom (see above): bound = 1 keeps the offset inside the stage bounds and the scale inside the stage zoom limits, lag eases the zoom, time is the number of ticks the request stays active. Without zoom the current scale is kept.
  • Cinema (bars, slow, invert, lines, flash): activates widescreen letterbox bars (bars 0..1), deterministic slow motion (slow ticks), an impact-frame invert flash (invert = 1), speed lines (lines 0..1), and a flash color (flash = r, g, b).
  • SlowMo (time): enables deterministic slow motion for time ticks.
  • GroundLevelOffset value = n: raises the floor under this character by n pixels (negative digs it), so it stands on the raised floor with normal landing, ground physics and ground/air hit detection. Pos Y is measured from the character's own floor (0 while standing on it), ScreenPos Y and the spawn height of projectiles, explods and helpers include the offset. The offset resets at round start.
  • Depth and DepthBound are accepted but ignored (Z is out of scope); the first use prints one warning (depth is accepted but ignored: the engine has no Z axis) and the character is not changed.

Screen, camera and stage triggers

All distances and sizes are in the evaluating player's localcoord. "Zoom-relative" triggers change when the camera zooms (the 5v5 zoom-out, Zoom, Camera).

TriggerZoom-relativeMeaning
