Redirections

parent root helper target partner enemy enemynear playerid p2 stateowner nearestfoe

helper(id) and target(id) take an optional ID; partner(n) is the n-th other non-helper player on the same side (default 0; a helper redirects through its root; NaN when there is none); enemy(n) and enemynear(n) pick the n-th opponent. Example: trigger1 = enemynear, life < 200. nearestfoe (engine extension) picks the living, non-standby opponent closest in 2D (x and y), which matters in team fights; it falls back to enemy(0) when nobody is alive. Homing example: x = (NearestFoe,Pos X - Pos X) * Facing.

Expressions

  • Integer vs float like M.U.G.E.N: 7 / 2 = 3, 7.0 / 2 = 3.5.
  • Ranges: stateno = [200, 299], (200, 299].
  • Operators: + - * / % ** ! && || ^^ & | ^ ~ = != < <= > >= and := in var(n) := value.

Pause and freeze rules

EntityHit pause (attacker) / hit shake (defender)PauseSuperPause
Fighter or helperAnimation, Time, physics and timers stop; only controllers with ignorehitpause = 1 runFrozen, except the pauser during movetime and helpers with pausemovetime ticks leftFrozen, except the pauser during movetime and helpers with supermovetime ticks left
ExplodKeeps going with ignorehitpause = 1 (default); with 0 it stops while its owner is in hit pause or hit shake, position binding includedFrozen unless pausemovetime ticks are leftFrozen unless supermovetime ticks are left
ProjectileNot affected by the owner's hit pauseFrozen unless pausemovetime ticks are leftFrozen unless supermovetime ticks are left
  • A pausemovetime/supermovetime budget is spent one tick per frozen frame and only by its own kind of pause.
  • AnimTime, AnimElemTime, AnimElemNo and Time hold their value for the whole hit pause or shake and resume on the first free tick.
  • HitPauseTime is the attacker's remaining hit pause; GetHitVar(hitshaketime) and HitShakeOver describe the defender's shake. Every other GetHitVar field is a snapshot taken when the hit lands and does not change during the shake; the recovery clock (HitOver) also waits for the shake to end.
  • Regression tests: crates/engine/tests/freeze_rules.rs.

Debugging

  • F2 in training shows hitboxes.
  • cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example mugen_check -- <folder> lists states and expressions with errors.

Load diagnostics

Every character load audits the controllers, triggers and parameters it parsed against what the engine actually implements. Nothing is hardcoded in a list: each unknown name is run once against a throw-away match and flagged when the dispatch falls through, so the report follows the engine as controllers and triggers are added.

The audit reports, per source file and state (.cns, .cmd, .st, .zss):

FindingMeaning
unsupported controllerthe type has no implementation
unknown triggerthe trigger name is not evaluated by the engine
unsupported redirection / string triggera redirection kind (partner, ...) or a string comparison (p3name = ...) the engine does not resolve
unknown parameterno code path of the controller reads that parameter
unknown AssertSpecial flagthe flag is not recognised

Each load prints one summary on stderr (n unsupported controllers, m unknown triggers, ...), deduplicated by name; TRACE=1 adds the names with the files and states that use them. Set UME_QUIET_DIAGNOSTICS=1 to silence it.

mugen_check prints the summary per character and, with --strict, prints the details and exits with a non-zero status when any character has findings:

cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example mugen_check -- --strict mugen/chars/kfm

CI runs it with --strict over crates/engine/tests/data/chars, so a feature used by the fixture characters that the engine does not implement fails the build. In code, ume_engine::diagnostics::audit_cns(file, text) returns the findings for a snippet and CharDef::diagnostics() for a loaded character.

Introspection triggers

Triggers that read back what a character created or what it is drawing. The last argument is a variable name written bare, like Ikemen GO; an axis is a second word (pos x). A lookup that finds nothing (no such explod, projectile or box) is undefined (NaN): any comparison with it stays undefined and counts as false, so test for existence with NumExplod, NumProj or HelperIndexExist first when the difference matters. Positions and velocities are in the character's own coordinates, positions follow the Pos convention (x relative to the camera, y relative to the floor).

TriggerVariables
ExplodVar(id, index, var)id time removetime bindtime bindid anim animelem animelemtime animtime animplayerno spriteplayerno facing ignorehitpause layerno pausemovetime supermovetime sprpriority pos x/y/z vel x/y/z accel x/y/z scale x/y. Reads the index-th explod of the caller with that id (id below 0 matches any)
ProjVar(id, index, var)projid time projremovetime projhits projmisstime projpriority projsprpriority projedgebound projstagebound lowbound highbound projhitanim projremanim projcancelanim projremove anim animelem facing teamside pausemovetime supermovetime pos x/y/z vel x/y/z accel x/y/z velmul x/y remvelocity x/y/z scale x/y. Reads the index-th live projectile of the caller with that id
PalFXVar(var)time (ticks left) add.r/g/b mul.r/g/b color invertall; prefix bg. or all. for the background and global effects. No effect active reads as the identity (add 0, mul 256, color 256)
ClsnVar(type, index, edge)type is clsn1, clsn2, size or dummy; edge is back, front, top or bottom, relative to the character and its facing. size is the body size box from size.ground.back/front and size.height; dummy has no boxes
ClsnOverlap(type, playerid, type)now accepts size (both sides) and dummy (first side, never overlaps) besides clsn1 and clsn2
ProjClsnOverlap(index, playerid, type)the attack box of the caller's index-th projectile against a box of that player
HelperVar(var)for a helper: id helpertype keyctrl ownpal preserve; undefined for a non-helper

AnimElemVar(var)the current animation element: group image time hflip vflip xoffset yoffset xscale yscale angle alphasource alphadest numclsn1 numclsn2

Not implemented yet, and reported by the load diagnostics: BGMVar, SoundVar (the engine core holds no audio state), AnimLoopCount, AnimPrefix, HelperName, the angle, friction, xshear, drawpal.* and shader variables of ExplodVar, and the attr, guardflag, hitflag, shadow variables of ProjVar. An unknown variable name is reported once per character load as explodvar(name) and evaluates to 0.

Overlays for migrated fighters

tools/mugen2umf/overlays/ holds CNS patches layered on an exact migration through --extra (scripts.cns, with override: true for patches that replace a whole state). goku_ssj4_ryuken.cns replaces the Ryu Ken dragon helper (state 3050) with a homing version: it steers toward NearestFoe with a smoothed turn, flips with Turn when the target is behind, tilts with AngleDraw and slows on contact. goku_ssj4_afterimage.cns adds AfterImage trails to the Goku skills through [Statedef -2], which appends to the original instead of replacing it.

AssertSpecial flags

AssertSpecial accepts flag, flag2, flag3, flag4 and flag5 (a comma list also works in one parameter) and an optional enabled (default 1). Flag names are case insensitive. The full Ikemen GO v1.0.0 set is understood: 58 per-character flags and 19 global flags, plus the engine extension Immovable.

A flag lasts for the tick in which it is asserted. During hit pause the flags asserted before the pause stay on (Ikemen behavior); AnimateHitPause always has to be asserted again. IsAsserted(<flag>) reads the same table, so IsAsserted(NoWalk) and IsAsserted(TimerFreeze) both work.

A flag that is not in the table is ignored. The loader prints one AssertSpecial flags not recognised and ignored line per character, and mugen_check prints an UNKNOWN-FLAGS line for it.

Global flags (19)

FlagEffect
IntroHolds the round in the intro (capped at 10 s)
RoundNotOverHolds the round-over state (capped at 15 s)

RoundFreezeRound timer and round state clock stop

Red life, dizzy and guard points

Every fighter carries three Ikemen GO life systems next to Life. They are always on; a character that never reads them is unaffected apart from the extra bars of state.

Red life

RedLife is the recoverable part of the life bar. It never drops below Life and never rises above LifeMax.

  • A hit subtracts the HitDef redlife value from RedLife, so the red bar grows over the real life bar. A guarded hit uses the second redlife value.
  • LifeAdd, LifeSet, RedLifeAdd and RedLifeSet keep the rule above. When Life rises over RedLife, RedLife follows it.
  • A new round resets RedLife to LifeMax.
  • NoRedLifeDamage stops hits from changing it.

Dizzy points

DizzyPoints start at DizzyPointsMax (the data.dizzypoints constant, data.life when absent).

  • A hit that is not guarded subtracts the HitDef dizzypoints value, multiplied by the defender's defence multiplier.
  • At 0 the defender enters common state 5300 (dizzy) with Dizzy set and control removed. Airborne or falling defenders do not become dizzy.
  • The points refill as the state starts; Dizzy clears when the state ends and the defender is out of hit state.
  • NoDizzyPointsDamage stops hits from lowering the points.

Guard points

GuardPoints start at GuardPointsMax (data.guardpoints, data.life when absent).

  • A guarded hit subtracts the HitDef guardpoints value, multiplied by the defender's defence multiplier.
  • At 0 the defender enters common state 5400 (guard break) with GuardBreak set and control removed.
  • The points refill as the state starts; GuardBreak clears when the state ends and the defender is out of hit state.
  • NoGuardPointsDamage stops guarded hits from lowering the points.

Common states

common1.cns ships states 5300 (dizzy, animation 5300 then 5000) and 5400 (guard break, animation 5400 then 150 then 5000). A character may override either state in its own CNS. When neither state exists the matching system only tracks the numbers.

HitDef defaults

When a HitDef omits redlife, dizzypoints or guardpoints, the engine derives them from the damage with the character's [Constants] multipliers:

ConstantDefaultSuper default (attr has H)
lifetoredlifemul0.750.75
lifetodizzypointsmul1.80
lifetoguardpointsmul1.5-0.33

The keys are written default.lifetoredlifemul and super.lifetoredlifemul in a [Constants] section. A negative guard-points value gives guard points back, so a super move restores a little guard on contact. score = <hit>, <guard> is also read by HitDef and stored for GetHitVar(score).

Triggers and controllers

RedLife, Dizzy, DizzyPoints, DizzyPointsMax, GuardBreak, GuardPoints, GuardPointsMax, GetHitVar(redlife), GetHitVar(dizzypoints) and GetHitVar(guardpoints) read these values. RedLifeSet, RedLifeAdd, DizzyPointsSet, DizzyPointsAdd, DizzySet, GuardPointsSet and GuardPointsAdd change them (see Ikemen extensions).

ZSS states / Estados ZSS

ZSS is the brace-based state syntax introduced by Ikemen GO. List a .zss file in a character's .def (st, st1…st9, stcommon) and it is compiled to the same state controllers as CNS.

ZSS é a sintaxe de estados com chaves criada pelo Ikemen GO. Liste um arquivo .zss no .def do personagem (st, st1…st9, stcommon) e ele vira os mesmos controllers de um CNS.

[StateDef 200; type: S; movetype: A; physics: S; anim: 200; ctrl: 0;]

if AnimElem = 2 {
	HitDef{ attr: S, NA; damage: 20, 0; animtype: Light }
}
if Time = 0 {
	PlaySnd{ value: 0, 0 }
} else {
	VarAdd{ v: 1; value: 1 }
}
persistent(0) ignorehitpause {
	PowerAdd{ value: 10 }
}
switch Var(1) {
case 1, 2:
	CtrlSet{ value: 1 }
default:
	CtrlSet{ value: 0 }
}
FeatureStatus
[StateDef n; key: value;], negative statesSupported
if / else if / else, switch / case / defaultSupported
persistent(n), ignorehitpauseSupported
Any state controller Name{ key: value; … }Supported
let locals (compiled to var(59) downwards, 20 slots)Supported
for / while (unrolled up to 32 iterations per tick, then bounded)Supported
break / continueSupported
call name(args) and [Function name(params)] (inlined, arity checked)Supported

A ZSS file that fails to compile (wrong arity, unknown function, malformed loop, too many locals) is reported as a compile error and not loaded; it never silently drops logic. Loops are bounded to 32 iterations per tick; a while that never changes its condition stops at the cap instead of hanging the match.

Conditions are checked per controller, as in CNS. A controller that changes a value used by its own if affects the controllers that follow it.

As condições são avaliadas por controller, como no CNS. Um controller que muda um valor usado no próprio if afeta os controllers seguintes.

PT-BR: RunState executa os controllers de outro state sem trocar de state; Height ajusta a altura do corpo no tick; GetHitVarSet grava campos do GetHitVar (hittype no lugar de type); ModifyHitDef e ModifyReversalDef alteram só os campos listados; OverrideClsn, ResizeClsn e TransformClsn (clsn = 1 ataque, 2 corpo) mudam as caixas de colisão e aparecem no F2.

PT-BR: AssertCommand mantém um comando ativo por time ticks; AssertInput injeta bits no input do jogador pelos próximos time ticks; ShiftInput empurra (positivo) ou descarta (negativo) ticks do histórico de inputs.

TriggerReturns
Map(name)Named value, 0 when unset (use Root, Map(name) or Parent, Map(name) to read another scope)
TeamMap(name)Value in the team map of the player's side, 0 when unset
RedLifeRed life
Dizzy, DizzyPoints, DizzyPointsMaxDizzy flag and points
GuardBreak, GuardPoints, GuardPointsMaxGuard break flag and points
StandBy1 while tagged out
NumTextTexts the player has on screen
ClsnOverlap(clsn1, id, clsn2)1 when the player's box type overlaps the box type of the player with that id
NumPartnerTeammates on the same side
IsAsserted(flag)1 while the AssertSpecial flag is on (character or global flag)
TeamMode0 single, 1 simul (Parallel), 2 turns (Sequence), 3 tag (reserved, no tag mode yet). Also accepts TeamMode = Simul, TeamMode = turns, TeamMode = 1 (names are case-insensitive)
TeamSizeMembers of the player's team (the whole roster in Sequence mode, the fielded players otherwise)
TeamLeaderPlayerNo of the player's team leader
NumPlayerPlayers in the match (both rosters; 6 for a 3v3 Sequence, 10 for a 5v5 Parallel)
PlayerNo1-based slot of the player: P1, P2, P3... interleaved by side (a helper reports its root's slot); in Sequence mode member * 2 + side + 1
MemberNo1-based position of the player in its team (a helper reports its root's position)
PlayerIndexExist(n)1 when the 0-based index n exists in the match player list (helpers included)
LastPlayerIDID of the most recently created player or helper
IntroState1 before the intro starts, 2 while the intro plays, 0 afterwards
OutroState1 while the round is decided (KO / time over), 2 during the win poses, 0 otherwise

Map keys are case-insensitive. Each map holds at most 256 keys of at most 64 characters; writes that would exceed either limit are ignored.

Chaves de map não diferenciam maiúsculas. Cada map guarda no máximo 256 chaves de até 64 caracteres; escritas acima desses limites são ignoradas.

data.dizzypoints and data.guardpoints in the [Data] section default to data.life. How hits spend these values is described in Red life, dizzy and guard points.

data.dizzypoints e data.guardpoints na seção [Data] usam data.life como padrão.

Helper accepts helpertype = projectile: the helper's HitDef contacts count as projectile hits (ProjHit, ProjContact, ProjGuarded and their *Time forms fire on the helper and on its root, keyed by the helper id), the attacker is not put in hit pause and the helper has no hurtbox. ownprojectile = 1 keeps the projectiles the helper fires on the helper: NumProj and NumProjID of the helper count them and the root does not. size.* parameters (for example size.xscale, size.yscale, size.height, size.ground.back) override the character constants for that helper only, including Const(size.*) and the size of its hurtboxes. A helper spawned by another helper inherits the parent's size.* overrides unless it is spawned with ownclsnscale = 1, which starts from the character's own constants.

Helper aceita helpertype = projectile: os contatos do HitDef do helper contam como acertos de projétil (ProjHit, ProjContact, ProjGuarded e as formas *Time valem no helper e no root, indexados pelo id do helper), o atacante não entra em hit pause e o helper não tem hurtbox. ownprojectile = 1 mantém no helper os projéteis que ele dispara: NumProj e NumProjID do helper os contam e o root não. Os parâmetros size.* (por exemplo size.xscale, size.yscale, size.height, size.ground.back) substituem as constantes do personagem só para aquele helper, inclusive Const(size.*) e o tamanho das hurtboxes. Um helper criado por outro helper herda os size.* do pai, a menos que seja criado com ownclsnscale = 1, que parte das constantes do próprio personagem.

Module controllers / Controllers de módulo

Ikemen GO modules and motifs use these controllers. They are always parsed (a character that contains them still loads and runs); the table says what each one does here. A controller that is not supported does nothing and writes one warning line to the match's compatibility log (Match::console) the first time it runs. The list lives in ume_engine::sctrl::module::MODULE_CONTROLLERS so tools can query it with module_status(name) / rejected_by_design().

Controllers de módulo do Ikemen GO são sempre interpretados (o personagem carrega e roda); os não suportados não fazem nada e registram um aviso único no log de compatibilidade.

ControllerStatusNotes
MatchRestartsupportedResets wins and the round counter and restarts at the start of the next tick
LoadFile, SaveFilerejected by designCharacters never get file access; content runs in a sandbox
ShaderSetrejected by designThe renderer has a fixed pipeline; user shader code is not loaded
Storyboard, RemoveStoryboard, Dialogueplanned[SceneDef] files are parsed but there is no storyboard runtime yet
SaveState, LoadStateplannedNeeds the rollback snapshot of the match (see the roadmap)
LifebarActionplannedThe HUD has no scripting hooks yet
ChangeMovelistplannedThe movelist is fixed at load time

Screenpacks

🇧🇷 Screenpacks são os menus, telas de seleção e barras de vida no formato M.U.G.E.N. Coloque o pacote em data/ e rode o verificador abaixo.

A screenpack is the set of files that draws everything around a fight: title menu, character select, lifebars, fonts, intro and logo storyboards.

Status: the runtime now loads a screenpack when one is present (mugen/data/system.def, mugen/screenpacks/<pack>/system.def or UME_SCREENPACK). The native UI stays as the fallback for anything a pack does not provide:

  • system.def menu.itemname.* labels replace the main-menu titles (Arcade, Survival, teams, Training, Watch, Exit).
  • select.def [Characters] order drives the select grid order.
  • intro.storyboard text scenes are played over the arcade opening cutscene, timed by each scene's end.time.
  • fight.def lifebar pos/range.x place and size the life bars (converted from the pack localcoord to the 426×240 HUD space); the rest of the HUD stays native.
  • Parsed sprites/fonts/sounds are kept in ume_formats::screenpack::Screenpack for the remaining screens, but system/fight sprite drawing (backgrounds, bar sprites, fonts) is still native.

The checker below tells whether a pack parses; the game never refuses to start because of a broken pack (it falls back to the native UI and logs the warnings).

Layout

data/
  system.def      title menu, select screen, music, storyboards
  select.def      roster grid and stage list
  fight.def       lifebars, power bars, round/KO announcers
  system.sff      sprites used by system.def
  system.snd      menu sounds
  fight.sff/.snd  lifebar sprites and announcer voices
font/
  *.fnt           bitmap fonts (v1 binary or v2 text)

File names in [Files] are looked up next to system.def, then in data/, font/ and the game root.

Supported files

FileSections read
system.def[Info] localcoord, [Files], [Music] (*.bgm, .loop, .loopstart, .loopend, .volume), [Title Info] menu.itemname.*, [Select Info] grid, every [<name>BGdef] / [<name> N] background
select.def[Characters] (randomselect, empty, per-character stage and key=value), [ExtraStages], [Options]
fight.def[Files], every pN.* bar part (bg0, bg1, mid, front, counter, pos, range.x) and any element by prefix
Storyboards[SceneDef] spr, startscene, [Scene N] timings, fades, clearcolor, layerall.pos, layerN.*, bg.name, bgm
.fnt v1embedded PCX, [Def] Size, Spacing, Colors, Offset, Type=Fixed/Variable, [Map] with literal or 0xNN chars
.fnt v2[Def] Type=bitmap/truetype, Size, Spacing, Offset, File

Elements

Every visual item follows the same pattern, so anything you can place in one screen works in another:

prefix.anim = 10
prefix.spr = 5,0
prefix.font = 1,0,1
prefix.text = "Round %i"
prefix.offset = 160,120
prefix.scale = 1,1
prefix.facing = -1
prefix.layerno = 1
prefix.displaytime = 60

Checking a screenpack

cargo run -p ume-formats --example screenpack_check -- <game root> data/system.def

It prints what was loaded and one warning: line per missing or broken file. A screenpack with no error: line parses cleanly; displaying it in the engine is not implemented yet.

Screenpack study

What M.U.G.E.N and Ikemen GO screenpacks (motifs) do differently from a plain menu, and what Ultimate MUGEN took from it. Only ideas are used; no third-party art, layouts or sounds are copied.

Sources

  • Ikemen GO wiki: Screenpack features
  • Ikemen GO wiki: Updating to 1.0
  • Ikemen GO menu system (DeepWiki)
  • Ikemen GO issue 329: KOF98-style versus select
  • MUGEN Guild: screen pack docs
  • MUGEN Guild: X-Men Children of the Atom screenpack for Ikemen GO
  • MUGEN Guild: Street Fighter Alpha Zero screenpack, 16:9 and 4:3

The search was limited to forum threads and wiki mirrors; the default motif files themselves could not be fetched, so parameter names below are from secondary sources.

What packs do differently

AreaDifferentialUltimate MUGEN
StructureOne system.def points to select.def, fight.def, sprites, sounds and fonts; any missing file falls back to the default motifSame layout and fallback, see Screenpacks
SelectGrid size and cursor set by parameters, animated portraits, per-character stage and slotsGrid, cursors, team slots and palette row already native, see Character select
VersusOrder select on the versus screen, animated portraits, KOF98-style pickVersus screen with team strips exists; order select is a follow-up
VictoryWinner portrait, name and a typed victory quote after Arcade, Versus, Quick Match and WatchWinner pose and name existed; quote is a follow-up
ResultsTime, combo and damage grading, time-challenge best times on the select screenNew stats strip (below)
ResolutionPacks ship for 4:3 and 16:9 with localcoordlocalcoord is converted to the 426x240 HUD space
ParserUnknown fields produce warnings instead of silent failureChecker prints one warning: per broken file

Implemented from this study

The results screen shows four glass chips under the winner line: match time, best combo of each side, total damage dealt by each side and life left of each side as a percentage. src/match_stats.rs observes the match after every tick (outside the deterministic engine, so rollback and replays are unaffected) and src/app/results_stats.rs draws the chips. Texts are localized in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

Preview: UME_SHOTS_ONLY=results xvfb-run -a target/release/ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute.

Next candidates

  1. Order select inside the versus screen for team modes.
  2. Victory quote line typed under the winner name.
  3. Rank grade (S to D) from time, life left and combo.
  4. Best-time records per character in the select screen for time-attack modes.

Deeper survey (second pass)

Community screenpacks checked by their stated features (no art or layout copied):

PackDifferentialTakeaway for the engine
IKEMEN Generations HD (OroCrimson)Category-first select: up/down picks a category, left/right a character; custom KOF 2002 style lifebarsCategory navigation for big rosters
Infinite Legacy X HDVery large slot counts (700 slots); author notes the engine struggles with huge gridsPaging and virtualized grid already exist; keep it that way
Capcom vs SNK HD Black EditionSelectable slot densities (120 to 840)Grid density as a setting

Ikemen-GO-Screenpack and PR #56Official default motif being replaced with original art and MIT fontsReference for a clean default motif
Engine PR #4146Alpha and blend on every animation and text element; slot cycling; stage select buttonsPer-element alpha is worth copying in our HUD tokens
Ikemen-GO-Plus screenpack.luaLua hooks read localcoord from system.defScripting is out of scope; keep data-driven
external-lua-modulesCarousel-style select as external modulesCandidate for a future carousel layout

Also noted: the grid in recent Ikemen nightlies is oblique and capped near 80 slots by default, which suggests a single fixed grid model is a weak point for the whole ecosystem.

Caveats: several pages are older (2023 to 2025), and popularity is inferred from forum and listing pages, not download counts.

Implemented in the second pass

  • Select categories: Tab now cycles four categories: all, originals (no bosses), M.U.G.E.N, and bosses (src/app/select_category.rs). Labels are localized.
  • Per-element HUD opacity: the advantage banner, passive meter and guard tag draw at 80, 85 and 90 percent alpha (src/hud/opacity.rs, ume_shell::alpha_scale). Glass panels from the post pass are not affected yet.

Grid density

The select grid has three presets, cycled with G on the select screen and saved as grid= in the config: compact (9 rows), normal (7 rows, the previous default) and large (4 rows). The settings file was split into settings/persist.rs, settings/window.rs and settings/tests.rs to make room.

Preview: UME_SHOTS_ONLY=results also writes grid-0.png, grid-1.png and grid-2.png.

Sprite Atlas Import

The CLI limits atlas files to 64 MiB, image dimensions to 16,384 pixels per side and 8 million total pixels, and output canvases to 2,048 pixels to keep local imports bounded.

The import_sprite_atlas example validates and imports a transparent 3-column by 2-row atlas containing six poses. It leaves the source atlas untouched and exports one standalone PNG per requested pose name.

cargo run -p ume-engine --example import_sprite_atlas -- --atlas .\poses.png --out assets\chars\sprites\fighter --cols 3 --rows 2 --names 01_idle,02_walk,03_attack,04_crouch,05_hit,06_fall --canvas 400 --validate-only
cargo run -p ume-engine --example import_sprite_atlas -- --atlas .\poses.png --out assets\chars\sprites\fighter --cols 3 --rows 2 --names 01_idle,02_walk,03_attack,04_crouch,05_hit,06_fall --canvas 400

--canvas defaults to 400 pixels. Every output has that square size; opaque pixels are uniformly scaled with nearest-neighbor sampling, centered horizontally by their cell, and aligned by their alpha bounds to the common floor at y=392. Transparent cell padding does not affect placement. The default standing-pose reference is 80% of the source cell height. Use --reference-height to provide the source alpha height of the standing pose when a character family requires explicit calibration. The same reference is applied to all six poses, so crouching and falling poses retain the standing scale. Only transformed opaque bounds must fit the canvas.

The importer requires actual RGBA alpha, six non-empty cells, and a meaningful connected alpha component in every pose. Alpha below 16 is discarded in exported frames and ignored for border and component validation. It rejects poses whose alpha reaches the cell edge and sheets with excessive isolated alpha components; inspect and repair the atlas instead of accepting clipped poses or noise. These checks are diagnostics, not visual quality approval. --validate-only also normalizes all six poses and checks that their opaque bounds fit before reporting success. All six PNGs are encoded before any output file is written.

meta.json is merged without discarding unrelated fields. Each imported frames[name] entry records the 320-pixel reference and normalized axes (axisX=200, axisY=392 by default). The importer preserves the top-level refHeight exactly as found, including leaving it absent, so older frames keep their image-height fallback. Existing frame entries with the same names are replaced. Existing PNGs are protected unless --overwrite is supplied. --validate-only performs validation and collision checks without writing files.

Validation evidence: a synthetic padded 300x200 RGBA atlas passed validation and produced six 400x400 PNGs. An independent PNG decode confirmed the last opaque row was 391, meeting the floor edge at axisY=392, with no exported alpha below 16. A fixture with alpha crossing a cell border and an oversized normalization request were rejected; validate-only created no output directory. The generated Bruno walk-cycle atlas also passed validation and import with --reference-height 468; its output bbox was x=115..271, y=75..391 with no alpha below 16. The source atlas SHA-256 remained 56AED5E92D7F55A80C0CD288DA983E033DA17EEB6F67D8A95D099F0147ACE1D7.

The PNG writer converts straight RGBA channels to tiny-skia's premultiplied pixel representation and encodes the result. Atlas bytes are never modified.

Sprite Toolkit

Local, dependency-light tools (Rust, charforge binary) in crates/charforge/ (spritekit module) that turn generated art into MUGEN-ready assets. They never touch assets/chars or stages: output goes to a folder you choose.

cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- slice sheet.png out/ --group 9000 --axis feet
cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- slice sheet.png out/ --mode grid --grid 6 2
cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- palettes base.act variants/ --only red blue dark --keep 1 2
cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- air out/manifest.json --action 200 --ticks 4 --attack
cargo test --release -p ume-charforge
ToolWhat it does
sliceDetects the background (transparency or border color), cuts sprites by connected pieces or by grid, sets each axis at the feet (shared floor per row), builds one shared 256-color palette (index 0 transparent, flagged when quantized) and writes indexed PNGs plus manifest.json
palettesBuilds .act variants (hue, saturation, brightness presets) from a base .act; index 0 and --keep indices never change
airEmits an AIR action from the manifest with Clsn2 anatomical boxes (head, torso, legs) and optional Clsn1 for extended limbs, relative to each sprite axis

Library functions in collision_boxes.py also offer interpolate_boxes for in-between frames.

What was not ported

The move generator is in Move Generator. CharFactory's GUI editors, AI assistant and MCP server, tick-by-tick simulator and SFF/SND writers overlap with the engine itself (crates/formats, crates/engine, mugen_check) or are large. Candidates for later work are listed in the Move Generator page.

Acknowledgments

Approach inspired by CharFactory by eduardovbe, MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 eduardovbe. The code here is a fresh, smaller implementation; the MIT notice is reproduced in REFERENCES.md.

Move Generator

crates/charforge/ (movekit module) turns a TOML description of moves into MUGEN text: animations with automatic Clsn boxes, statedefs, command entries and a [Statedef -1] block. Edit the spec and regenerate instead of hand-editing the output.

cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- moves moves.toml out/
cargo test --release -p ume-charforge

Writes moves.air, moves.cns, moves.cmd and statedef-1.cns. A full example is in crates/charforge/examples/moves.toml; it expects sprites sliced by Sprite toolkit at sprites/manifest.json.

Spec

KeyMeaning
[defaults]sprite_manifests, clsn1_height (standing height, grows the attack box), hitsound, guardsound, super_sound, voice_channel
kindnormal, crouch, air, special, air_special, super, projectile, throw (sets damage, pause, power and attribute defaults)
state, animState number and animation number (default: the state)
command, command_name, command_timeMUGEN input notation; default name spec_<state>
frames[group, item, ticks, "hit"?, {x, y, flip, trans, clsn1, clsn2}?]; "hit" adds an automatic Clsn1
hitHitDef list; elem or elems choose the animation elements (default: first frame with Clsn1); extra adds raw parameters
sounds, vel, vfx, helpers, cancel, extra, voicePlaySnd, velocity, Explod, Helper, cancel and raw controllers
power, superpausePower cost and SuperPause for supers
phasesExtra chained states with name, next, like; the move is the first state

Generated entries in [Statedef -1] are ordered super, special, throw, normal and gated by roundstate = 2, state type and power.

Validating

cargo run --release -p ume-charforge -- check <char_dir> --strict loads the character with the engine loader and prints the same diagnostics as mugen_check; --strict fails on unsupported controllers, triggers or parameters.

Next candidates from CharFactory

A tick-by-tick move simulator for frame data, a combo tuner, palette range tools and a contact-sheet renderer. Not ported yet.

Make a stage (quick start)

English · Português (BR)

There are three kinds of stage work. Pick the one you need:

You wantNeeds code?Go to
A new background from your own art, with the M.U.G.E.N formatNoM.U.G.E.N stage
More content for one of the five story arenas (objects, music, animated sky)NoStory arenas
A new arena in the story mode or a new built-in arenaYes, RustWhat needs code

1. A M.U.G.E.N stage

  1. Put two files in mugen/stages/: my-stage.def and my-stage.sff (the art).
  2. Start from docs/examples/stage/my-stage.def.

The .def file is plain text with sections:

SectionWhat to set
[Info]name, displayname, author
[Camera]startx, boundleft, boundright (how far the camera can go), boundhigh, boundlow, verticalfollow, tension
[PlayerInfo]p1startx, p2startx (where each fighter starts)
[StageInfo]zoffset (height of the floor line on screen), localcoord (the drawing size, for example 320, 240)
[BGdef]spr: the .sff file
[BG name]One section per layer (see below)

Each background layer:

[BG Sky]
type = normal          ; normal (one sprite) or anim (an action from the .air file)
spriteno = 0, 0        ; group, image of the .sff
layerno = 0            ; 0 = behind the fighters, 1 = in front
start = 0, 0          ; position in local units
delta = .2, .2         ; parallax: 1, 1 moves with the floor, smaller moves slower
tile = 1, 0            ; repeat on x, on y (0 = no repeat)

Every key of the stage format, including scale, rotation and clipping windows, is in the stage reference.

Text after ; is a comment. Key names are the M.U.G.E.N ones, so a stage copied from a M.U.G.E.N pack is a good starting point.

Limits of this path: the animated loop, story strips, breakables and per-stage music from the next sections do not apply to M.U.G.E.N stages.

2. Story arenas

The story mode has five arenas: brazil, neon, bamboo, volcano and dojo. Each one can be extended with data:

WhatWhereNotes
Backdrop stripassets/stages/story/<arena>.pngOne segment per fight (four waves and the boss). Regenerate with python3 tools/story_segments.py
Animated backgroundassets/stages/animation/<arena>/Eight opaque 1672×941 keyframes (00.png through 07.png) and eight interleaved -mid.png frames. Playback advances every four ticks and wraps after 64 ticks. Keep the camera and fighting floor registered throughout the loop.
Breakables, food, bonus roundassets/story/objects.toml, table [stages.<arena>]Full format in Stage objects
Fight musictweaks.toml, section [music], key <arena id>Path to .ogg, .mp3, .wav or .flac, relative to tweaks.toml. Desktop only. See Configuration

Example tweaks.toml:

[music]
fight = "music/my-fight.ogg"   ; every fight without its own track
dojo = "music/dojo.ogg"        ; wins over fight, only in the dojo

Example objects.toml entry:

[stages.dojo]
objects = [
  { fight = 0, kind = "crate", x = -78.0, lane = -22.0, drop = "apple" },
]

Verify with the Stage objects evidence tour: UME_TOUR=storyobjects and UME_TOUR=storyloop.

Built-in arena loops, size and interactivity

  • True 60 FPS seamless loop: built-in animated stages (assets/stages/animation/<id>/00.png..07-mid.png) decode in parallel (ume_formats::par::map) and cross-fade smoothly between consecutive frames across a closed 96-tick cycle (loop_sample), eliminating wrap jumps from the last frame back to frame 0.
  • Expanded arena dimensions: built-in arenas span bound_left = -680 to bound_right = 680 (bound_high = -140, zoom_out = 0.62, zoom_in = 1.05) with 0.21 panoramic parallax in illustration_layout.
  • Reactive floors & interactive arena props: all 21 illustrated stages (including brazil and the 14 World Wonders via StageKind::Arena) render StageReact ground cracks, scorch marks, ripples and impact debris. In Versus/Arcade fights, src/stages/interactive.rs places destructible crates and explosive hazard barrels (ObjectEvent::Blast) on the outer wings (|x| >= 220, keeping the center fighting lane clear); knocked-back fighters slamming into props shatter them, and both sides can collect dropped pickups (any_collector = true). Set UME_STAGE_PROPS=0 to disable arena props.

3. What needs code

These things cannot be done with files today. Each one is a feature gap, not a bug in your files:

  • A new built-in arena. Native stages are Rust functions in src/stages.rs (builtin()). A new one needs code, an embedded PNG and a thumbnail. See Creating stages.
  • A new story arena. The list of arenas is fixed in src/stages/story_strip.rs (STORY_ARENAS) and the story mode data in src/story/stages.rs.
  • An animated sky for a M.U.G.E.N stage. Loop frames are only read for built-in arena ids.
  • A [Music] section in a .def. Music per stage comes from tweaks.toml only.
  • A type = parallax layer. Planned, not in the format.

Test

cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it wiki_examples::
UME_SHOTS_ONLY=stages cargo run --release -- --shots out/   # screenshots of every stage

The first command checks the sections of the example .def. The second saves screenshots of the stages to out/.

Creating stages

There are two paths: a M.U.G.E.N stage (.def + .sff files, no programming) or a native stage (Rust code, with procedural layers and reactive effects).

M.U.G.E.N stage

Put my_stage.def and my_stage.sff in mugen/stages/.

[Info]
name = "My Stage"
displayname = "My Stage"

[Camera]
startx = 0
starty = 0
boundleft = -150
boundright = 150
boundhigh = -25
boundlow = 0
verticalfollow = .2
tension = 50

[PlayerInfo]
p1startx = -70
p2startx = 70

[StageInfo]
zoffset = 210
localcoord = 320, 240

[BGdef]
spr = my_stage.sff

[BG Sky]
type = normal
spriteno = 0, 0
layerno = 0
start = 0, 0
delta = .2, .2
tile = 1, 0
velocity = .1, 0

[BG Floor]
type = normal
spriteno = 1, 0
start = 0, 160
delta = 1, 1
mask = 1

[BG Flag]
type = anim
actionno = 10
start = 80, 60
delta = .8, .8

[Begin Action 10]
2,0, 0,0, 6
2,1, 0,0, 6
SectionSupported keys
[Info]name, displayname
[Camera]startx, boundleft, boundright, boundhigh, boundlow, verticalfollow, tension
[PlayerInfo]p1startx, p2startx
[StageInfo]zoffset, localcoord
[BGdef]spr
[BG ...]type (normal, anim, parallax), spriteno, actionno, layerno (0 behind, 1 in front), start, delta, tile, tilespacing, velocity, trans, mask, scalestart, scaledelta, angle, xshear, window, maskwindow, windowdelta, spacing

Layer transform parameters (Ikemen / M.U.G.E.N 1.1), applied by both the live renderer and the stage-select preview:

KeyMeaning
scalestart = x, yBase scale of the sprite, anchored at its axis (default 1, 1).
scaledelta = x, yScale change per stage unit of camera movement, multiplied by delta: scale = scalestart + scaledelta * camera * delta, so the layer grows or shrinks as the camera moves (default 0, 0).
angleRotation in degrees around the sprite axis, counter-clockwise for positive values.
xshearHorizontal shear: each row is shifted by xshear times its distance from the axis.
window = x1, y1, x2, y2Clipping rectangle in stage units.
maskwindow = x1, y1, x2, y2Second clipping rectangle; when both are present the layer is clipped to their intersection.
windowdelta = x, yHow fast the clipping window scrolls with the camera (defaults to the layer delta).
spacing = x, yGap between tiles; used when tilespacing is absent (tilespacing wins when both are set).

Planned: configurable shadows and reflections.

Music, sky and parallax

[Music] plays the stage track when the fight starts (it replaces the default track; without it the fight uses the usual music). The file is resolved relative to the .def, then from the root of the content folder.

[Music]
bgmusic = sound/my_theme.ogg
bgmvolume = 80
bgmloopstart = 0
bgmloopend = 0
KeyDefaultMeaning
bgmusicnoneTrack file (.ogg, .mp3, .flac or .wav)
bgmvolume100Percent of the normal music volume
bgmloopstart, bgmloopend0Loop points in samples; both 0 loops the whole file

type = parallax is a layer that repeats without end on the X axis and drifts with its velocity, without tile = 1, 0. Use it for a sky strip, far hills or clouds. delta still sets how much the layer follows the camera.

[BG Ridge]
type = parallax
spriteno = 2, 0
layerno = 0
start = 0, 140
delta = 0.8, 1
velocity = 0.1, 0

[Sky] draws an animated sky behind the fighters, on top of the first background layer. It works for every stage, including those that come from a .def. type is one of:

TypeLook
auroraGreen-blue bands of light that drift sideways over the top of the screen
godraysLight rays fanning out from the top centre
starsA starfield that twinkles
cloudsSoft clouds that drift across the upper part of the screen
KeyDefaultMeaning
color255, 255, 255Tint, r, g, b from 0 to 255
intensity0.6Opacity at its brightest, 0 to 1
speed1Speed of the drift and pulse, 0 to 8
[Sky]
type = aurora
color = 120, 255, 200
intensity = 0.5
speed = 1

The bundled example stage assets/stages/data/example/ uses all three.

Reading the stage from scripts

StageVar(<name>) returns the stage value in the stage's own localcoord units. The section prefix is optional: StageVar(camera.boundleft) and StageVar(boundleft) are the same query.

NameValue
info.name, info.displayname, info.author, info.mugenversiontext, compared with StageVar(info.author) = "name" (case-insensitive)
camera.startx, camera.starty, camera.boundleft, camera.boundright, camera.boundhigh, camera.boundlownumbers
camera.verticalfollow, camera.tension, camera.zoomin, camera.zoomoutnumbers
playerinfo.p1startx, playerinfo.p2startx, playerinfo.leftbound, playerinfo.rightboundnumbers
playerinfo.autoturn1 unless the stage sets autoturn = 0
stageinfo.zoffset, stageinfo.localcoord.x, stageinfo.localcoord.y, stageinfo.roundtimenumbers (localcoord alone means the width; roundtime is -1 when the stage does not set it)
shadow.intensity, shadow.yscale, reflection.intensitynumbers

Text queries evaluate to 0 when used as a number. Unknown names evaluate to 0 and print one warning when the expression is compiled. On the built-in flat and native stages the values come from the engine defaults.

Camera parameters

The [Camera] group accepts these extra keys. Every key is optional and its default reproduces the previous camera, so a stage that omits them behaves exactly as before.

KeyDefaultEffect
verticalfollow0.2Fraction of the highest fighter's height the camera follows upward
tension50Horizontal dead zone: the camera only pans when a fighter comes closer than this to a screen edge, so a cornered fighter stays put while the opponent walks in
verticalfollowdelta0Dead zone in stage pixels: the vertical target only changes when it moved at least this much, which stops small jumps from shaking the camera
yscrollspeed0.3Share of the remaining vertical distance covered per tick (clamped to 0..1)
zoominspeed, zoomoutspeed0.04Share of the remaining zoom difference covered per tick when the camera zooms in or out (clamped to 0..1; 0 holds the zoom, 1 snaps in one tick)
lowestcap0When 1 the camera never sinks below starty
dynamicboundhigh0When 1 boundhigh is raised by boundhighdelta for every unit of zoom-out above 1x, so the sky stays reachable while zoomed out
boundhighdelta0Used by dynamicboundhigh

autoturn in [PlayerInfo] (default 1) controls whether fighters turn around by themselves when the opponent crosses over them in the stand, walk and crouch states. autoturn = 0 keeps their facing until a controller changes it (AssertSpecial flag = noautoturn still disables it per character). StageVar(camera.<key>) and StageVar(playerinfo.autoturn) read all of these.

Built-in stage from data only

A built-in stage does not need Rust. Create a folder assets/stages/data/<id>/ with a stage.def and the sprite file it names (for example example.sff). At build time every folder there is embedded in the binary (build.rs), appears in the stage selector as a built-in stage, and is loaded like any MUGEN stage, including [Music], [Sky] and parallax layers. The display name comes from [Info] displayname.

assets/stages/data/example/
  stage.def
  example.sff

The example folder is a working stage with an aurora sky and a parallax ridge. scripts/make-example-stage.py regenerates it. Rebuild after adding or changing files, because the files are embedded.

Native stages in Rust remain available for procedural art and reactive effects (see below).

Native stage

Native stages live in src/stages.rs and their animated effects in src/stagefx.rs.

  1. Write a fn mine() -> Stage that builds layers with lay(...) and the primitives from ume_engine::raster (rect, lin, gradients) and texgen (blobs, grain, haze). Use dojo() as a model.
  2. Register it in builtin():
#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
StageEntry { id: "mine".into(), name: "My Stage".into(), thumb: [[10, 10, 30], [40, 40, 90], [200, 120, 60]], build: Box::new(mine) },
}
  1. For reactive effects (dust, crowds, water), add a StageKind variant and handle it in stagefx.rs.
  2. Capture screenshots to review: UME_SHOTS_ONLY=stages UME_STAGE=mine cargo run --release -- --shots out/.

Each Layer has delta (parallax), y, front (drawn in front of the fighters) and dynamic (no bitmap, drawn by stagefx).

Built-in pixel art

The twenty-one native arenas use embedded full-color PNG artwork in assets/stages/: seven core realms (dojo.png, neon.png, bamboo.png, plains.png, spirit.png, volcano.png and brazil.png), seven world landmarks (great_wall.png, petra.png, christ_redeemer.png, texas.png, chichen_itza.png, colosseum.png, taj_mahal.png), and seven Ancient Wonders of the World (pyramids_giza.png, hanging_gardens.png, temple_artemis.png, statue_zeus.png, mausoleum_halicarnassus.png, colossus_rhodes.png, lighthouse_alexandria.png). Generation prompts and tool provenance are recorded in assets/stages/prompts.json. No external image service or filesystem access is needed at runtime.

StageArt::Illustrated draws the background with nearest-neighbor filtering, aligns the fighting floor at 85% of the image height, and clamps horizontal camera movement to the image edges. Team zoom retains the native ground proportion. Fighter shadows, reflections and combat effects remain active; the old procedural prop animations are exclusive to procedural artwork.

All twenty-one built-in stages have eight ambient animation phases under assets/stages/animation/<stage_id>/. Each 1672×941 transparent PNG adds stage-specific petals, leaves, embers, rain, dust, or spirit motes while preserving the original artwork and fight floor. The game composites the overlays once when a stage loads, then advances the loop every eight simulation ticks. Native builds embed the small overlays; the web build fetches them only for the selected stage. Regenerate the overlays with python tools/gen_stage_loops.py; prompts and event descriptions are recorded in assets/stages/prompts.json.

Living layers

Every illustrated stage also carries an ambience profile (src/stages/ambience.rs, data in src/stages/ambience/profiles/): translucent mist banks that drift sideways, particles (petals, embers, fireflies, dust, leaves, sparks, birds), additive light pools anchored to lanterns, windows, fire and sun, and slanted god rays. They are drawn every frame with vertex-coloured polygons over the flat artwork (front: true layers pass in front of the fighters), react to camera parallax, use Match::game_time for motion and scale their particle count with the effects setting. A unit test caps every profile at 420 polygons per frame and checks every value range. To animate a new illustrated stage add a Profile for its id in profiles/classic.rs or profiles/wonders.rs; unknown ids fall back to a few drifting dust motes.

The stage selector displays the same artwork, cropped to each tile without changing its aspect ratio. Random selection and imported M.U.G.E.N stages retain their existing gradient tiles. Imported stages keep their own artwork during combat.

Set UME_STAGE_ART=procedural to compare the original procedural stages. The selector continues to show the default pixel-art illustrations. Capture the selector with UME_SHOTS_ONLY=stage-select ultimate-mugen --shots out/ --res 1280x720 --mute, or all seven fights with UME_SHOTS_ONLY=stages.

Native Arenas, Lore & Character Affinities

Each native arena in Ultimate MUGEN represents a critical focal point in the convergence of dimensions. Below is the full guide to the seven native battlegrounds, their world lore, and the fighters who call them home.

1. Sunset Dojo Roof (dojo) — Telhado do Dojo — Pôr do Sol

  • Atmosphere: An ancient mountain pagoda dojo perched above misty valleys at golden hour. Cherry blossom branches frame the weathered timber deck, with warm paper lanterns flickering against amber-rose clouds.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Kaito Arashi: The sacred training grounds where Kaito completed his Arashi-ryu mastery before beginning his wandering journey.
    • Akio Hoshi: Neighboring mountain summit where the Starfall Dojo observes the evening sky.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Lian Feng: Travels from Mount Wudang for an exhibition duel between Chinese flowing silk kicks and Japanese storm karate.
    • Jin Kazaguruma: Arrives via the rooftops to test his wind chakrams against Kaito's gale fist.
  • Narrative Context: Represents traditional martial honor, disciplined breathing, and the tranquil purity of combat before cosmic corruption touches the world.

2. Neo-Metropolis 2099 (neon) — Neo-Metrópole 2099

  • Atmosphere: The rain-slicked rooftop of a mega-skyscraper in a cyberpunk metropolis. Towering holographic ads in cyan and magenta glow through the midnight mist, while aerial cruisers drift between neon-lit towers.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • VX-9 Volta: The cybernetic testing ground and rooftop escape route where Volta severed his corporate telemetry.
    • Valdric Morn: The industrial command sector where the Red Star Empire deploys heavy mechanized garrison units.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Captain Marlow Reyes: Raids corporate data servers with his sky-galleon, dueling security units on the helicopter deck.
    • Akio Hoshi: Climbs the mega-towers to challenge Valdric's cold military technology with pure stellar plasma.
  • Narrative Context: Symbolizes the collision of rampant technocracy with human spirit, where high-voltage capacitors and corporate tyrants clash with rogue awakenings.

3. Moonlit Bamboo Grove (bamboo) — Bambuzal ao Luar

  • Atmosphere: An ancient, whispering jade bamboo forest illuminated by a radiant full moon. Deep teal shadows, a murmuring mountain brook, glowing fireflies, and weathered stone lanterns create an aura of silent danger.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Shion Kurogane: Shion's secluded sanctuary where he meditates under the pale moon, practicing his heavy lunar sword forms.
    • Suzume Kagerou: The shadow corridor through which Suzume stalks her targets, moving silently between bamboo stalks.
    • Lian Feng: Sacred groves surrounding the lower slopes of the Jade Lantern sanctuaries.
    • Jin Kazaguruma: The high canopy highways where Jin leaps between bamboo tips with his gale chakrams.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Kaname Fuyutsuki: Dueling Shion under the full moon to determine whether sorrow or divine duty wields the truer blade.
    • Mikazuki Oboro: The shadows twist into nightmare ravens as Oboro sends phantom assassins to eliminate the surviving clan heirs.
  • Narrative Context: The battleground of stealth, patience, and poetic stillness, where a single rustle of bamboo leaves heralds a lethal strike.

4. Rocky Plateau (plains) — Planalto Rochoso

  • Atmosphere: Immense sandstone mesas and sun-baked canyon terraces beneath a luminous azure sky. Golden steppe grasses sway along weathered geological strata, offering an expansive, unobstructed natural arena.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Daichi Ginrou: The rugged canyon perimeter where Daichi runs with silver wolves and tests his golden ki against solid stone.
    • Akio Hoshi: Ancient meteorite impact sites where Akio meditates on fallen cosmic stones.
    • Captain Marlow Reyes: The open desert canyons where Marlow grounds his sky-galleon for repairs and duels.
    • Sylene Vashti: A windswept highland where Sylene practices freezing the arid air into protective glacial walls.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Bruno Volk vs. Daichi Ginrou: A clash of titans where heavy boxing punches collide with lupine claws, shaking the mesa.
    • Marlow Reyes vs. Lian Feng: A high-stakes duel over ancient maps found within the sandstone ruins.
  • Narrative Context: Represents raw, untamed natural vitality, geological endurance, and the honest joy of physical combat beneath the open sun.

5. Gate of Spirits (spirit) — Portão dos Espíritos

  • Atmosphere: Weathered vermilion torii gates standing sentinel over an ancient mist-shrouded shrine courtyard. Turquoise spirit motes drift between mossy stone lanterns and colossal sacred camphor trees beneath a quiet night sky.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Kaname Fuyutsuki: The sacred gateway protected by Kaname's Everwinter blade, serving as the border between the mortal and spirit realms.
    • Haruki Sumi: The ancient shrine vaults where Haruki studies forgotten sealing texts and prays to keep the Twilight Titans asleep.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Mikazuki Oboro: Manifests his shadow illusions directly at the torii gate, seeking to tear open the veil between the living and the dead.
    • Garan the Ashen Oni: Stalks the shrine perimeter, seeking to shatter Haruki's paper talismans and consume the spirits within.
    • Suzume Kagerou: Infiltrates the sacred grounds to intercept Oboro's disciples before they desecrate ancestral graves.
  • Narrative Context: The metaphysical heart of the world, where divine judgments are passed and the spiritual fabric of reality is either defended or corrupted.

6. Volcanic Crater (volcano) — Cratera Vulcânica

  • Atmosphere: An active basalt caldera glowing with incandescent rivers of orange magma. Crimson volcanic smoke, floating embers, and intense amber rim lighting illuminate a solid obsidian fighting terrace laced with glowing fissures.
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Garan the Ashen Oni: The hellish subterranean threshold from which Garan crawled into the mortal realm.
    • Mikazuki Oboro: The convergence apex where the ritual of the Scarlet Eclipse focuses planetary cosmic energy.
    • Valdric Morn: The industrial geothermal smelting foundries where the Red Star Empire manufactures heavy warmachines.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Sylene Vashti: Sylene ventures into the burning caldera to freeze the molten veins and avenge her frozen homeland.
    • Kaito Arashi: The climactic final confrontation against Oboro and Garan to disperse the crimson clouds with the Eye of the Storm.
  • Narrative Context: The domain of primordial chaos, destruction, and ultimate stakes. The final testing ground where the fate of all converging realities is decided.

7. Hinterland Plaza — Brazil (brazil) — Praça do Interior — Brasil

  • Atmosphere: A warm, charming small town square in the Brazilian interior (inspired by historic Minas Gerais and São Paulo countryside) at golden hour. Pastel colonial stucco houses with aged wooden shutters, a cream-and-blue church in the background, a traditional bandstand (coreto), flowering ipê and jacarandá trees, and classic Portuguese stone paving (calçada portuguesa).
  • Native Fighters (Home Stage):
    • Bruno "Bulldozer" Volk: The beloved town square where Bruno grew up, works out at the local gym, and protects his neighbors.
  • Key Challengers & Story Battles:
    • Haruki Sumi: Arrives seeking quiet shelter and warm hospitality, welcomed by Bruno with fresh coffee and cheese bread (pão de queijo).
    • Daichi Ginrou: Enters the town with a wide grin, drawn by rumors of an unbeatable heavyweight champion who fights with bare fists.
    • Valdric Morn: An imperial scouting squad attempts to annex the town for raw resources, only to be met by Bruno and an outraged community.
  • Narrative Context: Represents the warmth of community, the resilience of everyday working people, and the peaceful mortal lives that the heroes are fighting to protect. It uses the plains theme music and has no legacy procedural counterpart.

The 7 Modern Wonders of the World

8. Great Wall of China (great_wall) — Grande Muralha da China

  • Atmosphere: An ancient stone fortification winding across rugged mist-shrouded green mountain ridges at sunrise. Imposing brick watchtowers frame the battlement fighting deck, with golden morning sunlight breaking through soft clouds and fluttering imperial banners.
  • Lore & Affinities: Sacred bastion where martial artists of the East test their endurance and footwork. Lian Feng and Jin Kazaguruma hold exhibition clashes along the winding ramparts.

9. Petra — Al-Khazneh (petra) — Petra — Al-Khazneh

  • Atmosphere: The monumental rose-red rock-cut Hellenistic temple facade of The Treasury carved into towering sandstone canyon walls of the Siq. Warm desert sunlight, glowing bronze braziers, and a level sandstone arena floor.
  • Lore & Affinities: Hidden desert sanctuary of forgotten merchant princes and desert nomads. Daichi Ginrou and Marlow Reyes duel for ancient relics stored within the rock-cut vaults.

10. Christ the Redeemer (christ_redeemer) — Cristo Redentor — Corcovado

  • Atmosphere: Perched atop Mount Corcovado in Rio de Janeiro at golden sunset. The colossal Art Deco statue opens its arms over Guanabara Bay and Sugarloaf Mountain far below as twilight colors wash across the sky and city lights flicker to life.
  • Lore & Affinities: A beacon of divine grace and sanctuary overlooking the metropolis. Bruno Volk and Haruki Sumi clash under the sacred silhouette at dusk.

11. Inland Town — Texas, USA (texas) — Cidade do Interior — Texas, EUA

  • Atmosphere: A historic frontier small town in inland West Texas at dusty golden sunset. Weathered wooden clapboard saloon and general store with covered boardwalk porches, an old red brick courthouse with a bell tower cupola, a spinning steel windmill water tower, telegraph poles with drooping wires, the Texas Lone Star flag fluttering in the breeze, saguaro and prickly pear cactus framing the edges, and a broad level packed sand and dirt fighting road.
  • Lore & Affinities: The rugged heartland of lone wanderers, brawlers, and frontier lawmen. Bruno Volk and Captain Marlow Reyes duel in high-noon brawls along the dusty thoroughfare.

12. Chichén Itzá (chichen_itza) — Chichén Itzá — Templo de Kukulcán

  • Atmosphere: The grand Mesoamerican step-pyramid of El Castillo under a deep purple twilight sky scattered with ancient Mayan constellations. Carved feathered serpent heads flank the stone balustrades amid lush tropical jungle foliage.
  • Lore & Affinities: Nexus of celestial alignments and feathered serpent deity worship. Mikazuki Oboro and Garan invoke eclipse magic on the ceremonial plaza.

13. Colosseum of Rome (colosseum) — Coliseu de Roma

  • Atmosphere: The monumental Roman amphitheater in late golden-hour afternoon. Multi-tiered travertine arches, weathered Corinthian columns, imperial red vexillum banners, and packed golden fighting sand.
  • Lore & Affinities: Legendary epicenter of gladiator combat and martial glory. Bruno Volk, Daichi Ginrou, and Valdric Morn clash in ruthless exhibition duels before the imperial banners.

14. Taj Mahal (taj_mahal) — Taj Mahal — Palácio de Mármore

  • Atmosphere: The radiant ivory-white marble mausoleum reflected in the tranquil Yamuna reflecting pool at pink-gold dawn. Slender cypress trees, lotus pools, and intricate carved marble jali screens frame the polished fighting deck.
  • Lore & Affinities: Eternal monument of love and perfection. Akio Hoshi and Lian Feng exchange harmonious ki strikes across the pristine marble terrace.

The 7 Ancient Wonders of the World

15. Great Pyramids of Giza (pyramids_giza) — Pirâmides de Gizé

  • Atmosphere: Colossal limestone pyramids of Khufu and Khafre rising against a burning desert sunset. The limestone profile of the Great Sphinx and distant date palm silhouettes gaze over the level sandstone terrace.
  • Lore & Affinities: Primordial tomb complex where Pharaohs attained immortality. Garan and Marlow Reyes search for forbidden astral relics beneath the shifting dunes.

16. Hanging Gardens of Babylon (hanging_gardens) — Jardins Suspensos da Babilônia

  • Atmosphere: Monumental multi-tiered palace terraces cascading with tropical blossoms, date palms, weeping willows, and aqueduct waterfalls. Lapis lazuli glazed brick walls with gold lion reliefs overlook the Euphrates.
  • Lore & Affinities: Mesopotamian wonder built by royal love. Haruki Sumi and Sylene Vashti duel amid fragrant jasmine and cascading mountain waters.

17. Temple of Artemis at Ephesus (temple_artemis) — Templo de Ártemis em Éfeso

  • Atmosphere: Colossal Greek temple colonnade of fluted Ionic marble columns under a starry Aegean night sky. Glowing bronze sacrificial braziers, olive groves, and coastal hills frame the polished marble courtyard.
  • Lore & Affinities: Sacred sanctuary of the huntress goddess. Suzume Kagerou and Shion Kurogane cross blades under the cool lunar light.

18. Statue of Zeus at Olympia (statue_zeus) — Estátua de Zeus em Olímpia

  • Atmosphere: Sanctuary interior housing the colossal chryselephantine seated Zeus on an ornate cedarwood throne. Ivory skin, golden robes, winged Nike, and burning bronze cauldrons casting dramatic shadows across mosaic marble.
  • Lore & Affinities: The seat of Olympian authority and thunderous power. Kaito Arashi and Valdric Morn test storm energy against imperial authority.

19. Mausoleum at Halicarnassus (mausoleum_halicarnassus) — Mausoléu de Halicarnasso

  • Atmosphere: Monumental marble tomb with sculpted Amazonomachy friezes, 36 slender Ionic columns, a stepped pyramid roof, and a crowning marble four-horse chariot overlooking the turquoise Aegean harbor.
  • Lore & Affinities: Splendor of Anatolian and Hellenic artistry. Kaname Fuyutsuki and Akio Hoshi duel beneath the guardian marble lions.

20. Colossus of Rhodes (colossus_rhodes) — Colosso de Rodes

  • Atmosphere: Titanic bronze statue of Helios crowned with a spiked solar halo standing tall over the stormy twilight harbor entrance. A blazing beacon brazier pierces violet tempest clouds while turquoise waves crash against the pier.
  • Lore & Affinities: Guardian of the Mediterranean sea routes. VX-9 Volta and Marlow Reyes clash on the rain-swept harbor pier beneath the beacon flames.

21. Lighthouse of Alexandria (lighthouse_alexandria) — Farol de Alexandria — Pharos

  • Atmosphere: The monumental three-tiered Pharos tower projecting a brilliant golden light beam over churning Mediterranean waves at midnight. White limestone battlements and royal Ptolemaic banners frame the ramparts.
  • Lore & Affinities: Guiding light across dangerous seas and cosmic crossroads. Kaito Arashi, Shion Kurogane, and Jin Kazaguruma meet at the midnight ramparts as the beacon sweeps the horizon.

Visual Effects

Presentation-only effects live in src/vfx.rs and src/vfx/; the simulation never reads them.

  • Impact tiers (src/vfx/impact.rs): light (<40 damage), medium (<90), heavy (heavy hitdef or >=90) and hyper (>=150). Each tier sets spark count and speed, glow, shockwave radius, flare, camera punch, shake, flash and chromatic kick. Works for any character because it reads the engine Hit event.
  • Ground cracks (src/vfx/crack.rs): heavy and hyper hits on a grounded defender leave glowing cracks that fade out (high quality only).
  • Quality (src/vfx/quality.rs): follows the fx option (0 low, 1 medium, 2 high). Counts scale by 0.35 / 0.7 / 1.0; medium drops cracks and stage lights, low also drops debris and half of the flare. Touch devices already start at medium.
  • Particles stay in the shared MAX_PARTS pool; no allocation happens per hit beyond the pool.
  • UME_SHOTS_ONLY=fx renders hit, heavy, hyper, counter, guard and super stills.
  • Super and awakening (src/vfx/awaken.rs): layered rings (chest and ground), energy pillar of embers, 360 degree spark burst, ground cracks on high quality.
  • Dash (src/vfx/dash.rs): speed streaks and a ground ring when a fighter starts a ground dash.
  • KO finish (src/vfx/ko.rs): three staggered shockwaves, white core, 360 degree sparks, radial slashes, debris and ground cracks on the loser. Simulation-side cost: cargo test --release --bin ultimate-mugen cost -- --ignored --nocapture.

Cinematic post-processing (assets/postfx.toml)

src/postfx/look.rs reads postfx.toml (next to the executable, or localStorage on the web) and falls back to the embedded assets/postfx.toml. Missing keys keep neutral values and out-of-range values are clamped.

SectionKeysEffect
bloomintensity, threshold, knee, tintGlow strength, where it starts, soft-knee width (Bevy/Unreal style, no hard cut) and a warm halation tint
gradetonemap, exposure, split, shadows, highlightsACES filmic curve (0 off, 1 full), exposure, and a split tone that tints shadows and highlights
distortionshockwave, heatScreen refraction from impact rings and heat haze around supers
lenschroma, vignette, grain, sharpenMultipliers for the existing lens effects and contrast-adaptive sharpening (4 extra taps)
qualitygrade_from_level, shockwave_from_level, heat_from_level, bloom_from_levelLowest fx level (0 to 2) where each effect runs
  • Shockwaves: rings with a radius of 24 or more push up to 4 refraction bands (ume_shell::waves::shockwave) into the composite pass; no extra render pass.
  • All of it lives in the single composite shader, so the cost is one extra texture-free math block per pixel; fx level 0 skips post-processing entirely.
  • Tests: cargo test -p ume-render --test headless and cargo test --bin ultimate-mugen postfx.

How it compares

TechniqueWhere it comes fromHere
Soft-knee bloom thresholdBevy, Unrealbloom.knee
Warm halation tintFilm look, Godot glow colourbloom.tint
Contrast-adaptive sharpeningFidelityFX CAS, Bevy ContrastAdaptiveSharpeninglens.sharpen
ACES filmic tonemapGodot, Bevy tonemappinggrade.tonemap

Not done yet: HDR scene target (Godot/Bevy glow on float textures; the scene is 8-bit here), multi-mip bloom and anamorphic streaks, and normal-mapped 2D lights.

Antialiased shapes

Vector shapes drawn through ume_shell::quad carry a one-pixel alpha fringe built in the vertex data (crates/render/src/canvas/shape.rs), so slanted UI bars, circles, rings and diagonal lines have smooth edges on every backend without MSAA.

  • draw_convex (used by Ui::quad), draw_circle, draw_ellipse, draw_poly, draw_circle_lines and draw_line are feathered. draw_triangle, draw_mesh and rectangles stay hard, because they are used as pieces of larger meshes and a fringe would leave seams.
  • Axis-aligned edges are never feathered: they already land on the pixel grid, and stacked strips keep touching.
  • Corners are mitered with a 3x limit, and shapes with an inradius under 1 px fall back to the plain fan.
  • Lines and rings thinner than 1 px keep their width and fade their alpha instead, so hairlines stop flickering.
  • glow (src/glow.rs) is one radial gradient mesh (241 vertices, one layer of overdraw) whose falloff integrates the 14 stacked discs it replaced (910 vertices, 14 layers), so the look is the same without banding.

Cost, measured with UME_TOUR=perf (Kaito vs Shion, 1280x720): fight frames went from 2999 to 3921 vertices on average and batch build from 0.20 to 0.23 ms; draw calls did not change (12.5).

CPU tactics

crates/engine/src/ai.rs picks moves by distance and dice; crates/engine/src/ai/tactics.rs adds reactions for CPU level 3 and above. Works for native (UMF) and M.U.G.E.N fighters alike, because it only reads commands, the move list and fighter state.

TacticTriggerAction
Anti-airRival airborne, descending (vel.y > 0) and within ~105 unitsPicks a usable command whose motion starts F, D, DF (dragon punch)
Whiff punishRival attacking, no contact yet, state time over 6 ticks, just out of reach (0.8 to 2.0 times the near range)Picks a multi-step (ranged) command
Hit confirmOwn attack connected (move_hit > 0) and control not back yetPicks a multi-step command; the compiler's cancel rules let it connect
Meter disciplineEvery random or reactive pickNeeds power >= cost; EX moves keep one bar in reserve; supers only while the rival is in hit-stun, below 40 % life, or the fighter is below 50 % life

Each reaction fires with probability 0.35 + 0.6 * skill and sets a short cooldown.

Evidence

cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example native_duel (21 fighters, 1260 rounds, level 6, 3 seeds): see docs/evidence/ai-tactics/.

BeforeAfter
Knockout rate83.4 %96.7 %
Average round70.9 s54.5 s
Damage per round13881527
Win-rate spread24.7 pts23.2 pts
Rounds with stuck fighter00

Tests: cargo test --release -p ume-engine --test it ai_tactics:: and the unit tests in ai/tactics.rs.

Reading the rival (ai/reading.rs)

SkillBehaviour
Reaction delayThe CPU only sees an attack after (8 - level) * 2 ticks, so low levels block late and level 8 reads at once
Guard heightBlocks low or high from the attack's guardflag instead of guessing
Block punishRival move was guarded and he is still recovering: answers with a single-input normal (more often at higher levels)
Rival profileMoving averages of how often the rival jumps and guards: jumpy rivals raise the anti-air chance, turtles raise the attack chance

Evidence in docs/evidence/ai-reading/: cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example ai_ladder plays mirror matches between levels (level 8 beats level 3 in 66.7 % to 86.5 % of rounds, level 6 beats 3 in 54.8 % to 81.0 %), and native_duel shows 96.7 % to 99.4 % knockouts with the average round going from 54.5 s to 45.6 s.

Contributing to Ultimate MUGEN

English · Português (BR)

Thanks for helping. This page gets you from a fresh clone to a merged pull request. The full documentation is the wiki at https://juninmd.github.io/ultimate-mugen/wiki/.

Where to start

  • Pick an issue labelled good first issue, or open one describing what you want to change before writing large code.
  • Read the architecture overview and the file layout rules once; they explain where code belongs.
  • Characters, stages and data changes need no Rust: see Make a character and Make a stage.

Build and run

git clone https://github.com/juninmd/ultimate-mugen
cd ultimate-mugen
cargo run --release

On Linux install libudev-dev libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev pkg-config first. The browser build is ./scripts/build-web.sh, served from web/dist.

Checks to run before a pull request

CheckCommand
Rust testscargo test --workspace --release
File size ceiling (250 lines)node scripts/file-size.mjs
Crate boundariesnode scripts/crate-boundaries.mjs
Script testsnode --test scripts/*.test.mjs
Wiki book./scripts/build-wiki.sh (needs mdbook)
Browser smoke./scripts/build-web.sh then node scripts/web-smoke.js web/dist (Playwright)

Do not run cargo fmt --all: the tree is not rustfmt-clean and it rewrites unrelated files. Format only files you created with rustfmt --edition 2021 <file>.

Rules

  • No comments in code; names must explain intent. Explanations go to the wiki.
  • English is the default language for code, commits, issues and docs. Portuguese lives in *.pt-BR.md files and docs/wiki/pt-BR/; keep both in sync.
  • A source file stays under 250 lines. Files already over the ceiling may not grow; see File layout.
  • crates/engine is deterministic: no clocks, threads, randomness or allocation inside Match::tick.
  • Respect the crate boundaries in Architecture; scripts/crate-boundaries.mjs enforces them in CI.
  • Update docs/wiki/ whenever a format, controller, trigger, flag or folder layout changes.
  • Significant design changes get an ADR in docs/wiki/adr/.

Pull requests

  • Title must be type(scope)?: description with type in feat|fix|perf|refactor|docs|test|build|ci|chore|style|revert; commit-lint rejects anything else.
  • Keep a PR to one concern. Put new logic in a new file and wire it with one line in shared files, so parallel PRs do not collide.
  • Include screenshots or GIFs (before and after) for anything visible, and a browser smoke result for gameplay, rendering, loading or input changes.
  • Releases are automatic from master commit types; feat is minor, fix and perf are patch.

Acknowledgments

Ultimate MUGEN is inspired by Elecbyte's M.U.G.E.N and Ikemen GO. Please keep that credit respectful in docs and discussions.

Architecture

English · Português (BR)

How the codebase is split, which direction dependencies may point, and where to extend it. Decisions behind these rules live in the ADRs.

Crate map

CrateResponsibilityMay depend on
ume-formatsINI, SFF, AIR, SND, ACT, PCX, PNG, FNT, stages, VFS (folders and zips)nothing in the workspace; builds for wasm32
ume-engineFighter VM, expressions, triggers, controllers, HitDef, match rules, UMF compilerume-formats
ume-netplayggrs rollback, state checksum, replay formatume-engine
ume-renderSprite and post-processing pipelines on wgpuwgpu only
ume-shellAdapter, surface, window, input, quad draw API, audio out, frame pacingume-render
ume-marketGitHub marketplace: listing, bundles, safety limitsume-formats
ume-charforge, ume-devtoolsAuthoring and audit toolingformats, engine
ultimate-mugen (src/)Screens, HUD, stages, VFX, audio mixing, settings, registryeverything above, GPU only through ume_shell::quad

scripts/crate-boundaries.mjs fails CI when a runtime dependency breaks this table (for example ume-render depending on winit, or ume-engine depending on wgpu).

Runtime flow

  1. ume-formats parses character and stage files, or the native UMF JSON, into plain data.
  2. ume-engine compiles CNS, ZSS and UMF into one bytecode and runs Match::tick at a fixed 60 Hz. It never reads a clock, a thread or the GPU.
  3. ume-netplay clones and checksums Match for rollback and replays.
  4. src/ reads Match state each frame and draws it through ume_shell::quad, which batches into ume-render.

Determinism is the reason the simulation is single-threaded and allocation-free per tick. Loading and decoding may use threads through ume_formats::par::map.

Where code goes

You want to addPut it in
A state controller or triggercrates/engine (new file, one wiring line in controllers.rs or triggers.rs) and document it in CNS-Scripts.md
A file format or parsercrates/formats
A fighter, stage or routeData only: UMF JSON, .def, TOML; no Rust
A screen or HUD elementsrc/app/<screen>.rs or the matching feature folder in src/
A GPU effectcrates/render, exposed through ume_shell::quad
A marketplace rulecrates/market

Extension points that need no code in the engine

  • Native fighters: assets/chars/*.json (UMF character).
  • Stages: M.U.G.E.N .def or native stage data (Stages), story objects in TOML (Stage objects).
  • Arcade routes and unlocks: TOML (Route files).
  • Passives: data in a fighter (Passives).

Keeping it maintainable

  • One responsibility per file, 250-line ceiling, grandfathered files may not grow (File layout).
  • A refactor that moves code is its own pull request and changes no behavior.
  • Add an ADR when a decision changes a boundary, a dependency or a data format.

Rules for a new kind of content

  1. Define it as a data file under assets/, embedded through build.rs when it ships with the game.
  2. Give it a wiki page with an English and a pt-BR version, and add a row to the table above.
  3. Add a test that loads the shipped files, so a broken data file fails CI instead of the game.
  4. Record the choice in an ADR when it introduces a new format.

Customizing the engine

Architecture

PathResponsibility
crates/formatsM.U.G.E.N file readers: INI, SFF, AIR, SND, ACT, PCX, PNG, stages, virtual file system (folders and zips). No platform dependencies
crates/engineState machine: expressions (expr.rs), triggers (triggers.rs), controllers (controllers.rs), HitDef (hitdef.rs), fight (matchs.rs), commands and input, UMF compiler (native/)
src/Application: window, render, HUD, audio, menus, native stages, visual effects, controls and gamepad
web/Page, service worker and the browser JS bridge
assets/charsBundled UMF fighters

Tick flow: inputs → Match::tick → for each fighter, [Statedef -3/-2/-1] and the current state → controllers whose triggers are true → physics → collision and apply_hit → camera. Simulation runs at 60 ticks per second, is deterministic and independent from rendering.

Add a state controller

  1. In crates/engine/src/controllers.rs, inside run, add a branch with the lowercase name:
#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
"victoryquote" => { let v = n(m, "value", -1.0) as i32; m.fighters[i].victory_quote = v; }
}

victory_quote is a new field you add to Fighter.

  1. n(m, "param", default) reads a numeric parameter; n2(m, "param", default, index) reads the Nth value; sc.has("param", 0) tests presence; sc.raw("param") returns the text.
  2. Add the field in fighter.rs if you need new state.
  3. Write a test in crates/engine/tests/combat_logic.rs calling ume_engine::controllers::run.
  4. List the name in CNS-Scripts.md and pt-BR/Scripts-CNS.md. cargo test -p ume-engine --test it wiki_sync:: fails for an implemented controller that is not listed and for a listed one that is not implemented. Return true from the module's run (or fall through to the last branch) so the load diagnostics do not report it as unsupported.

Add a trigger

In crates/engine/src/triggers.rs, add a branch to the name match:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
"winko" => b(m.match_over && m.winner_side == f.side as i32 && m.won_by_ko),
}

f is the evaluated fighter and m the match. won_by_ko would be a new field on Match. b(bool) converts to 0/1. Triggers returning floats must appear in is_float in expr.rs. List the new name in CNS-Scripts.md and pt-BR/Scripts-CNS.md; wiki_sync checks both directions.

Add a file format

Put the decoder in crates/formats/src/<format>.rs, export it in lib.rs and test it with real files in crates/formats/tests/real_files.rs. The crate must keep compiling for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
