How to check a new name

  1. Add it to the matching list in mugen_coverage_matrix.rs.
  2. Run cargo test -p ume-engine --test it mugen_coverage_matrix::.
  3. If it fails, implement the controller or trigger and document it in CNS-Scripts.md.

3D fighters

Status: shipped behind the Cargo feature model3d, on by default. Rollback: remove model3d from default in the root Cargo.toml; the game then draws the 2D donor sprites and hides the 3D category.

Principle

The simulation stays 2D. Hitboxes, physics, state machine and rollback never read the model. A 3D fighter is a UMF fighter (assets/chars3d/<id>.json, usually extends a native kit) whose drawing is replaced by a GLB model, so a 3D fighter fights a 2D one with the same rules. Light mode (lite::scale() < 1) falls back to the 2D sprites.

Pipeline

  1. Model::from_glb parses a .glb (own parser over serde_json, PNG textures through png): nodes, skins, meshes, materials, animations.
  2. StateMap (JSON) maps native anim names (anims) or MUGEN state ranges (states) to a clip, loop flag and speed.
  3. The pose is a pure function of anim_no/anim_elapsed (or stateno/statetime), skinned on the CPU, so it is rollback safe.
  4. Model::project uses an orthographic camera on the fight plane, flat Lambert shading and back-to-front triangles, drawn through ume_shell::quad::draw_mesh batched by texture. No GPU pipeline change.

In the game

  • src/model3d.rs is the facade (draw, draw_fit, is_3d, portrait); src/model3d/specs.rs lists the models.
  • Fight: one line in render.rs. Select, versus and results panels: draw_fit inside draw_char_fit. Tiles and loading use portrait.
  • The select screen has a 3D category.
  • The awakened form swaps to the second model (Ichigo: Hollow Total).
  • src/model3d/aura.rs draws the 3D-only effects: the AfterImage trail as additive tinted copies of the current frame (crimson Shunpo, gold Sonido in Hollow form) and a reiatsu barrier in front of the fighter in guard states (120-155) that flashes on guard hit (150-155).

Asset tools

tools/retarget (Python, stdlib only):

  • retarget.py <clips dir> <source.glb> <out.glb> <rig> bakes the clips listed in clips.json onto a rig from rigs.json.
  • autorig.py <mesh.glb> <clips dir> <out.glb> fits a skeleton and skin weights to an unrigged mesh.
  • keyposes.py <in.glb> <out.glb> <rig> bakes the hand-keyed clips of keyposes.json (Bankai stance, three-hit sword string, Getsuga wind-up, charge and release, Juujishou cross, Shunpo, Cero, guard, pointing win pose). A pose sets hips offset, torso/chest/head yaw-pitch-roll and limb directions as [azimuth, elevation] in character space (0 = toward the rival, +90 = his left); bladeR is solved by blade_solve.py into the wrist rotation that aims Zangetsu, and keys_<rig> overrides a clip for one rig (the Hollow fires Cero from the horns). Feet stay on the floor automatically. Re-run on both GLBs after editing; the script is idempotent.
  • Contact sheet of clips: cargo run --release -p ume-model3d --example clip_sheet -- <model.glb> <out.png> Clip1,Clip2 <frames>.
  • Portrait: cargo run -p ume-model3d --example portrait -- <model.glb> <states.json> <out.png>.
  • Voices: tools/voices/generate.py <id> adds the fighter to voices.bank and keeps the other banks.

3D stage: Airport

airport3d ("3D Airport — Sunset") is a live 3D backdrop behind the same model3d feature, so dropping the feature removes the stage with no other change.

  • assets/model3d/airport.glb (128 KB) is generated by python3 tools/airport/build.py <out.glb> (stdlib only): airliners, terminal with jet bridges, control tower, runway, hills, clouds and sun. No third party art; vertex colors per material, emissiveFactor marks unlit lights and the sun.
  • Clip ambient (40 s loop): one jet lands on the far runway, one taxis across the apron, a baggage tug crosses the stand.
  • Model::project_scene (crates/model3d/src/perspective.rs) is the perspective projector: near-plane clip, flat Lambert, per-vertex distance fog, gradient sky. It feeds the same z-buffer Raster used by the fighters.
  • src/model3d/airport.rs renders 480x270 (320x180 in lite mode) at 30 Hz into one texture that fills the stage rect; the 2D parallax scroll of illustrated stages still applies. Lite "backdrop off" shows a still of the same scene.
  • Measure: cargo run --release -p ume-model3d --example airport -- assets/model3d/airport.glb out.png 480 270 1.

Ichigo moves

Jumps: D, U or U, U super jump (also in the air), two air jumps, three air dashes. Specials: Getsuga Tenshou (~D, DF, F, x), charged Getsuga (~D, DB, B, y, hold y; 45 ticks for the max wave), Shunpo (~D, DB, B, b, Sonido trail in Hollow form), Shunpo Rush, Hollow Cero (~D, DB, B, a, hold a; 40 ticks for the big beam), Getsuga Juujishou, Kuro Getsuga, Hollow Rampage; Hollow Total adds Cero Oscuras. Charges use the holdRelease move field (see UMF character).

Credits

See assets/model3d/ATTRIBUTION.md.

Match Mutators

Mutators change the rules of one match without touching fighter data. The first mutator is gravity.

FieldDefaultRangeEffect
gravity1.00.25 to 4.0Scales the fall of airborne fighters and the drop of grounded fighters that are left in the air

Values outside the range, or not finite, are rejected by Mutators::with_gravity and return None, so a bad value never reaches the simulation.

Scope in this version: the scale applies to the fighter's own movement.yaccel. Hit gravity from HitDef (yaccel on the hit) is not scaled yet.

Both peers of a rollback match must use the same mutators. They are set on the Match before the first tick (m.mutators = ...). The default 1.0 is a no-op, so existing matches are unchanged.

Code: crates/engine/src/mutators.rs, applied in physics_step (crates/engine/src/matchs.rs). Tests: crates/engine/tests/mutators.rs.

Photo Mode

Photo mode freezes a fight and gives you a free camera, color filters and a clean frame to save as a PNG. It works in normal fights, training, survival and replays, so you can pause a replay on the perfect hit and shoot it.

Open and close

  1. Pause the fight (P, Esc, Enter or the pause button). In a replay, pause with Space.
  2. Press C. The pause menu disappears and the camera is yours.
  3. Esc, P or C leaves photo mode and returns to the pause menu.

Photo mode is not available in online matches, where the simulation can never stop.

Controls

KeyAction
W A S D / arrowsPan the camera (slower the closer you are)
+ / -, PageUp / PageDown, mouse wheelZoom between 0.6x and 2.5x
FCycle the filter: Natural, Cinema, Noir, Vivid, Retro
HShow or hide the HUD (hidden by default)
.Advance one frame to find the exact moment
RRecenter the camera
Enter / SpaceTake the photo (desktop only)

The overlay (state line, key help and rule-of-thirds guides) is not part of the saved image.

Where photos go

Desktop builds write photos/ultimate-mugen-<milliseconds>.png next to the executable at the window resolution. The web and mobile builds have the camera and filters but no save, because the browser or the OS screenshot already covers it.

How it works

  • Camera: crates/engine/src/photo_camera.rs is display-only, like the Replay Camera. It temporarily changes the camera position, the view size and the ground offset, draws, and restores every field, so the simulation, replay result and checksums never change. Panning is clamped to the stage bounds, vertical pan to 120 units and zoom to 0.6x to 2.5x.
  • Filters: each filter is a set of values for the post-processing Look (saturation, vignette, grain, grade, chroma, bloom). The look is swapped for the draw and restored right after, and the post-processing level is raised to at least 2 so filters also show with effects set to minimum.
  • HUD: Hud::hidden skips the HUD, cut-in bars and banners.
  • Cost: no extra draw pass. The only addition is the same post-processing the game already runs.

Verification

UME_SHOTS_ONLY=photo xvfb-run -a target/release/ultimate-mugen --shots <dir> --res 1280x720 --mute writes the pause screen, a clean frame, the HUD frame, the four filters and a wide shot. Tests: cargo test -p ume-engine --test it photo_camera:: and the photo unit tests in the root crate.

Replay Camera

The replay camera is a display-only director. It frames the fight during replay playback but never changes the simulation: the camera is saved before drawing and restored right after, so the replay result and checksums stay the same.

Inputs per frame: one Subject per fighter (x and whether a hit is active). Output: the focus x and the zoom for the draw.

  • Focus is the midpoint of the fighters, leaning 35% toward the attacker so hits are framed.
  • Pan eases 12% of the way toward the focus each frame, on top of the simulation camera.
  • Zoom tightens when fighters are close, up to 1.6x the match zoom, and stays at the match zoom when they are far apart.
  • With no valid fighters the previous framing is kept.

Pure and deterministic: no clock, no randomness.

Code: crates/engine/src/replay_camera.rs (framing applied in src/app/fight_screen.rs around the draw). Tests: crates/engine/tests/replay_camera.rs.

Rivalries

Português (BR)

A native fighter can declare rivals in its JSON, keyed by the opponent's fighter id. Each entry can change what the fighter says at the round start and give a small attack bonus in that matchup.

"rivals": {
  "akio": { "intro": "Akio. Your star shines, but the storm asks no permission.", "taunt": "..." },
  "garan": { "attack": 1.06 }
}
KeyMeaning
introFirst-speaker line at the round start, used instead of the generic intro.
tauntAnswer line, used instead of the generic taunt.
attackAttack multiplier against that opponent only, clamped to 0.9 to 1.15.

The bonus multiplies the fighter's attack after passives, so it never exceeds the global cap in Passives. Fighters without rivals behave as before.

Current pairs follow Lore: Kaito and Akio (friendly rivals), Suzume against Oboro, Sylene against Valdric and Kaname, Bruno and Marlow against Valdric, Shion against Garan.

Roster audit

ume-tools roster-audit loads every character and stage of an installed M.U.G.E.N collection, plays real CPU fights between them and writes a machine-readable report of everything that is broken: loading, visuals (missing or invisible sprites), sound (calls with no sample), mechanics (stuck states, fighters below the floor, endless attacks, watchdog rescues), the browser-specific import checks and the memory each fighter needs.

It is the reproducible replacement for "open the game and try a few characters by hand".

Running it

cargo build --release -p ume-devtools
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit                     # mugen/chars + mugen/stages -> docs/evidence/homologation
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --only "goku"        # one family of characters (stages still all run)
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --limit 20 --no-fights   # a quick static pass
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --opponent "vegeta"  # force every fight against one opponent
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --fail-over critical # exit 2 on any critical finding (CI gate)
FlagMeaning
--chars <dir> / --stages <dir>roots to scan (default mugen/chars, mugen/stages)
--out <dir>where report.json, report.md and issues.csv are written
--limit N / --stage-limit Naudit only the first N characters / stages
--fights Nfights per character (each against a different opponent and stage, default 2)
--stage-fights Nopponent rotation step when a stage is the subject
--only, --only-stage, --opponentsubstring filters for characters, stages and the forced opponent
--no-fights, --quietstatic pass only, and no per-item progress on stderr
--fail-over <severity>exit code 2 when a finding at that severity or worse exists

Runs are parallel (one load per character per worker, never the whole collection in memory) and every fight is wrapped in catch_unwind, so one broken pack cannot abort the audit.

What a fight checks

Each fight runs 30 seconds of CPU versus CPU on a real stage with the stage background running:

CodeSeverityMeaning
fight-paniccriticalthe match panicked while ticking (the message is kept in the report)
fight-non-finitecriticalposition, velocity, life or power became NaN/inf
fight-life-range, fight-power-rangemajorlife or power left its own bounds
fight-below-floor-p1/p2majorthe fighter stayed more than 12 px under the floor for more than 20 ticks
fight-stuck-p1/p2major420 ticks without control outside the lying states
fight-endless-attack-p1/p2major240 ticks stuck inside one attack state
fight-no-contactmajorthe pair never landed a hit in 30 seconds
fight-off-camera-p1/p2majorthe fighter sat outside the view for more than 3 ticks
fight-watchdog-rescuemajorthe character's own hit/getup script never returned control
fight-camera-nancriticalthe camera position or zoom became non-finite
fight-engine-warningminora warning the engine raised during the fight (missing anim, missing state)

What the static pass checks

CodeSeverityMeaning
char-load-fail, char-load-paniccriticalthe pack cannot be loaded at all
char-no-anims, char-no-states, char-no-commandscriticalthe .air/.cns/.cmd produced nothing
char-web-quarantinecriticalthe browser import refuses the pack (ume_formats::health), so it never shows up on the web
char-unsupported-controller, char-unknown-triggermajora controller or trigger the engine does not run
char-sprite-missingmajoran animation frame references a sprite the .sff does not have
char-sprite-transparentminorthe frame exists but every pixel is transparent
char-sound-missingmajorPlaySnd asks for a sample the .snd does not have
char-unknown-parameterminora controller parameter the engine never reads
char-wasm-atlas-overflow, char-wasm-atlas-pressuremajor/minorthe sprite pixels cannot fit the 2048 browser atlas (4.2 M pixels), so it has to evict and re-upload
char-load-slowminorloading took more than 2.5 s

Stage codes: stage-load-fail, stage-load-panic, stage-no-layers, stage-no-sprites, stage-layer-sprite-missing, stage-layer-anim-missing, stage-bounds-tight, stage-spawn-overlap, stage-music-outside-vfs, stage-no-shadow.

Reading the report

  • report.md ranks the characters and stages with the worst findings, and lists the slowest loading packs and the slowest simulation ticks.
  • report.json carries the summary, every finding and every fight (hits, damage, distinct states, tick cost).
  • summary.json is the compact form (counts by code plus the first examples), small enough to keep in the repository.
  • issues.csv is the same list flattened for a spreadsheet or a diff between two runs.

A finding is evidence to reproduce, not a verdict: --only <name> --opponent <name> replays the exact pair, and --no-fights isolates the static problems of one pack.

Web validation

The browser is the strictest target: it refuses packs that the desktop loader tolerates, and it has a much smaller texture budget. The atlas findings come from summing the pixels of every sprite in the pack (indexed and RGBA alike) and comparing with the 2048 atlas the wasm build uses (4.2 M pixels). Reproduce an actual import with:

node scripts/web-mugen-smoke.js web/dist mugen/incoming/my-char.zip

It imports the pack through the real file input, deep-links into a fight with the imported fighter and fails on a panic, a frozen clock, a stalled renderer or a heap above the limit. When the pack is already in the roster (the bundled elecbyte.zip), set MUGEN_SMOKE_CHAR to the fighter and the test validates content-key deduplication instead of expecting a new entry.

Signature Meter

Português (BR)

Each native fighter can declare a signature block under passives in its JSON. It is a per-fighter meter that changes how the fighter plays, on top of rage, stacks and enrage time.

"passives": {
  "signature": {
    "name": "Storm",
    "max": 100,
    "gainHit": 6,
    "gainSpecial": 12,
    "gainHurt": 3,
    "decayDelaySeconds": 2.5,
    "decayPerSecond": 14,
    "drainOnSuper": true,
    "riskPerSecond": 0,
    "tiers": [
      { "at": 34, "attack": 1.08, "speed": 1.04 },
      { "at": 100, "attack": 1.32, "speed": 1.12, "defence": 0.9 }
    ]
  }
}
KeyMeaning
maxMeter size, 1 to 200.
gainHit, gainSpecial, gainHurtGain when a move connects, a special or super starts, and when hit.
decayDelaySeconds, decayPerSecondIdle time before the meter drains, and the drain rate.
drainOnSuperSpends the meter when a super ends, so the super benefits from it.
riskPerSecondLife lost per second while the meter is full. Never kills.
tiersUp to four steps. The highest reached applies attack (0.5 to 2), defence (0.5 to 1.5) and speed (0.8 to 1.25).

Attack still goes through the global cap in Passives. The meter resets each round and shows as a strip under the life bar.

Current fighters: Kaito (Storm, builds and speeds him up) and Volta (Overload, strong at full meter but costs life).

More fighters: Suzume (Lotus, builds from specials and speeds her up), Marlow (Tide, gains from being hit as well and adds defence), Jin (Wind Chain, builds fast and decays fast for speed) and Sylene (Ice Layers, mostly gained by taking hits, adds defence).

Smoke test (debug mode)

One in-engine runner checks every main feature on every platform and leaves evidence: a screenshot per step and a report that says which feature broke and why.

Run it

TargetCommandOutput
Desktop (Linux, macOS, Windows)ultimate-mugen --smoke <dir> (Linux headless: xvfb-run -a ultimate-mugen --smoke <dir> --res 1280x720)<dir>/report.json, <dir>/report.md, <dir>/shots/*.png
Webnode scripts/smoke-web.js web/dist <dir>same files
Web mobileSMOKE_MOBILE=1 node scripts/smoke-web.js web/dist <dir> (Pixel 7 viewport, touch)same files

The process exits with 1 when any check fails. UME_SMOKE_ONLY=boot,fight_1v1 (desktop env var, also honoured by the web driver) runs only those features; the web page accepts ?smoke=1&smoke_only=boot. UME_SMOKE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS overrides the average frame budget (500 ms).

What it covers

Feature idChecks
bootfighters and stages registered, nothing quarantined, no import errors, title renders
screensmenu, settings, controls, MUGEN import, market, replays, player card and tuning render
selectfighter select (1P and 2P) and stage select render
fight_1v1fight loads, round intro ends, combat deals damage, KO ends the match, results screen follows
trainingtraining mode loads and the simulation advances
team_5v5ten fighters load and render
storystory intro and the first wave load and render

Every feature also checks the average frame time and every screenshot is checked for a blank or flat frame.

Reading a report

report.md lists one row per feature. A failed feature expands to the failing checks, each linking its screenshot. A panic is written to the report with the feature that was running, so the failing area is known even when the game dies.

Adding a check

Add a function in src/smoke/features/ (new file when the module nears 250 lines), list it in src/smoke/features.rs and use ctx.check(name, ok, detail) or ctx.shot(app, name, warm_frames). Drive the game through App state like the screenshot tours do; keep a feature under a few seconds.

Not covered yet

Netplay, auto update, zip import and the on-screen touch controls are not exercised by the runner.

Nightly sweeps

Full-roster simulations that take 10 to 30 s each (native_roster_lab, native_air_abilities, native_match_invariants, native_input_moves, native_normal_reach, native_no_stuck_states, native_attack_keyframes, pixel_states_test and the air-normals sweep) are marked #[ignore = "nightly: full-roster sweep"]. The PR gate skips them; .github/workflows/nightly.yml runs them every day (cargo test --workspace --release -- --ignored), and locally you can run them the same way.

Fight census

ume-tools fight-census --roster a,b,c --level 8 plays every ordered pair AI against AI and prints KO time, guard rate, stalls and win percentage per fighter. Use it to spot balance outliers before and after a stat change.

Standing Hits (knockdown rule)

Fighters used to fall after about one grounded hit in seven. The rule below lets light and medium hits push the defender back while they stay on their feet; strong hits, supers and long combos still knock down.

Rule

For a hit on a grounded, living defender whose HitDef asks for fall, the engine keeps the defender standing when all of these hold:

  • the hit takes less than the threshold of the defender's maximum life (default 16%);
  • the combo total including this hit is under 3x the threshold (so a long string still ends in a knockdown);
  • the attacker is covered by the scope (default: native fighters only);
  • the attack is not a hyper (H* attr), has no down.bounce, wall.bounce or trip ground.type, no p2stateno, and no forcenofall;
  • the hit is not the killing blow.

When it applies, the defender takes the stand-hit states (5000/5010, then slide 5001/5011), the authored vertical velocity is dropped and the horizontal push grows up to 75% (the closer the hit is to the threshold, the bigger the push). Hits on airborne defenders (juggles) are never touched, so air combos behave exactly as before.

Code: crates/engine/src/matchs/knockdown.rs (Match::standing_push), wired in Match::apply_hit.

Scope and compatibility

ScopeCoversWhy
Native (default)hits from UMF native fighterstheir fall is derived from level: heavy / launch, not authored per move
Everyonealso M.U.G.E.N fightersM.U.G.E.N HitDefs set fall on purpose (sweeps, launchers); opt-in only
Classicnobodyexact M.U.G.E.N behaviour

Scope follows the attacker because the HitDef is the attacker's data; the defender's own states (5000...) work for both kinds.

Setting

Settings > Gameplay > Knockdowns on hit (knockdown in ultimate-mugen.cfg): Classic, Native 8%, Native 16% (default), Native 24%, Everyone 16%. A higher threshold means fewer knockdowns. The value is stored in replays (knockdown_scope, knockdown_threshold; replays saved before it existed replay as Classic) and netplay uses the default preset.

Measuring

ume-tools knockdown-rate --roster akio,bruno,... --frames 5400 --rule native --threshold 16 runs AI vs AI over the roster and prints, per damage bucket, how many hits on a grounded defender ended in a knockdown. Results are in the PR that introduced the rule.

Story Mode Scripting (TOML)

Ultimate MUGEN's Story Mode is driven by a declarative TOML campaign script. You can customize every stage, wave, boss, dialogue beat, recovery rate, and credit count — or disable Story Mode completely.

Loading Order

  1. UME_STORY_SCRIPT=<path> environment variable (if set and readable).
  2. story/campaign.toml in the working directory or next to the game executable.
  3. Built-in default campaign (assets/story/default.toml).

If an external script fails to parse or is invalid, the engine falls back safely to the built-in default campaign.

Disabling Story Mode

You can disable Story Mode in either of two ways:

  • In-game: Settings -> Gameplay -> Story mode (TOML) -> OFF.
  • Via TOML: Create story/campaign.toml with:
[campaign]
id = "disabled"
enabled = false

Schema Reference

[campaign]
id = "my_campaign"
enabled = true
credits = 3
wave_recovery = 0.2
stage_recovery = 0.6
boss_life_factor = 1.5
boss_attack_factor = 1.1

[campaign.title]
en = "CYBER REBELLION"
pt = "REBELIÃO CIBER"
es = "REBELIÓN CIBER"

[[stages]]
arena = "neon"
accent = [0.4, 0.9, 1.0]
lane_far = -22.0
lane_near = 8.0
boss = "volta"
alt_boss = "akio"
waves = [
  ["npc_razor", "npc_spitfire"],
  ["npc_colossus"],
]

[stages.title]
en = "SECTOR ZERO"
pt = "SETOR ZERO"
es = "SECTOR CERO"

[stages.beats]
en = ["The grid is locked.", "Break the firewall."]
pt = ["A rede está trancada.", "Quebre o firewall."]
es = ["La red está bloqueada.", "Rompe el cortafuegos."]
  • title and beats accept either a plain string / string list (used in all languages) or a { en, pt, es } table.
  • alt_boss is used automatically when the player picks the stage's primary boss.

Story Studio (in-game editor)

Settings → Gameplay → Story Studio edits the active campaign without leaving the game: credits, life regained per wave and per stage, boss life and attack, and the four dialogue lines of each stage in the current language. Every change is validated, saved as TOML (story-campaign.toml in the app storage, localStorage on the web) and applied immediately. Restore original script deletes the saved copy.

Lookup order for the campaign: UME_STORY_SCRIPT → Story Studio save → story/campaign.toml.

Epilogue editor

Story Studio → Epilogues… edits the ending of any fighter (or the * fallback): title, the boss line and hero reply on the rooftop, and each narration page, in the current language. Saves go to story-epilogues.toml (one ["fighter"] table per edited epilogue, merged over the bundled epilogues.json); Restore original epilogue removes the override. A ● in the header marks an edited epilogue.

The epilogue editor's Scene row cycles the background (any stage with art) with Left/Right and saves immediately as scene = "..." in the TOML override.

Story Studio also edits each stage's name (per language) and boss (Left/Right cycles through the installed fighters); the epilogue's final boss follows the last stage's boss. The Foes per wave row (Left/Right) sets 1 to 4 enemies in every wave of the stage.

At the final boss introduction, choose Spare or Finish with Left/Right or by tapping the option. The choice selects the corresponding epilogue.

After that choice, tap the sides of the helper picker to browse allies and tap the selected name to call them into the final fight.

Unleashed Potential

Characters without their own transformation (imported M.U.G.E.N. and UME characters) get a generic one that needs no edits to their files. Press the transform button (T, the same as native awakenings) when the fighter is grounded, has control and the round is live.

StepName (pt-BR / en)CostDurationEffect
1stPotencial Liberado / Unleashed Potentialhalf a power bar12 sattack x1.2, damage taken x0.9
2ndModo Fúria / Fury Modefull power bar9 sattack x1.4, damage taken x0.75

Each step is available once per round. A character has at most three transformations in total, its own forms included, so a character with three own forms gets none of these. Fury can only follow Unleashed Potential. Characters with their own forms (forms or the legacy anim 196) keep their own transformation and never get this one.

Visuals: the fighter's aura and tint change (blue for Potential, red for Fury), a short ring and tag play on activation, and the HUD shows a timer strip under the power meter. Native forms also show a form strip on the HUD.

Code: crates/engine/src/potential.rs (state and multipliers), crates/engine/src/matchs/unleash.rs (activation), src/vfx/awaken.rs (effects), src/hud/passive_meter.rs (strips). Test: crates/engine/tests/potential.rs.

Virtual pad (web, phones and tablets)

The web build shows an on-screen gamepad on every touch device: a stick on the left, eight attack buttons (X Y Z SP / A B C SUPER) and a row with BACK, OK, AWAKE and II (pause) on the right. It is drawn with plain HTML and CSS shapes (no sprites) in web/vpad.js, above the canvas, and stays visible on every screen: title, menus, select, VS, fight, pause and story.

How it works

  • Each finger is tracked by its pointerId, so the stick and several buttons can be held at the same time. A finger can slide from one attack button to the next.
  • The browser hit-tests the buttons itself, so canvas size, device pixel ratio and render scale do not affect where a touch lands.
  • The engine reads the pad once per frame through ume_vpad_poll() (fighter bits) and ume_vpad_nav() (menu OK/BACK/START). The stick and A/B also drive menus, like a physical gamepad.
  • A tap shorter than one frame is still delivered for two frames.
  • Fingers are released on pointerup, pointercancel, lostpointercapture, page blur, tab hide and pagehide. A long press (contextmenu) does not release them.
  • The pad turns on when the device reports touch (maxTouchPoints, ontouchstart, pointer: coarse) or on the first touch. Nothing hides it afterwards. ?touch=1 forces it on a desktop.

Debugging on a real phone

Open the game with ?debug=1. A box in the top-left corner shows whether the pad is on, the device pixel ratio, the viewport, the fingers held, the bits sent to the engine and counts of pointerdown, pointerup and pointercancel.

Tests

node scripts/web-vpad-smoke.js web/dist drives the real web build in Chromium with real multi-touch (Input.dispatchTouchEvent). It checks that the pad is visible and unobstructed on every screen, navigates the menu, select and stage screens only by touch, walks, jumps, attacks while holding the stick, holds three fingers at once, releases one finger without losing the stick, pauses and resumes. VPAD_DEVICE picks the Playwright device (default Pixel 7 landscape; CI also runs Pixel 7 portrait and iPhone 13 landscape). VPAD_SHOTS=<dir> saves screenshots.

Architecture decision records

An ADR records one decision that changes a crate boundary, a dependency or a data format, so later contributors know why it was made and when it can be revisited.

How to add one

  1. Copy 0000-template.md to NNNN-short-title.md with the next free number.
  2. Fill the sections; keep it under one page.
  3. Open it in the same pull request as the change, with status Proposed; set Accepted when it merges.
  4. Never edit an accepted ADR to change its decision: add a new ADR that supersedes it and update the old status line.

Index

ADRDecisionStatus
0001Own wgpu renderer and winit shell, no game frameworkAccepted
0002One bytecode for CNS, ZSS and UMF; no LuaAccepted
0003Deterministic single-thread simulation for rollbackAccepted
0004Wiki rendered with mdBook under /wiki/ on GitHub PagesAccepted
0005Crate dependency boundaries enforced in CIAccepted
0006Content is data first, with a documented extension tableAccepted
0007UMF 2: JSON kept, compact frames, canonical layout, quality floorAccepted
0008UMF JSON Schema checked in CI; JSON + PNG kept after measuring alternativesAccepted / Proposed
0009LZ4 sprite container for native and M.U.G.E.N. spritesAccepted
0010Exact M.U.G.E.N. migration: original data in UMF, same load path, parity toolAccepted

ADR NNNN: Title

  • Status: Proposed
  • Date: YYYY-MM-DD

Context

What problem or constraint forces a decision.

Decision

What we do, in one or two sentences.

Consequences

What gets easier, what gets harder, and what would make us revisit it.

ADR 0001: Own wgpu renderer and winit shell, no game framework

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-03

Context

M.U.G.E.N sprites are palette-indexed and need palette swaps, PalFx and large atlases at low cost. The engine must run on Windows, Linux, macOS, the browser (WebGL2), Android and iOS from one codebase.

Decision

Rendering is ume-render on wgpu with the palette in the fragment shader. The window, input and surface live in ume-shell on winit. Game code draws only through ume_shell::quad, never through wgpu directly. macroquad and Bevy are not used.

Consequences

One pipeline serves every target and indexed sprites upload one byte per pixel. We own the batching and atlas budget, so those need benchmarks when changed. The quad name is a leftover from an earlier API shape and may be renamed in a separate refactor.

ADR 0002: One bytecode for CNS, ZSS and UMF; no Lua

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-03

Context

Characters arrive as M.U.G.E.N CNS, Ikemen ZSS or the native UMF JSON. Running three interpreters would triple the semantics to keep deterministic.

Decision

All three formats compile to one bytecode executed by the engine VM. Lua scripts are not executed; the wiki lists what Lua packs do and the data-driven alternatives.

Consequences

Fighters in any format fight each other with the same rules, and the tick stays allocation-free. Packs that depend on Lua logic need their behavior expressed in data. New controllers and triggers are added once in crates/engine.

ADR 0003: Deterministic single-thread simulation for rollback

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-03

Context

Rollback netplay (ggrs) and replays need the same inputs to give the same fight on every machine.

Decision

Match::tick runs single-threaded at a fixed 60 Hz with no clock, no thread and no randomness outside Match::random, and allocates nothing per tick. Match stays Clone with a stable checksum, and new state fields join the checksum.

Consequences

Netplay, replays and tests share one simulation. Performance work targets loading, rendering and data layout instead of parallelizing the tick. cargo test -p ume-engine --release --test it tick_alloc:: guards the allocation rule.

ADR 0004: Wiki rendered with mdBook under /wiki/ on GitHub Pages

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-15

Context

The wiki is Markdown in docs/wiki (English) and docs/wiki/pt-BR, readable only through the repository. Outside contributors need a browsable, searchable site, and the web game already owns the root of the Pages site.

Decision

scripts/wiki-book.mjs stages docs/wiki and the contributing guides into one mdBook source with a generated SUMMARY.md. scripts/build-wiki.sh builds it, and pages.yml publishes it to /wiki/ next to the game. The Markdown files stay the single source; no page is duplicated.

Consequences

Sections are declared in scripts/wiki-book.mjs; a page not listed there still appears under Reference, so nothing is lost. Links that point outside docs/ (for example to scripts/) are plain repository paths and do not resolve on the site. mdBook is a single Rust binary with no Node toolchain.

ADR 0005: Crate dependency boundaries enforced in CI

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-15

Context

The crate table in AGENTS.md described which crate may depend on which, but nothing stopped a drift such as the simulation importing the GPU.

Decision

scripts/crate-boundaries.mjs lists forbidden runtime and build dependencies per crate and runs in the release-scripts CI job. Dev-dependencies are exempt, because tests and examples may combine crates.

Consequences

A boundary change needs an edit to the script and a new ADR, which makes it a visible decision. The check reads Cargo.toml only, so it does not catch an indirect path through another allowed crate.

ADR 0006: Content is data first, with a documented extension table

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-15

Context

Fighters, stages, routes, story objects, looks and props already ship as data files, but the list of them lived only in the heads of contributors. Outside contributors need to know which changes need no Rust and where each file is documented.

Decision

New content kinds are data files under assets/, embedded by build.rs when they ship with the game, and each one gets a row in Extension points with its English and pt-BR documentation and a test that loads the shipped files. Code changes in crates/engine or crates/formats are reserved for behavior or formats the data cannot express.

A single content-pack manifest that lets the marketplace declare several kinds of content in one repository is a possible next step; it needs its own ADR before any loader change, because it touches the registry and the marketplace.

Consequences

Contributors can add a fighter, stage or route without reading the engine. Every new data kind carries a documentation and test cost up front. The manifest idea stays out of the code until a concrete marketplace need justifies it.

ADR 0007: UMF 2 is the definitive native fighter format

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-21

Context

Native fighters were one minified JSON line of about 50 KB each (21 fighters, 1.04 MB). Reviews could not read the diffs, frame lists repeated {"pose": ..., "ticks": ...} hundreds of times, and nothing stated what a fighter must contain. Formats compared: TOML, RON, YAML, KDL, JSON5, M.U.G.E.N CNS, ZSS and binary. None beats JSON here: serde and wasm already read it, every editor and CI tool understands it, and the compiler already turns it into the shared bytecode (ADR 0002).

Decision

Keep JSON and define UMF 2:

  1. "format": "umf/2". umf/1 files still load, so marketplace and imported fighters keep working.
  2. A frame with only a pose name and a tick count is written "pose*ticks". Frames with hit, effect, sprite, hurt or offset stay objects. Both forms can mix in one list.
  3. One canonical layout, produced by node scripts/umf2-migrate.mjs: stable key order, values on one line up to 200 columns, objects and arrays expanded above that. CI fails when a shipped fighter is not canonical.
  4. A quality floor tested in native_quality_bar: every fighter keeps at least 17 normals, 9 specials, 3 supers and 3 projectile moves, no zero-tick frame and no hit without damage.
  5. The migration is lossless: the deserialized fighter of all 21 shipped files is identical before and after, apart from the format field.

Consequences

Fighters stay one file at assets/chars/<id>.json: the roster tests, examples and tools address that path and splitting it would touch about 100 files for little gain. Per-fighter folders, shared move kits beyond kits/core.json and a packed release blob remain open and need their own ADR if they are wanted. The migrator is idempotent, so future edits only need to run it before committing.

ADR 0008: UMF schema in CI, and JSON + PNG storage reviewed

  • Status: Accepted for the schema and for keeping JSON; Proposed for the cooked texture pack (superseded by ADR 0009: LZ4 instead of QOI)
  • Date: 2026-11-22

Context

The UMF 2 format of ADR 0007 was documented only in prose. The loader ignores unknown keys (serde), so a typo such as hitz or lyfe passed every test and did nothing. The question was also open whether JSON + PNG is the best storage for performance and maintenance.

Decision

  1. docs/schema/umf-2.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) describes fighters and umf-kit/1 kits and rejects unknown keys. scripts/umf-schema.mjs validates with a small in-repo validator (no dependency) and scripts/umf-schema.test.mjs runs it on every shipped fighter, kit and example in the release-scripts CI job. Packs outside the repo run node scripts/umf-schema.mjs <file>.
  2. Keep JSON for fighter definitions. Keep PNG as the authoring and interchange texture format.
  3. Proposed, not implemented: a build-time cooked pack that trims transparent borders and stores the frames as QOI, decoded by a small in-repo decoder. See the numbers below.

Measurements

Rust release builds, 21 shipped fighters and the 137 sprites (400x400 RGBA) of kaito. Native = this container; wasm = the same code built for wasm32-wasip1 and run in Node (V8), which is not a browser. Medians of 5 to 15 runs; the container is noisy (about 20% between runs), and every conclusion held in all three full runs. The atlas could not be run under Node WASI (it crashed on the 56 MB image).

Definitions, all 21 fighters:

FormatBytesgzipParse native / wasm (ms)
JSON as shipped1,158,382191,01112.9 / 12.5
JSON minified907,786167,8119.9 / 10.7
MessagePack656,470175,7558.3 / 11.1
CBOR664,551173,17114.9 / 18.9

Typed NativeChar parse, all fighters: JSON 10.7 ms, MessagePack 12.4 ms, CBOR 23.2 ms. bincode and postcard write a fighter but cannot read it back (Value, untagged enums and deserialize_with need a self-describing format).

Textures, 137 sprites:

FormatMBgzip MBDecode native / wasm (ms)
PNG, own decoder7.895.58102 / 134
PNG, png crate7.895.5870 / 122
WebP lossless5.444.9491 / 191
QOI4.843.0028 / 32
LZ4 raw RGBA7.275.1635 / 38
PNG, trimmed4.534.5244 / 89
QOI, trimmed4.632.9821 / 27
One atlas, PNG / QOI5.35 / 5.415.25 / 3.3996 / 56 (native)

Trimming transparent borders keeps 48% of the pixels: decoded RAM per fighter goes from 87.7 MB to 42.1 MB.

Consequences

  • Definitions parse in about 0.6 ms per fighter, so format is not a cost. MessagePack saves 8% after gzip and is not faster typed; it would cost diffs, hand editing and the schema. JSON stays.
  • The real cost is texture decode and memory. Cooked trimmed QOI would cut decode about 80% on both targets, the gzip download by 47% and RAM by 52%. PNG stays the source of truth, so artists keep their tools and the sprite art itself is never rewritten. A single atlas is worse than separate files: one big image decodes slower and blocks lazy loading.
  • The cooked pack needs a change to the sprite pipeline (pack_build.rs, decode_cache.rs) and the wasm build, so it waits for approval and its own pull request with a browser smoke test.
  • Swapping the own PNG decoder for the png crate would gain about 30% native and 9% wasm but adds a dependency; not taken.
  • Limits: one fighter's sprites, Node instead of a browser, no GPU upload time.

ADR 0009: LZ4 sprite container for fighters and M.U.G.E.N. characters

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-22
  • Supersedes: the "cooked texture pack" proposal of ADR 0008 (QOI for every sprite)

Context

Decode time and resident size of sprites dominate loading, most of all on wasm32, which has one thread. M.U.G.E.N. characters are 8-bit indexed (palette applied on the GPU); native fighters are RGBA and the web packs already quantise them to a palette.

Measurements

Release build, 62 real characters (54,381 indexed sprites, 2.33 GB decoded), each sprite compressed and decoded on its own, one thread:

CodecPack MBµs per sprite
Original .sff (RLE8/LZ5)85461
LZ461828
zstd level 3 (C)41248
zstd level 19 (C)34155
deflate 637873
PNG8, png crate / own decoder50292 / 130
QOI RGBA96884
ruzstd (pure Rust)412140

With 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads on 4 cores the order does not change; LZ4 scales 3.6x from 1 to 4 threads. In wasm32 (Node), LZ4 decodes 672 sprites in 66 ms, the fastest codec that builds without a C toolchain. QOI RGBA stores four bytes per pixel and loses the GPU palette. On 2,610 native RGBA sprites, QOI is 42% smaller than LZ4 after gzip and decodes about 10% slower.

Decision

  1. LZ4 (lz4_flex 0.14, safe mode) is the one compression for stored sprite pixels, for M.U.G.E.N. and native fighters alike.
  2. Two containers share it: UML1 per sprite and UMSF per .sff (see the wiki page Sprite Container). Readers detect the magic, so PNG and classic .sff still load.
  3. Web fighter packs now carry UML1 indexed sprites instead of PNG8.
  4. PNG stays the authoring and interchange format; native art is never rewritten.

Consequences

  • Chars cook to about 27% less data and decode in about 62% of the time; loading stays bit-exact (cook-sff verifies every sprite).
  • zstd would save a third more bytes at 1.7x the decode time and needs a C toolchain for wasm32; it is not adopted.
  • QOI would shrink native RGBA sprites further; a later per-sprite codec byte can add it without breaking UML1 readers.
  • New dependency: lz4_flex (MIT, pure Rust, no unsafe in the enabled features).
  • Not in this change: lazy decode on first draw, and cooking desktop loose PNGs or imported zips at install time.

ADR 0010: Exact M.U.G.E.N. migration to UMF

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-22

Context

The Python converter (tools/mugen2umf, PR #964) rewrote M.U.G.E.N. states as native UMF moves. Each port lost behavior the heuristics did not model: Black Widow hyper cinematics, her throw and Widow's Strike jump, Goku SSJ4 palettes 2 to 5, throws and the charge ramp. Every fix was another heuristic.

Decision

  • A migrated fighter carries the original data inside UMF: a mugen block with the CNS, ST, common states and CMD text verbatim, AIR as JSON keyed by action, [Info], and an exact sprite pack (art.type: "mugen": one indexed PNG per SFF sprite, SFF palettes, pal1..12.act, sounds as WAV, meta.json in SFF order).
  • The engine loader is split into read_mugen_sources and assemble_mugen_char(MugenSources); ume_native::exact rebuilds MugenSources from the bundle, so a migrated fighter runs through the same code path as the original.
  • UMF-only data (profile, quotes, rivals, move names, extra routes and scripts) is layered on top; native moves on top of exact fighters follow in a separate change.
  • The converter, parity check and MCP server are one Rust crate (tools/mugen2umf). Parity is a structural CharDef diff plus every Statedef -1 route played from its real input for 150 ticks on both sides, compared tick by tick.

Consequences

  • Black Widow, Goku SSJ4 (two versions), Gogeta SSJ4, Super Majin Vegeta, Goku SSJ GT, Aizen (SFF v2) and Goku UI are identical on every data section and every route.
  • Engine gaps now affect the original and the migrated fighter the same way and are fixed in the engine, not in the converter.
  • Bundles are larger than hand-tuned UMF moves (one PNG per sprite); the LZ4 container of ADR 0009 can pack them later.

Formatos aceitos

FormatoUsoArquivos
UMFLutador nativo, declarativoassets/chars/<id>.json
M.U.G.E.NLutadores e cenários clássicos.def, .sff v1/v2, .air, .cmd, .cns, .snd, .act

Lutadores UMF e M.U.G.E.N rodam na mesma máquina de estados e podem se enfrentar.

Roadmap

O plano de compatibilidade e as decisões de arquitetura estão em docs/ROADMAP.pt-BR.md. Itens marcados como planejado nesta wiki ainda não existem na versão atual.

Status de compatibilidade

O progresso rumo à paridade com o Ikemen GO v1.0.0 é acompanhado na issue #135, com uma issue para cada controlador, trigger ou recurso faltante. As listas de controladores, triggers e redirecionamentos suportados em Scripts CNS são conferidas com a engine por cargo test -p ume-engine --test it wiki_sync::: um nome listado que a engine não trata, um nome implementado que não está listado ou uma diferença entre as páginas em inglês e português quebra o teste. Cada carregamento de personagem também aponta os controladores, triggers e parâmetros usados que a engine ignora (veja "Diagnóstico no carregamento" na mesma página).

Agradecimentos

Obrigado à equipe do Ikemen GO e à Elecbyte, criadora do M.U.G.E.N, pela inspiração.

Ajustes de personagem

Configurações → Jogabilidade → Ajustes de personagens muda parâmetros de cada personagem sem alterar os arquivos originais. Os valores são porcentagens (100% = sem mudança), salvos em char_tuning.toml ao lado do executável (web: armazenamento do navegador).

ParâmetroVale paraMecanismo
VidaMUGEN e UMEdata.life
Dano causadoMUGEN e UMEdata.attack (multiplicador de ataque)
Dano recebidoMUGEN e UMEtuning.defence lido pelo multiplicador de defesa
Andar, correr, pularMUGEN e UMEconstantes velocity.*
GravidadeMUGEN e UMEmovement.yaccel
Barra de poderMUGEN e UMEdata.power
Custo de energiaMUGEN e UMEvalores negativos de PowerAdd multiplicados por tuning.power_cost

Faixas: 25% a 300% (barra de poder e custo de energia: 0% a 300%). Personagem com todos os valores em 100% não é gravado no arquivo. Use "Restaurar padrão" para voltar ao original.

Formato:

["native:kaito"]
life = 150
defence = 75

Código: src/char_tuning/ (modelo, armazenamento, testes), src/registry/tuning.rs (aplicado ao armazenar o personagem), src/app/char_tuning_screen.rs (tela).

Arquitetura

English · Português (BR)

Como o código é dividido, em que direção as dependências podem apontar e onde estender. As decisões por trás das regras ficam nos ADRs.

Mapa de crates

CrateResponsabilidadePode depender de
ume-formatsINI, SFF, AIR, SND, ACT, PCX, PNG, FNT, cenários, VFS (pastas e zips)nada do workspace; compila para wasm32
ume-engineVM do lutador, expressões, triggers, controllers, HitDef, regras de partida, compilador UMFume-formats
ume-netplayRollback com ggrs, checksum de estado, formato de replayume-engine
ume-renderPipelines de sprites e pós-processamento em wgpusomente wgpu
ume-shellAdaptador, superfície, janela, entrada, API quad, saída de áudio, ritmo de quadrosume-render
ume-marketMercado no GitHub: listagem, pacotes, limites de segurançaume-formats
ume-charforge, ume-devtoolsFerramentas de criação e auditoriaformats, engine
ultimate-mugen (src/)Telas, HUD, cenários, VFX, mixagem de áudio, opções, registrotudo acima, GPU só por ume_shell::quad

O scripts/crate-boundaries.mjs falha o CI quando uma dependência de runtime quebra a tabela (por exemplo ume-render dependendo de winit, ou ume-engine dependendo de wgpu).

Fluxo em execução

  1. ume-formats lê arquivos de personagem e cenário, ou o JSON nativo UMF, para dados simples.
  2. ume-engine compila CNS, ZSS e UMF para um único bytecode e executa Match::tick a 60 Hz fixos. Nunca lê relógio, threads ou GPU.
  3. ume-netplay clona e calcula checksum de Match para rollback e replays.
  4. src/ lê o estado de Match a cada quadro e desenha por ume_shell::quad, que agrupa em lotes no ume-render.

O determinismo é o motivo de a simulação ser single-thread e sem alocação por tick. Carga e decodificação podem usar threads via ume_formats::par::map.

Onde o código vai

Você quer adicionarColoque em
Um controller ou triggercrates/engine (arquivo novo, uma linha de ligação em controllers.rs ou triggers.rs) e documente em Scripts-CNS.md
Um formato de arquivo ou parsercrates/formats
Um lutador, cenário ou rotaSó dados: JSON UMF, .def, TOML; sem Rust
Uma tela ou elemento de HUDsrc/app/<tela>.rs ou a pasta da funcionalidade em src/
Um efeito de GPUcrates/render, exposto por ume_shell::quad
Uma regra do mercadocrates/market

Pontos de extensão sem código no engine

  • Lutadores nativos: assets/chars/*.json (Personagem UMF).
  • Cenários: .def do M.U.G.E.N ou dados nativos (Cenários), objetos de história em TOML (Objetos de cenário).
  • Rotas de arcade e desbloqueios: TOML (Arquivos de rota).
  • Passivos: dados no lutador (Passivos).

Manter sustentável

  • Uma responsabilidade por arquivo, limite de 250 linhas, arquivos antigos não crescem (Layout de arquivos).
  • Refatoração que move código é um pull request próprio e não muda comportamento.
  • Crie um ADR quando uma decisão mudar uma fronteira, uma dependência ou um formato de dados.

Arquivos de rota e desbloqueio (TOML)

Substitui em dados os caminhos de arcade em Lua e as condições unlock do Ikemen GO. Veja Scripts Lua para o raciocínio. Não há runtime de script: a rota é um arquivo TOML e as condições usam uma pequena linguagem de expressões verificada ao carregar.

Onde ficam os arquivos

ArquivoUsoOrigem
route_<id do lutador>.tomlRota de arcade daquele lutadorPasta de dados (ao lado do executável, armazenamento do app no Android, armazenamento do navegador na web)
unlocks.tomlRegras de desbloqueio e ocultação de lutadores e cenáriosMesmo lugar; sem ele vale o assets/routes/unlocks.toml embutido

Um arquivo com erro é reportado no console com o número do passo ou da regra e depois ignorado, então o jogo mantém o comportamento embutido.

Rota de arcade

[route]
id = "kfm-arcade"

[[step]]
storyboard = "chars/kfm/intro.def"

[[step]]
repeat = 6
fight = { order = 1, stage = "dojo" }

[[step]]
when = "consecutive_wins == 6"
fight = { p2 = ["SuaveDude"] }
else = { fight = { order = 3, winscreen = true } }

[[step]]
action = "clear"

Cada [[step]] tem exatamente um entre fight, storyboard ou action.

ChaveSignificado
fightorder (1 pega o próximo oponente comum, 2 ou mais pega o chefe), p2 (ids ou nomes, vale o primeiro que existir), stage, winscreen
stageID ou nome do cenário; random escolhe um cenário aleatório. A primeira luta pula a seleção de cenário quando a rota define um cenário. Um cenário desconhecido mantém a escolha automática normal.
storyboardExibe um storyboard .def de um pacote MUGEN importado, incluindo camadas de imagem .sff e animações .air; os arquivos referenciados são resolvidos em relação ao storyboard
actionclear encerra a rota
repeatDe 1 a 99 vezes; when é verificado a cada repetição
whenCondição; o passo só roda se for verdadeira
elseMesmas chaves do corpo de um passo (fight, storyboard, action); roda quando when é falso

Storyboards entre lutas são exibidos antes do próximo combate. Um storyboard antes da primeira luta substitui a abertura padrão do arcade; um storyboard final aparece antes do epílogo ou dos resultados finais. Pressione confirmar ou toque em qualquer lugar para avançar a cena, ou Voltar/Iniciar ou Pular para pular o storyboard atual. Se o storyboard ou o arquivo de sprites necessário não puder ser carregado, a engine informa o caminho e continua a rota.

A rota é planejada quando o arcade começa, supondo que o jogador vence todas as lutas, que é o único caminho possível de uma partida. Perder uma luta encerra a partida como sempre.

Condições

Números, texto entre aspas, true, false, variáveis, == != < <= > >=, &&, ||, ! e parênteses.

VariávelValor
stats.arcade.clearArcades concluídos salvos
consecutive_wins, match_noLutas já planejadas nesta partida
modearcade, story, survival, cpu, versus, training, watch ou team
netplay1 em partida online, senão 0
team_size1 ou 2 (só em rotas)
playerId do lutador escolhido pelo jogador

Variável desconhecida é erro de carregamento e lista as conhecidas.

Desbloqueios

[[unlock]]
target = "char:oboro"
when = "stats.arcade.clear >= 1"

[[hide]]
target = "char:oboro"
when = "mode == \"bossrush\""

O alvo é char:<id> ou stage:<id>. Um alvo com regras unlock fica disponível só enquanto todas forem verdadeiras; um alvo com regras hide fica oculto enquanto qualquer uma for. Alvos sem regra continuam abertos. As regras de lutador valem na seleção; as de cenário são lidas mas ainda não aplicadas.

Fora desta versão

Lógica arbitrária, resultados por round (perfect_rounds), rótulos e goto, e arcos do modo história.

Atualização automática

A versão desktop se atualiza a partir da última Release do GitHub. A tag da release é a fonte da verdade: a CI grava UME_RELEASE_VERSION no binário, publica os artefatos e a build instalada se substitui pelo executável correspondente à sua plataforma.

Artefatos da release

Cada release traz, por plataforma (windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, macos-aarch64):

ArtefatoFunção
ultimate-mugen-v<versão>-<plataforma>.zip / .tar.gzPacote para instalação manual (binário + README)
ultimate-mugen-v<versão>-<plataforma>[.exe]Executável puro baixado pelo atualizador
latest.jsonManifesto de atualização lido pela build em execução
SHA256SUMS.txtHashes legíveis de todos os artefatos

O latest.json mantém o pacote em platforms.<plataforma> e adiciona o binário puro:

{
  "version": "0.4.0",
  "notes": "Notas curtas da release",
  "pub_date": "2026-11-05T12:00:00Z",
  "platforms": {
    "windows-x86_64": {
      "url": "https://github.com/juninmd/ultimate-mugen/releases/download/v0.4.0/ultimate-mugen-v0.4.0-windows-x86_64.zip",
      "sha256": "<sha256 do pacote>",
      "size": 1234567,
      "binary": {
        "url": "https://github.com/juninmd/ultimate-mugen/releases/download/v0.4.0/ultimate-mugen-v0.4.0-windows-x86_64.exe",
        "sha256": "<sha256 do binário>",
        "size": 9876543
      }
    }
  }
}

Só as três plataformas publicadas se atualizam sozinhas. Web, Android, iOS, Linux que não seja x86_64 e macOS Intel seguem apenas com o aviso na tela.

Fluxo

  1. Na inicialização o jogo busca releases/latest/download/latest.json por HTTPS (timeout de 8 s, ignorado em silêncio quando offline).
  2. Uma version mais nova com entrada binary para a plataforma atual mostra um painel no título/menu com a versão instalada e a disponível. Nada é baixado até a pessoa aceitar "Atualizar agora".
  3. Ao aceitar, o download roda em segundo plano (timeout de 180 s) para .update-v<versão>[.exe] ao lado do executável em execução.
  4. O download só é aceito se o sha256 e o tamanho em bytes baterem com o manifesto e se o executável baixado responder --version com ultimate-mugen <versão>.
  5. Verificado o pacote, ele substitui o executável instalado (no Windows o executável em uso é renomeado para .old antes) e o jogo reinicia com --no-update-check, para que um manifesto ruim não cause laço de reinícios.
  6. O .old anterior é apagado na inicialização seguinte.

Falha de download, máquina offline ou pasta de instalação somente leitura mudam apenas a linha de status; a build em execução continua funcionando. "Agora não" esquece a versão até o próximo boot, e o aviso do rodapé continua visível.

Linha de comando e como desligar

FlagEfeito
--check-updateMostra se existe release mais nova e sai
--updateBaixa, verifica e instala a release mais nova, depois sai
--no-auto-update / UME_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1Mantém o aviso no rodapé e nunca mostra a pergunta (então nunca baixa nem instala)
--no-update-check / UME_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1Nenhuma requisição de rede

Builds locais -dev nunca se atualizam.

Conferir uma release

node scripts/release-manifest.mjs --verify latest.json --dir <artefatos> --version <versão> --repo juninmd/ultimate-mugen confere que o pacote e o binário puro existem, que as URLs apontam para a release da tag e que os sha256 batem. O workflow Release roda exatamente essa checagem no rascunho antes de publicar e valida o manifesto público depois.

Cobertura de animações nativas

Esta entrega completa a arte dedicada de poses do elenco nativo: todo quadro de animação que o motor consegue nomear resolve para o próprio arquivo PNG. Os canvases numerados compartilhados (09_hit1, 13_fall2, ...) continuam atendendo os aliases legados, e quadros de efeito puramente procedurais (boltHit, feixes) ficam renderizados pelo motor por design; ambos são resoluções aprovadas, não lacunas.

Incluído nesta etapa

  • As imagens dedicadas portrait.png dos dezesseis lutadores seguem nos cartões do seletor e no HUD.
  • Toda pose textual referenciada por uma animação tem PNG dedicado em assets/chars/sprites/<id>/, incluindo defesa, agachamento, salto, flip, turn, land, vitória, intro, taunt, o conjunto de derrotas df* e as poses de dano baixo que antes reutilizavam idle. Poses inline têm o quadro inline_<hash> renderizado uma única vez.
  • Os PNGs dedicados devem ser gerados em pixel art arcade via generate_image usando uma âncora canônica validada do próprio personagem (a ferramenta depreciada generate_missing_sprites baseada no rig vetorial foi removida). Escreva quadros 400×400 RGBA com eixo (200, 392) e metadado refHeight 320, seguindo a convenção existente.
  • Verificação: cargo run --release -p ume-engine --example native_sprite_audit -- <out.json> --require-complete deve passar para todos os lutadores, e cargo run --release -p ume-devtools --bin ume-tools -- audit-sprites --out <report.json> deve ficar limpo em geometria e bordas alfa. O cargo run --release -p ume-devtools --bin ume-tools -- audit-moves é a auditoria estática do elenco (inputs, cancels, throws, hit boxes).

Ciclo de QA com sprite-gen

A skill sprite-gen segue como ferramenta oficial de QA de qualidade artística nos loops nativos, sem exigir credenciais de geração de imagem:

  • ume-tools motion-descriptor --character assets/chars/<id>.json --sprites assets/chars/sprites/<id> --animation walk --out walk.json
  • sprite-gen inspect-motion --source walk.json --out walk-report.json mede âncoras, quadros duplicados, deriva da caixa e contato com as bordas; contato de pé exige --contacts e --foot-box explícitos.
  • ume-tools preview-motion e ume-tools preview-scene renderizam GIFs e MP4s de revisão com os estágios do sprite-gen. Veja Importação de Sprite Atlas pelo caminho de importação component-row quando se quiser arte gerada por IA.

Limites conhecidos

Inventários e relatórios de auditoria não comprovam que as animações ocorrem naturalmente em partida: gatilhos de estado, fluidez de transição e ajuste das hitboxes precisam ser validados no Treino. Recores são aplicados no carregamento pelo sistema de paletas, então a conferência visual deve cobrir cada paleta de um lutador, não apenas a primeira.

Homologação

O ume-tools roster-audit carrega todos os personagens e cenários de uma coleção M.U.G.E.N instalada, joga lutas reais de CPU contra CPU entre eles e grava um relatório legível por máquina de tudo que está quebrado: carregamento, visual (sprites ausentes ou invisíveis), som (chamadas sem amostra), mecânica (estados travados, lutador abaixo do chão, ataques sem fim, resgates do watchdog), as checagens específicas da importação no navegador e a memória que cada lutador precisa.

É o substituto reproduzível do "abrir o jogo e testar alguns personagens na mão".

Como rodar

cargo build --release -p ume-devtools
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit                     # mugen/chars + mugen/stages -> docs/evidence/homologation
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --only "goku"        # uma família de personagens (os cenários continuam todos)
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --limit 20 --no-fights   # passada estática rápida
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --opponent "vegeta"  # força todas as lutas contra um oponente
target/release/ume-tools roster-audit --fail-over critical # sai com 2 em qualquer achado crítico (gate de CI)
FlagSignificado
--chars <dir> / --stages <dir>raízes varridas (padrão mugen/chars, mugen/stages)
--out <dir>onde report.json, report.md e issues.csv são escritos
--limit N / --stage-limit Naudita só os N primeiros personagens / cenários
--fights Nlutas por personagem (cada uma contra outro oponente e cenário, padrão 2)
--stage-fights Npasso de rotação de oponentes quando o cenário é o alvo
--only, --only-stage, --opponentfiltros por substring para personagens, cenários e oponente forçado
--no-fights, --quietsó a passada estática, e sem progresso por item no stderr
--fail-over <severidade>código de saída 2 quando existe achado naquela severidade ou pior

A execução é paralela (um carregamento por personagem por worker, nunca a coleção inteira na memória) e cada luta roda dentro de catch_unwind, então um pacote quebrado não aborta a auditoria.

O que cada luta verifica

Cada luta roda 30 segundos de CPU contra CPU em um cenário real, com o fundo do cenário ativo, e só julga controle e animação durante o round (roundstate = 2), para não confundir intro ou vitória com travamento:

CódigoSeveridadeSignificado
fight-paniccríticaa partida entrou em pânico durante o tick (a mensagem fica no relatório)
fight-non-finitecríticaposição, velocidade, vida ou poder virou NaN/inf
fight-life-range, fight-power-rangemaiorvida ou poder saiu dos próprios limites
fight-below-floor-p1/p2maioro lutador ficou mais de 12 px abaixo do chão por mais de 20 ticks
fight-stuck-p1/p2maior420 ticks sem controle fora dos estados deitados
fight-endless-attack-p1/p2maior240 ticks preso dentro de um mesmo estado de ataque
fight-no-contactmaioro par não acertou nenhum golpe em 30 segundos
fight-off-camera-p1/p2maioro lutador ficou fora da câmera por mais de 3 ticks
fight-watchdog-rescuemenora rede de segurança do motor interveio (o script não devolve o controle)
fight-camera-nancríticaposição ou zoom da câmera virou não-finito
fight-engine-warningmenoraviso que o motor levantou durante a luta (anim ou estado ausente)

O que a passada estática verifica

CódigoSeveridadeSignificado
char-load-fail, char-load-paniccríticao pacote não carrega de jeito nenhum
char-no-anims, char-no-states, char-no-commandscrítica.air/.cns/.cmd não produziu nada
char-web-quarantinecríticaa importação do navegador recusa o pacote (ume_formats::health), então ele nunca aparece na web
char-unsupported-controller, char-unknown-triggermaiorcontroller ou trigger que o motor não executa
char-sprite-missingmaiorum quadro de animação aponta para um sprite inexistente no .sff
char-sprite-transparentmenoro quadro existe mas todos os pixels são transparentes
char-sound-missingmaiorPlaySnd pede uma amostra que o .snd não tem
char-unknown-parametermenorparâmetro de controller que o motor nunca lê
char-wasm-atlas-overflow, char-wasm-atlas-pressuremaior/menoros pixels de sprite não cabem no atlas 2048 do navegador (4,2 M pixels), então ele precisa expulsar e reenviar
char-load-slowmenorcarregamento acima de 2,5 s

Códigos de cenário: stage-load-fail, stage-load-panic, stage-no-layers, stage-no-sprites, stage-layer-sprite-missing, stage-layer-anim-missing, stage-bounds-inverted, stage-bounds-tight, stage-spawn-overlap, stage-music-outside-vfs, stage-no-shadow.

Lendo o relatório

  • report.md ranqueia os personagens e cenários com os piores achados, e lista os pacotes mais lentos para carregar e os ticks de simulação mais caros.
  • report.json traz o resumo, todos os achados e todas as lutas (golpes, dano, estados distintos, custo por tick).
  • summary.json é a forma compacta (contagem por código e os primeiros exemplos), pequena o bastante para versionar.
  • issues.csv é a mesma lista achatada para planilha ou diff entre duas execuções.

Um achado é evidência para reproduzir, não veredito: --only <nome> --opponent <nome> replica o par exato e --no-fights isola os problemas estáticos de um pacote.

Validação na web

O navegador é o alvo mais crítico: ele recusa pacotes que o carregador do desktop tolera e tem um orçamento de textura muito menor. Os achados de atlas saem da soma dos pixels de todos os sprites do pacote (indexados e RGBA) comparada com o atlas 2048 usado pelo build wasm (4,2 M pixels). Para reproduzir uma importação de verdade:

node scripts/web-mugen-smoke.js web/dist mugen/incoming/meu-char.zip

Ele importa o pacote pelo input de arquivo real, entra direto numa luta com o personagem importado e falha com pânico, relógio congelado, renderizador travado ou heap acima do limite. Com um pacote que já está no elenco (o elecbyte.zip embutido), defina MUGEN_SMOKE_CHAR para o personagem e o teste valida a deduplicação por chave de conteúdo em vez de exigir uma entrada nova.

Biblioteca de habilidades

Blocos reutilizáveis para lutadores UMF. Um lutador convertido ou escrito à mão deve citar uma habilidade e ajustá-la, não reescrever os controladores. Os blocos são campos de dados do motor mais um kit embutido (abilities) com golpes prontos.

Mapa de lacunas: o que o pacote MUGEN faz e onde o UMF cobre

Padrão no pacoteBloco UMFSituação
Helper de bola de fogo, Projectileprojectileexistente
Rajada de ki (vários Projectile, um por quadro)projectile.repeatnovo
Teleporte atrás ou até o rival (PosAdd p2dist, Turn)blink (behind, front, above, back) e o antigo teleportnovo
Flash de carga, explosão de aura, Explod de animaçãovfxnovo
EnvShake fora de um golpequakenovo
Raio com vários golpes (projhits)projectile.hitsexistente
Voo, clone, forma (var)abilities.fly, helpers.clones, abilities.formsexistente
Rush com vários HitDefhits[] e moves[].velexistente
Helper com IA própria, Statedef -2/-3, Lua/ZSSscripts, ou ficar no formato legadonão migra

Campos do golpe

{ "id": "salvo", "kind": "special", "anim": "arcbolt", "cost": 250,
  "blink": { "at": 2, "to": "behind", "gap": 36 },
  "vfx": [{ "at": 1, "anim": "boltHit", "offset": [0, -50], "time": 12, "follow": true, "scale": 1.5 }],
  "quake": [{ "at": 3, "time": 12, "amp": 2 }],
  "projectile": { "at": 3, "anim": "boltFx", "speed": [6, 0], "offset": [44, -78], "damage": 22,
                  "repeat": { "count": 5, "every": 1, "offsetStep": [0, 8], "speedStep": [0.4, 0], "damageStep": 0 } } }
CampoSignificado
blink (objeto ou lista)quadro at, to = behind (vira, padrão), front, above, back; gap distância (padrão 40); y deslocamento vertical
vfx[]Um Explod de uma animação do lutador no quadro at: offset (padrão [0, -50]), time em ticks (padrão: até o fim da animação), follow prende ao lutador, scale, behind desenha sob o lutador
quake[]EnvShake no quadro at: time (8), amp (4)
projectile.repeatAbre um projétil em count (máx. 24): o k-ésimo sai no quadro at + k * every (padrão 2), deslocado por k * offsetStep, k * speedStep e k * damageStep. Uma rajada maior que a animação dispara o resto no último quadro

vfx reutiliza animações que o lutador já tem (quadros PNG). O motor nunca desenha um quadro por código.

Kit embutido abilities

Um kit de biblioteca: "extends": ["abilities"] não adiciona nada sozinho; só entram os golpes que você citar (por id ou com use). Golpes: ki_blast, ki_barrage, beam, instant_transmission, blink_strike, power_surge. Cada um traz números razoáveis; mude só o que difere. projectile e blink se mesclam campo a campo (veja o exemplo em Ability library).

Sempre troque anim (e projectile.anim) pelas animações do próprio lutador. Ferramentas que leem o arquivo do elenco sem parse_char (alguns testes) não entendem extends; os lutadores do elenco escrevem os blocos por extenso, e os kits servem a pacotes e mods.

Conversor

tools/mugen2umf converte Explod em explods e EnvShake em shake (com blink, vfx e quake disponíveis para escrita manual) e compara nomes de command sem diferenciar caixa, como o MUGEN faz (SPECIAL 1 no .cmd, "special 1" no gatilho). Antes da correção, um pacote assim ficava só com os normais: o Goku SS4 passou de 5 para 15 golpes.

Regras práticas

  • Repetir os mesmos controladores em dois golpes indica um bloco faltando: crie um campo ou um golpe de kit.
  • Um bloco novo precisa de teste unitário da expansão e de um teste do motor que o execute (crates/engine/tests/native_ability_blocks.rs).
  • Confira cada at contra a duração da animação; o compilador não estica animação.

Câmera de Replay

A câmera de replay é um diretor só de exibição. Ela enquadra a luta durante a reprodução, mas nunca muda a simulação: a câmera é salva antes do desenho e restaurada logo depois, então o resultado do replay e os checksums continuam iguais.

Entrada por frame: um Subject por lutador (x e se um hit está ativo). Saída: o foco x e o zoom do desenho.

  • O foco é o ponto médio dos lutadores, puxado 35% em direção ao atacante para enquadrar o golpe.
  • O pan avança 12% do caminho até o foco a cada frame, somado à câmera da simulação.
  • O zoom aperta quando os lutadores estão perto, até 1.6x o zoom da partida, e fica no zoom da partida quando estão longe.
  • Sem lutadores válidos, mantém o enquadramento anterior.

Puro e determinístico: sem relógio, sem aleatoriedade.

Código: crates/engine/src/replay_camera.rs (enquadramento aplicado em src/app/fight_screen.rs, em volta do desenho). Testes: crates/engine/tests/replay_camera.rs.

Criar cenários

Há dois caminhos: cenário M.U.G.E.N (arquivo .def + .sff, sem programar) ou cenário nativo (código Rust, com camadas procedurais e efeitos reativos).

Coloque meu_cenario.def e meu_cenario.sff em mugen/stages/.

SeçãoChaves suportadas
[Info]name, displayname
[Camera]startx, boundleft, boundright, boundhigh, boundlow, verticalfollow, tension
[PlayerInfo]p1startx, p2startx
[StageInfo]zoffset, localcoord
[BGdef]spr
[BG ...]type (normal, anim, parallax), spriteno, actionno, layerno (0 atrás, 1 na frente), start, delta, tile, tilespacing, velocity, trans, mask, scalestart, scaledelta, angle, xshear, window, maskwindow, windowdelta, spacing

Parâmetros de transformação da camada (Ikemen / M.U.G.E.N 1.1), aplicados tanto pelo renderizador quanto pela pré-visualização na seleção de cenário:

ChaveSignificado
scalestart = x, yEscala base do sprite, ancorada no eixo dele (padrão 1, 1).
scaledelta = x, yVariação de escala por unidade de movimento da câmera, multiplicada por delta: escala = scalestart + scaledelta * câmera * delta; a camada cresce ou encolhe conforme a câmera se move (padrão 0, 0).
angleRotação em graus em torno do eixo do sprite, anti-horária para valores positivos.
xshearCisalhamento horizontal: cada linha é deslocada por xshear vezes a distância dela ao eixo.
window = x1, y1, x2, y2Retângulo de recorte em unidades do cenário.
maskwindow = x1, y1, x2, y2Segundo retângulo de recorte; com os dois presentes a camada é recortada pela interseção.
windowdelta = x, yQuão rápido a janela de recorte acompanha a câmera (padrão: o delta da camada).
spacing = x, yEspaço entre os ladrilhos; usado quando tilespacing não existe (tilespacing vence se ambos existirem).

Planejado: sombras e reflexos configuráveis.

Música, céu e camada de paralaxe

[Music] toca a faixa do cenário no início da luta e substitui a música padrão. O arquivo é resolvido em relação ao .def e, depois, pela raiz da pasta de conteúdo.

[Music]
bgmusic = sound/meu_tema.ogg
bgmvolume = 80
bgmloopstart = 0
bgmloopend = 0
ChavePadrãoSignificado
bgmusicnenhumArquivo da faixa (.ogg, .mp3, .flac ou .wav)
bgmvolume100Percentual do volume normal da música
bgmloopstart, bgmloopend0Pontos de loop em amostras; 0 e 0 repete o arquivo inteiro

type = parallax é uma camada que se repete sem fim no eixo X e desliza com o velocity, sem precisar de tile = 1, 0. Use para uma faixa de céu, colinas distantes ou nuvens. O delta continua definindo quanto a camada acompanha a câmera.

[BG Cordilheira]
type = parallax
spriteno = 2, 0
layerno = 0
start = 0, 140
delta = 0.8, 1
velocity = 0.1, 0

[Sky] desenha um céu animado atrás dos lutadores, sobre a primeira camada de fundo. Funciona em qualquer cenário, inclusive nos que vêm de um .def. type pode ser:

TipoAparência
auroraFaixas verde-azuladas de luz que derivam para os lados no alto da tela

[Sky]
